artists.b: Aastatel 1972–1977 töötas ta Eesti Telefilmi joonisfilmigrupis kunstnik-kopeerijana. 1977. aastal alustas õpinguid ERKI-s, lõpetas 1983. aastal maalikunstnik-pedagoogina. Näitustel osalemist alustas 1982. Aastatel 1983–1984 töötas Tallinfilmi joonisfilmis kunstnik-maalijana. Aastatel 1984–1989 kunstiliste eriainete õpetajana Tallinna Kergetööstustehnikumis. Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liigea Eher 1989. aastast. Teoseid Eesti Kunstimuuseumi, Tartu Kunstimuuseumi, Venemaa kultuuriministeeriumi, Tretjakovi galerii, Alma-Ata Kunstimuuseumi ja Kasahstani Uzhgorodi kunstimuuseumi kogudesse ning erakogudesse.
artists.ben: From 1972 to 1977 he worked as an artist-copyist in the animated film group of Eesti Telefilm. In 1977 he began studies at ERKI, graduating in 1983 as a painter-pedagogue. He began participating in exhibitions in 1982. From 1983 to 1984 he worked as an artist-painter at Tallinnfilm's animated film studio. From 1984 to 1989 he was a teacher of artistic special subjects at Tallinna Kergetööstustehnikum. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1989. Works are held in the collections of the Art Museum of Estonia, the Tartu Art Museum, the Ministry of Culture of Russia, the Tretyakov Gallery, the Alma-Ata Art Museum and the Uzhgorod Art Museum in Kazakhstan, as well as in private collections.

artists.wdesc: Austrian sculptor, based in London from 1938 (1897–1966)

artists.b: EINMANN, Eduard (1913, Kullamaa – 1982, Tallinn). Einmanni looming on jagatav perioodideks. 1950. aastatel lõi ta natuuritruid tööliste, talupoegade, teadlaste ja kunstiinimeste portreejoonistusi, 1960. aastate töödes on märgatav stiliseeriv joon, 1970. aastatel pöördus kunstnik tagasi realistlikku portree- ja maastikumaali juurde. Kunsti õppis Einmann Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis ja Riigi Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis, kus lõpetas dekoratsioonimaali eriala. II maailmasõja ajal kuulus ta Jaroslavi eesti kunstnike kollektiivi. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/.

Arhitekt, TÜ kasvandik (tehnikateaduskond 1935-1936), Helsingi ülikool arhitektuur 1937-1940, Müncheni Tehnokaülikool arhitektuur 1942-1944, Ontario Kunstikolledž (Torontos) keraamika 1982-1992, Baieri Rahandusministeeriumi ehitusosakonna arhitekt 1945-1948, Rootsi 1948, Kanadasse 1949, Toronto ülikooli arhitektuuri õppejõud, ühtlasi eraarhitekt 1949-1982, Taani Kuningliku Kunstiakadeemia külalisprofessor 1964, professor emeritus 1982.
artists.ben: Architect, graduate of the University of Tartu (Faculty of Technology 1935-1936), University of Helsinki architecture 1937-1940, Munich Technical University architecture 1942-1944, Ontario College of Art (Toronto) ceramics 1982-1992, architect at the Bavarian Ministry of Finance's construction department 1945-1948, Sweden 1948, to Canada 1949, lecturer of architecture at the University of Toronto, also private architect 1949-1982, visiting professor at the Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts 1964, professor emeritus 1982.

artists.b: Sündinud 27.06.1954, Krasnojarski krai, Balahta rajoon, Venemaa. Haridus: 1977 Eesti Riiklik Kunstiinstituut, arhitektuur.

Eesti Raadioamatööride Ühingu liige, esimesi eesti raadioamatööre. 1930. a-te teisel poolel oli Aleksander Rähni töökoda Tallinna üks tuntumaid raadioparandustöökodasid. Veel tegeles A. Rähn raadioaparaatide erikonstruktsioonide, amatööride kontrollimise, supervastuvõtjate häälestamise, ristmähiste kerimisega.
artists.ben: A member of the Estonian Society of Radio Amateurs, one of the first Estonian radio amateurs. In the second half of the 1930s Aleksander Rähn's workshop was one of the best-known radio repair workshops in Tallinn. A. Rähn also worked on special constructions of radio apparatus, testing of amateurs, tuning of super receivers, and winding cross coils.

artists.b: 1891 - 1914 eriart Riias. I MS - sõjaväearst vene armees. 1919 - 1924 Saksamaal. 1924. aastast Tallinas ja Tartus kultuuri, teaduse ja kirjanduse alal tegev. Selle kõrval tegeles maaliga. Personaalnäitused Tartus, Rakveres ja Tallinnas.
artists.ben: 1891–1914 specialised in Riga. World War I – military doctor in the Russian army. 1919–1924 in Germany. From 1924 active in Tallinn and Tartu in the fields of culture, science and literature. Alongside this he also engaged in painting. Solo exhibitions in Tartu, Rakvere and Tallinn.

Eike Eplik (1982) is a sculptor and installation artist. She uses nature motifs for constructing narrative, utilises the gallery space from floor to ceiling, works with sculpting techniques from classic plaster casting to paper and wood assemblage and found objects. The processes in her art are partly subconscious and not always fully explainable. When preparing exhibitions Eplik relies on improvisation – to the extent material allows, of course.

One of Eplik's first exhibitions, “The girl who loved everything” (2012) is inspired by the Hungarian writer Ervin Lázár's fairytale “The seven-headed fairy”. The animals in the fairytale-like

created in the exhibition are cartoonish, many of them freaks, chimeras combined of multiple plants and animals, conglomerates frozen into weird compositions.

The exhibition “Some of the birds flew on their backs” (2015) played around with creating compositions of portrait paintings and still lifes, emphasising the perishable and temporal nature of the subject. This existential theme was further developed with the show “Beauty salon” (2017), where the artist explored the construction of beauty and its fleeting and unnatural core. Unlike her previous exhibitions, “Natural” (2018) foregrounded a mechanical-therapeutic way of making art – the artist exhibited installations-sculptures that imitated organic and natural forms in various stages of abstraction.

artists.b: Albert Eskel (1922–1975) rakendas 1960. aastail äratuntavalt isikupärast modernistlikku vormikõnet nii portreedes, figuraalsetes kompositsioonides kui ka monumentaalloomingus. Suur osa tema praegustest pronksskulptuuridest on viidud väärismaterjali alles pärast autori surma. Portreeloomingut, mis valati pronksi juba autori eluajal, iseloomustab pinnatöötluse varjundirikkus ning hea materjali võimaluste taju. Ta on enamasti lõiganud portreed väga madalalt, kaelaosa välistades, jättes modelleeringu ajuti taotluslikult robustseks. Figuraalsete kompositsioonide hulgas on ajastumärgilisi muusikateemalisi kompositsioone, millest osa lahendatud ka jämedakoelises šamotis. Kogu tema 1960. aastate loomingut iseloomustab jõulise väljenduslikkuse taotlus, vorm on lakooniline ja tähelepanuväärselt monumentaalse üldmõjuga. Monumentidest tuntakse enim Eduard Vilde monumenti Tallinnas (1965), ta on loonud aga ka rea mälestustahvleid ja hauasambaid.
artists.ben: Albert Eskel (1922–1975) applied a recognisably distinctive modernist formal language in the 1960s, both in portraits, figural compositions and monumental work. A large part of his bronze sculptures existing today were only cast in the precious material after the author's death. His portrait work, which was cast in bronze already during the author's lifetime, is characterised by a rich nuance of surface treatment and a good sense of the possibilities of the material. He has mostly cut the portraits very low, excluding the neck area, leaving the modelling occasionally deliberately rough. Among the figural compositions there are music-themed compositions marking the era, some of which are also executed in coarse-textured chamotte. All his work of the 1960s is characterised by a striving for forceful expressiveness, the form is laconic and remarkably monumental in overall effect. Among his monuments, the best known is the monument to Eduard Vilde in Tallinn (1965), but he has also created a series of memorial plaques and gravestones.

artists.b:
Sündis Tallinnas inseneri perekonnas.Ta lõpetas koos tulevase abikaasa Albert Eskeli ning mitme teise oma põlvkonna tuntud kunstnikuga 1948. aastal Tallinna Riikliku Tarbekunstiinstituudi, ent diplomit talle poliitilistel põhjustel ei antud. Tema isa Raiu Mullari oli silmapaistev vabadussõdalane ning vend Rünno Mullari, andekas matemaatik, saadeti okupatsioonivõimude poolt vangilaagrisse.

Aastail 1948–1952 töötas Juta Eskel mitmes Tallinna koolis joonistusõpetajana, 1952–1957 sai ta kunstnikuna tööd kunstitoodete kombinaadis.
artists.ben:
Born in Tallinn into an engineer's family. In 1948 she graduated, together with her future husband Albert Eskel and several other well-known artists of her generation, from the Tallinn State Institute of Applied Art, but was not given a diploma for political reasons. Her father Raiu Mullari was a prominent Estonian War of Independence veteran, and her brother Rünno Mullari, a talented mathematician, was sent to a prison camp by the occupying authorities.

In 1948-1952 Juta Eskel worked as a drawing teacher in several schools in Tallinn, in 1952-1957 she found work as an artist at the Art Products Combine.

artists.b: Eesti näitleja, õppis 1918–24 Tallinna Linna Poeglaste Reaalgümnaasiumis ja 1924–25 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis (Günther Reindorffi graafikaklassis). Õppinud laulu Armanda degli Abbati ja Helmi Eineri juures. Võeti 1925 Estonia õpperühma, töötas 1925–41 (tegi kaasa ka operetis) ja 1947–49 Estonias, 1947 Rakvere Teatris, 1949–65 Draamateatris ning 1966–83 Noorsooteatris; 1941–46 oli väljasaadetuna Solikamskis. Mänginud kuuldemängudes (Tolstoi Elav laip, 1956; Cronini Tsitadell, 1956; Büchneri Dantoni surm, 1963), telelavastustes (Hauseri Valge veri, 1959; Gruszezneski Suur Bobby, 1962; Dürrenmatti Meteoor, 1969; Bunini Öisel merel, 1977) ja rohkem kui 30 filmis (Päikese lapsed, 1932, Theodor Lutsu stuudio; Pöördel, 1957, Põrgupõhja uus Vanapagan, 1964, Indrek, 1975, Kõrboja peremees, 1979, kõik Tallinnfilm; Jäljed lumel, 1955, Vaikne hooaeg, 1968, mõlemad Lenfilm; Nõukogude Liidu suursaadik, 1969, Mosfilm; Kolme katku vahel, 1970, Eesti Telefilm). Oli tuntud ka maalijana ja enne Teist maailmasõda meeleolulauljana. Mälestusteraamat Näitleja on ajastu lühikroonika (1986). Temast on filmid Ants Eskola (1968, Eesti Telefilm) ja Ants Eskola: olla või mitte olla (2008, režissöör Kristjan Paul Virve). Tema vanglakirjad on publitseeritud raamatus Härra Ants. Ants Eskola kirjad Hugo Laurile Solikamski vangilaagrist (2005, koostanud Irja Vaher).
artists.ben: Estonian actor, studied 1918–24 at the Tallinn Municipal Boys' Secondary School and 1924–25 at the State School of Arts and Crafts (in Günther Reindorff’s graphic art class). Studied singing under Armanda degli Abbati and Helmi Einer. Was admitted in 1925 to the Estonia study group, worked 1925–41 (also performed in operetta) and 1947–49 at Estonia, in 1947 at Rakvere Theatre, 1949–65 at the Drama Theatre and 1966–83 at the Youth Theatre; from 1941–46 was deported to Solikamsk. Performed in radio plays (Tolstoy’s The Living Corpse, 1956; Cronin’s The Citadel, 1956; Büchner’s Danton’s Death, 1963), television productions (Hauser’s White Blood, 1959; Gruszecki’s Big Bobby, 1962; Dürrenmatt’s The Meteor, 1969; Bunin’s On the Night Sea, 1977) and in more than 30 films (Children of the Sun, 1932, Theodor Luts’s studio; Pöördel, 1957, The New Devil of Hell's Bottom, 1964, Indrek, 1975, The Master of Kõrboja, 1979, all Tallinnfilm; Traces in the Snow, 1955, The Quiet Season, 1968, both Lenfilm; Ambassador of the Soviet Union, 1969, Mosfilm; Between Three Plagues, 1970, Eesti Telefilm). Was also known as a painter and, before World War II, as a mood singer. Memoir book Näitleja on ajastu lühikroonika (1986). Films have been made about him: Ants Eskola (1968, Eesti Telefilm) and Ants Eskola: olla või mitte olla (2008, director Kristjan Paul Virve). His prison letters have been published in the book Härra Ants. Ants Eskola kirjad Hugo Laurile Solikamski vangilaagrist (2005, compiled by Irja Vaher).

artists.b: Õppis Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis Pallas maali- ja mööblikunsti (1926–1932). Pärast Pallase lõpetamist tegutses vabakunstnikuna Tartus, kus pidas aastatel 1934–1937 legendaarset kultuurirahva kohvikut "Ko-Ko-Ko. Pärast sõda aastatel 1945–1947 töötas ta Tartu 1. keskkoolis joonistusõpetajana ning aastatel 1947–1950 Kunstifondi Tartu büroo esimehena. Hiljem tegi illustratsioone ERM-i väljaannetele ja ajakirjadele ning loonud karikatuure. Oli aastast 1932 Eesti Kujutavate Kunstnikkude Keskühingu liige ning aastast 1945 Eesti NSV Kunstnike Liidu liige.
artists.ben: He studied painting and furniture art at the Pallas Higher Art School (1926–1932). After graduating from Pallas he worked as a freelance artist in Tartu, where between 1934 and 1937 he ran the legendary café for cultural figures, "Ko-Ko-Ko". After the war, between 1945 and 1947, he worked as a drawing teacher at Tartu 1st Secondary School, and from 1947 to 1950 as chairman of the Tartu bureau of the Art Fund. Later he made illustrations for ERM publications and magazines and created caricatures. He was a member of the Central Union of Estonian Visual Artists from 1932 and a member of the Estonian SSR Artists' Union from 1945.

Kadi Estland (1973) is a textile artist by education and her feminist work relies on the method of critical deconstruction. One of the focal points of Estland's work is the relationship between the individual and the system – she tells stories about vulnerable people in the contemporary world. By combining expensive and cheap materials or vernacular with high culture quotes, Estland creates emotional works that highlight the processes of reproduction of the patriarchy.

Since the beginning of the 2000s Kadi Estland’s (official name Kadi Soosalu) feminist work has shaped contemporary Estonian art and during that period she worked both individually and as part of collectives such as Valie Export Society, The Elfriede Jelinek School of English Language and Feminismiehitaja. These collectives focused on articulating women's rights and possibilities in Estonia at the end of the 1990s and in the beginning of the 2000s. Estland is also the founder and manager of the artist-run-space Nancy Nakamura Ideederiiul (Tallinn, 2013–2015), and free clothing store and community centre Suburbia Kopopola (with Minna Hint, Tallinn, 2015).

One of Estland's earliest appearances was together with Ele Praks and Helen Lehismets at the exhibition “Töötud armastajad” (Unemployed Lovers, 1999) at the Tallinn Art Hall Gallery. The exhibited set of embroidered pieces titled “Kuidas elatakse Ameerikas?” (How do they live in America?) evoked autobiographical narratives, where the artist's notes and comments played an important role, alluding to the possibility of other kinds of experiences. Through the personal nature of Estland's embroidery the work also acquired a political meaning and her conscious decision to use craft techniques was guided by an ideological principle.

In 1999 Estland founded the collective Valie Export Society together with Killu Sukmit and Mari Laanemets, borrowing its name from the Australian feminist artist Valie Export. With performances in public spaces the artists recreated Valie Export's artistic interventions, adapting them to the cultural context of the newly independent Estonia. For example, during the intervention “Homomeeter II” (a remake of Valie Export's “Homo Meter II”, 1976) the artists walked the streets of Tallinn, each with a loaf of bread attached to their stomach, offering slices of bread to passers-by. In “From the Portfolio of Doggishness” (2000) the members of the group walked around Tallinn with the art critic Hanno Soans tied to a leash (a reference to Valie Export's work “Aus der Mappe der Hundigkeit”, 1968).

artists.b: Haridus: 2007–2009 Goldsmiths College, MFA Art Practice; 2005–2007 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, interdistsiplinaarsed kunstid MA; 2004 Kent Institute of Art and Design, Suurbritannia, vahetusõpilane vabade kunstide teaduskonnas; 2001–2005 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, maal BA; 2000–2001 Non Grata Academia, performance.
artists.ben:
Merike Estna (1980) is an artist working in the space of expanded painting, with many of her works transcending the boundaries of the canvas to encompass different environments, objects, and bodies. Estna’s work intertwines repetitive patterns and mythological motifs. She references history, literature and myths, linking them to contemporary themes and personal stories. In recent years, the artist’s work has been strongly influenced by the culture of Mexico, where she has lived and worked since 2022.

Estna began her creative journey in the early 2000s with photorealistic and pop-inspired paintings and collages. Her early works feature hyper-sexualised female nudes, assertive men, and naive children, depicting a neoliberal consumer society. While studying at Goldsmiths College in London, the artist changed her mode of expression, and in 2012 began to reimagine the meaning of painting. As a result, her works include stage sets, benches, tiled floors, curtains, household items, clothing, and food and drink, inviting the viewer to experience them with their senses: her artworks can be touched, worn, or tasted. Estna first addressed the expanded boundaries of painting in her solo exhibition

at the Kumu Art Museum (2014), where canvases became spatial installations and painting principles were applied to various objects such as books, clothing, etc.

Since 2016, Estna has become increasingly interested in traditional craft techniques. Expanding the medium of painting, she has used ceramics, woven carpets and other textiles, making them carry personal stories and cultural messages (.

artists.b: Maria Evestus (sündinud 1986 Kuressaares) on lõpetanud Tartu Kõrgema kunstikooli (nüüdne Pallas) maali eriala (2014). Alates aastast 2013 on ta aktiivselt osalenud näitustel ja Eesti kunstioksjonitel ning aastast 2019 on ta Tartu Kunstnike Liidu liige. Kunsntik endast: “Olen maalikunstnik, kes kasutab nostalgilisi elemente ja sümboleid väravana vaatja alateadvusesse. Mu teostes valitseb kihiline segatehnika, kus kohtuvad kollaaž, akrüülmaal, efektlakid, grafiit, kangad jne. Oluline osa minu teostest on nende hoolega valitud piiratud koloriit ja rütmilisus, peamine inspiratsiooniallikas on (põhjamaine) loodus ja kõikvõimalikud sisulised ja vormilised kontrastid. Mind huvitab tänapäevase, üha tihedamalt kihistatud ajalooga maailma tõlgendamine läbi erinevate aegade ja sümbolite kokkusegamise, luues unenäolisi illustratiivseid universume. Kunstnikuna kõnetan teadlikult vaatajate kollektiivset alateadvust läbi tuttavate sümbolite, mis on tihti pärit loodusest, kohalikest ja välismaistest muinastjuttudest ja muistenditest, mõnikord segatuna lähikümnendite popkultuurielementidega. Need on lahtise lõpuga ajatud lood, mille sisse vaataja end ise saab asetada ulja seikleja või targa jutuves.
artists.ben: Maria Evestus (born 1986 in Kuressaare) graduated from the Tartu Art College (now Pallas) with a degree in painting (2014). Since 2013 she has actively participated in exhibitions and Estonian art auctions, and since 2019 she has been a member of the Tartu Artists' Union. The artist about herself: "I am a painter who uses nostalgic elements and symbols as a gateway into the viewer's subconscious. My works are dominated by a layered mixed technique, where collage, acrylic painting, effect varnishes, graphite, fabrics etc. meet. An important part of my works is their carefully chosen limited colour scheme and rhythmicity, the main source of inspiration being (Nordic) nature and all kinds of contrasts of content and form. I am interested in interpreting today's world, with its ever more densely layered history, through the mixing of different eras and symbols, creating dreamlike illustrative universes. As an artist I consciously address the viewers' collective subconscious through familiar symbols, often drawn from nature, local and foreign fairy tales and legends, sometimes mixed with pop-culture elements from recent decades. These are open-ended, timeless stories into which the viewer can place themselves as a bold adventurer or a wise storytel.

artists.b: Sündinud 02.07.1974, Budapest, Ungari. Haridus: 2003 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, fotograafia MA; 2001 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, graafika BA.
artists.ben:
Dénes Farkas (1974) is a Hungarian-Estonian photo and installation artist, focusing on the critique of visual representation, the relationship of image and text, and the role of social predetermination in individual experiences.

Even when Farkas' work includes people, the human figure is rarely seen. Only one of his earlier series, “Portraits of women” (2002–2003) depicted real people. With his next series “15 portraits” (2004) the artist stepped away from depicting people only to portray them through their refrigerators instead.

Farkas also has a keen interest in architecture, and so one of his most characteristic motifs is paper models of everyday situations. In his series “Superstructure“ (2009) and “How the fuck are you tonight” (2009), based on post-structural theory, Farkas photographed paper chairs, tables, sofas and other human-made objects and environments, placing them in compositions conveying social structures.

In 2013 Farkas represented Estonia at the 55th Venice Biennale with the exhibition “Evident in Advance”. At the centre of Farkas' installation was a library of 10 000 books; additionally, symbolic spaces for working with books, such as an archive, class room, and home were created. The audience was invited to explore the spaces with books and locate new spheres of meaning. As a labyrinth of language, translation and interpretation, “Evident in Advance” illustrated the quest for knowledge and the inevitable failure of trying to explain everything.

artists.b: Baltisaksa graafik, maalija ning apteeker. Sündis šveitsi päritoluga apteekri ning Limbaži raehärra pojana, ta ema oli kohaliku pastori tütar. 1828 sooritas Gehlhaar Tartu ülikooli juures apteekriabilise ja 1828, eksternina, proviisori eksami. 1834 sai ta oma isa apteegi omanikuks Limbažis. Arvatavasti õppis Tartu ülikooli joonistuskoolis C. A. Senffi juures, kuid oli kunstnikuna valdavalt iseõppija. 1828 andis Tallinnas välja esimese akvatintatehnikas vaategraafika sarja, mille kirjastaja oli Georg Eggers. Sarjas oli kolm T. Gehlhaari enda joonistatud vaadet, kuus lehte reprodutseerisid Johannes Hau guaššmaale ja kolm gravüüri vahendasid Karl Ferdinand von Kügelgeni seepiajoonistusi või maale. 1832/33 ilmus T. Gehlhaari koostatud/teostatud ja G. Eggersi kaubastatud, kuid anonüümselt ilmunud 12 lehest koosnev nn tušimaneeris akvatintasari. 1833–35 tegi Gehlhaar ka üksiklehtedena Tallinna ja selle ümbruse vaateid, samuti 1835 akvatintatehnikas Riia vaadete sarja. U 1840 litografeeris Georg Friedrich Schlater Tartus värviliselt 12-lehelise T. Gehlhaari etnograafilise sarja „Iseloomulikke stseene Eesti- ja Liivimaa talupoegade elust”. U 1850 teostas T. Gehlhaar 10 litograafiast koosneva Tallinna vaadete sarja (kirjastaja F. Kluge) jt üksiklehti (litograaf F. J. Tempeltey). T. Gehlhaari on loonud ka õli- ja guaššmaale.
artists.ben: A Baltic German printmaker, painter and pharmacist. He was born as the son of a pharmacist of Swiss origin who was also a town councillor of Limbaži; his mother was the daughter of a local pastor. In 1828 Gehlhaar passed the examination for pharmacist's assistant at the University of Tartu, and in 1828, as an external candidate, the examination for pharmacist. In 1834 he became the owner of his father's pharmacy in Limbaži. He presumably studied at the drawing school of the University of Tartu under C. A. Senff, but as an artist he was mainly self-taught. In 1828 he published in Tallinn the first series of view prints in aquatint technique, published by Georg Eggers. The series included three views drawn by T. Gehlhaar himself, six sheets reproduced gouache paintings by Johannes Hau, and three engravings rendered sepia drawings or paintings by Karl Ferdinand von Kügelgen. In 1832/33 there appeared, compiled/executed by T. Gehlhaar and marketed by G. Eggers but published anonymously, a series of 12 sheets in the so-called ink-manner aquatint technique. In 1833–35 Gehlhaar also made individual sheets with views of Tallinn and its surroundings, as well as, in 1835, a series of views of Riga in aquatint technique. Around 1840 Georg Friedrich Schlater lithographed in colour in Tartu T. Gehlhaar's 12-sheet ethnographic series "Characteristic Scenes from the Life of the Peasants of Estonia and Livonia". Around 1850 T. Gehlhaar executed a series of 10 lithographs of views of Tallinn (publisher F. Kluge) and other individual sheets (lithographer F. J. Tempeltey). T. Gehlhaar has also created oil and gouache paintings.

artists.wdesc: Italian engraver active in Antwerp and France (1520-1582)

artists.b: 1901 - 1903 esimesed kunstiõpingud Gabriele Edelmanni juures Liibaris, umb. 1904 - Wieni Naiskunstnike Akadeemias, 1904 - 1908 Müncheni naiskunstnike ühingu juures asuvas Naisakadeemias prof. Max Feldbauer ja Franz Marci juures. Samuti tarbekunsti v. Debschitze ja prof. v. Berlepschi juures.
artists.ben: 1901–1903 first art studies under Gabriele Edelmann in Liibar, c. 1904 at the Vienna Women Artists' Academy, 1904–1908 at the Women's Academy attached to the Munich Women Artists' Association under Prof. Max Feldbauer and Franz Marc. Also applied art under v. Debschitz and Prof. v. Berlepsch.

artists.b: Alexei Gordin (1989) on peamiselt tuntud maalijana, kuid ta tegeleb ka foto-, video- ja performance’i-kunstiga. Oma loomingus näitab Gordin musta huumori abil (kunsti)maailma absurdsust ja inimeste võõrandumist, käsitledes ühtlasi ebavõrdsuse ja marginaliseerunud ühiskonnagruppide probleeme. Gordini teoseid iseloomustab mõjutus karikatuurikunstist ning teksti ja visuaali kooseksisteerimine viitega koomiksi- ja meemikultuurile.
artists.ben: Alexei Gordin (1989) is known mainly as a painter, but he also works with photography, video and performance art. In his work Gordin uses black humour to show the absurdity of the (art) world and the alienation of people, while also addressing the problems of inequality and marginalised social groups. Gordin's works are characterised by the influence of caricature art and the coexistence of text and visuals with reference to comic and meme culture.

artists.b: Grigori (Georg) Tõnisson sündis Pärnus gümnaasiumi kojamehe pojana.  1911 trükiti tema maastikuvinjetid ning vested  Postimehe lisas Sädemed, peagi ilmusid ta karikatuurid ajalehtedes Kilk ja Meie Tallinna Ajaleht. 1913 asus elama Tallinna ja tööle ajakirja Leek. 1915 mobiliseeriti tsaariarmeesse, langes 1915 Saksa sõjavangi. 1918 tuli tagasi Tallinna ja asutas koos Hendrik Saarega (Kivilombi Ints) pilkekunsti ajakirja "Sipelgas" (ilmus 15 nr), mille juures Gori oli nii proosa- kui pildiautor (puulõikes). Alates 1920 oli ajalehe Vaba Maa toimetuse liige, 1938 Rahvalehe toimetuse liige. 1941 Gori arreteeriti, pärast vabanemist töötas ta ajalehtede Rahva Hääl ning Sirp ja Vasar juures. Saksa okupatsiooni ajal oli kaks korda vangis, kunstniku surmaaeg on 7.10.1944, selle põhjus (enesetapp?) on jäänud lahendamata. Maetud Tallinna Siselinna kalmistule.

Greenberg oli eesti maalikunstnik, kelle ajastu kunstisuundi järgiv looming läbis pika stiililise arengu. 1920. aastate lõpul valminud maalid on ekspressiivsed, väljenduslikkust lisava  krobelise tekstuuriga.  1930. aastatel oli Greenberg mõjutatud art deco’st, milles värvikäsitlus rõhutab vormide plastilisust. Sama aastakümne keskpaigas helenes Greenbergi koloriit impressionismi mõjutusel ning teda hakkas köitma teatrimaailm – näitlejate omapärane võlu ja naiste poeetilise nukrusega tepitud sarm. II maailmasõja ajal lisandusid tema loomingusse mure, leina ja traagika, mille väljendamiseks kasutas kunstnik klassikalisi lahendusi. Kunstihariduse omandas Greenberg Tallinnas Ants Laikmaa ateljeekoolis, Berliinis kunsttööstuskooli õhtukursustel, Münchenis A. Ažbe kunstikoolis, H. Groeberi ateljees ning Müncheni Kunstiakadeemias. Hiljem töötas õppejõuna Jaan Koorti nimelises Riigi Rakenduskunsti Koolis ja Tallinna Riiklikus Tarbekunsti Instituudis.
artists.ben: Greenberg was an Estonian painter whose work, following the artistic trends of the era, underwent a long stylistic development. The paintings created at the end of the 1920s are expressive, with a rough texture that adds expressiveness. In the 1930s Greenberg was influenced by art deco, in which the treatment of colour emphasises the plasticity of forms. In the middle of the same decade Greenberg's colouring lightened under the influence of impressionism, and he became fascinated by the world of theatre – the peculiar charm of actors and the charm of women quilted with poetic melancholy. During World War II, worry, grief and tragedy were added to his work, which the artist expressed using classical solutions. Greenberg received his art education at Ants Laikmaa's studio school in Tallinn, at the evening courses of the school of applied arts in Berlin, at A. Ažbe's art school in Munich, in H. Groeber's studio, and at the Munich Academy of Art. Later he worked as a lecturer at the Jaan Koort State School of Applied Art and at the Tallinn State Art Institute.

artists.b: Saksa maalikunstnik ja restauraator, viljeles portreed ja ikoonimaali. Kunstihariduse sai isa, Stuttgardi õukonnakunstniku ja Ludwigsburgi maaligalerii hoidja Johann Friedrich Groothi juures. Töötas Dresdenis, Danzigis ja Prahas. Tuli Eestimaa kindralkuberneri W. von Loewendaeli kutsel Tallinna ja siirdus siit edasi Peterburi, kus temast sai õukonnakunstnik valitsejanna Anna Leopoldovna ja pärast 1741. a. keisrinna Jelizaveta Petrovna juures. Osales 1742 koos L. Caravaque'i ja I. Vinjakoviga Moskvas Jelizaveta kroonimispidustuste dekoreerimisel. Oli alates 1743 keiserliku kunstikogu hoidja ja restauraator, tegeles ka selle täiendamisega. Alates 1743. a. töötas Venemaal ka tema vend, animalist Johann Friedrich Grooth (1717-1801).
artists.ben: German painter and restorer, who worked in portraiture and icon painting. He received his art education from his father, Johann Friedrich Groot, court artist in Stuttgart and keeper of the Ludwigsburg picture gallery. He worked in Dresden, Danzig and Prague. At the invitation of the governor-general of Estland, W. von Loewendael, he came to Tallinn and from there moved on to Peterburg, where he became court artist to the regent Anna Leopoldovna and, after 1741, to Empress Jelizaveta Petrovna. In 1742 he took part, together with L. Caravaque and I. Vinjakov, in decorating Moscow for Jelizaveta's coronation festivities. From 1743 he was keeper and restorer of the imperial art collection, and was also involved in expanding it. From 1743 his brother, the animal painter Johann Friedrich Grooth (1717-1801), also worked in Russia.

artists.b: On oletatav 1975 - on oletatav 1990 graafika (kujutav kunst) Akstratehnika - see tehnika leiutati Viljandis. Akstrakunsti viljelemist alustati 1970. a. II poolel A. Grossi juhendamisel nn. "Akstra" stuudios. Akstratehnika oli A. Grossi enda välja mõeldud. Tehnika peamisteks komponentideks oli emailvärv (kunstniku omavalmistatud koostisega, mida ta teistele ei avaldanud) ja lahjendatud bituumen. Heledat emailvärvi ja tumedat bituumenit kasutati siiditrüki põhimõttel, kuid siidiraami asemel oli trafarett. Need osad, mis trafareti alla ei jäänud, tuli kinni katta, pulverisaatori abil emailvärviga üle lasta ja siis emailvärv omakorda bituumeniseguga üle katta. Tulemuseks oli süsimust plaat. Edasi tuli oodata reaktsiooni, mis sarnanes foto ilmutamisega. Need kohad, mis olid kinni kaetud, läksid tumedaks, bituumeni alla jäänud hele emailvärv hakkas omakorda reageerima – bituumenist läbi pressima, aegamisi moodustus reaktsiooni tulemusena soovitud pilt. Selletaolise tehnika tulemuseks oli akvarellilaadne ebamääraste ja teravate piirjoontega veidi saladuslik maal. Seda tehnikat sai teostada kahe värviga. Tegemist oli omal ajal nutika äriideega, mille puhul kunstnik tiražeeris värvipulverisaatoriga taimede lehtedest kompositsioonide jäljendeid põrandapapile, reklaamides neid "tervisepiltidena" (Härm:1999). A. Grossi pildid olid 1980-ndate aastate algul viljandlaste hulgas väga populaarsed. Neid osteti kodudesse ja ühiskondlikesse hoonetesse. Asukoht: Eesti; Vabatekstiline asukoht: administratiivne üksus; Viljandi;.

Kunstnik Albert Gulk sündis 1969. aastal Antslas. Lõpetas 1996. aastal Tartu Ülikooli maaliosakonna. On töötanud Tartu Lastekunstikoolis õpetajana, hetkel vabakutseline. Osaleb näitustel alates 1988. aastast. Samal aastal asutas koos Ilmar Kruusamäe, Peeter Alliku ja Priit Pangsepaga Tartus Kursi koolkonna. Kuulub Eesti Kunstnike Liitu alates 1995. aastast. Albert Gulki töid iseloomustab isikupärane joonistuslaad, kus ta juhindub monumentaalkunsti ja pannooliku esituslaadi reeglitest. Kunstiteadlane Eha Komissarov on öelnud, et Gulki töötamislaadi kindlus ja veenvus tõstsid ta koheselt eesti joonistuse esiridadesse. Albert Gulki algupärast taidurlikkust toonitab fakt, et kunstnik ei kasuta oma joonistustes modelli ega foto abi ja toetub üksnes oma visuaalse mälu kujunditele.
artists.ben: Artist Albert Gulk was born in 1969 in Antsla. In 1996 he graduated from the painting department of the University of Tartu. He has worked as a teacher at the Tartu Children's Art School, currently a freelance artist. He has taken part in exhibitions since 1988. In the same year, together with Ilmar Kruusamäe, Peeter Allik and Priit Pangsepp, he founded the Kursi school in Tartu. He has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1995. Albert Gulk's works are characterised by a distinctive drawing style, in which he follows the rules of monumental art and the panel-like manner of presentation. Art historian Eha Komissarov has said that the certainty and conviction of Gulk's working manner immediately raised him into the front ranks of Estonian drawing. Albert Gulk's original artistry is underlined by the fact that the artist uses neither a model nor the help of a photograph in his drawings, relying solely on the images of his visual memory.

artists.b: Viktor Gurov (s. 1989) on lõpetanud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia graafilise disaini osakonna 2014. aastal bakalaureusekraadiga ja vabade kunstide teaduskonna (fotograafia) 2018. aastal magristrikraadiga (cum laude). Ta on vahetusüliõpilasena õppinud Aalto Ülikoolis Helsingis. Alates 2012. aastast on Gurov töötanud vabakutselise graafilise disainerina. Ta kujundab näituseid ning näituste katalooge. Aeg-ajalt õpetab Viktor Gurov Kunstiakadeemias külalisõppejõuna. 2018. aastal alustas ta tööd Eesti Rahvusraamatukogu näitusteosakonna graafilise disainerina. Gurov on osalenud rühmanäitustel nii Eestis kui ka välismaal, ta on kunstnike rühmituse Neandertali Koobaskooli liige, MTÜ Uus Materjal (kunstiprojekt-ajakiri) kolleegiumis ning grafitirühmituse ja tänavariiete brändi Multistab asutaja.
artists.ben: Viktor Gurov (b. 1989) graduated from the graphic design department of the Estonian Academy of Arts with a bachelor's degree in 2014 and from the Faculty of Fine Arts (photography) with a master's degree (cum laude) in 2018. He studied as an exchange student at Aalto University in Helsinki. Since 2012 Gurov has worked as a freelance graphic designer. He designs exhibitions and exhibition catalogues. Viktor Gurov occasionally teaches as a guest lecturer at the Academy of Arts. In 2018 he began working as a graphic designer in the exhibitions department of the National Library of Estonia. Gurov has participated in group exhibitions both in Estonia and abroad; he is a member of the artists' group Neandertali Koobaskool, on the board of the NGO Uus Materjal (an art project-magazine), and a founder of the graffiti group and streetwear brand Multistab.

artists.b: Põgenes ööl vastu 19.09.1944 koos 12 kaaslasega sakslastelt varastatud päästepaadiga aerutades Rootsi. Pärast seda külastas esmakordselt Kuressaaret mais 1986, seejärel veel 1991. Eestis käis ka 1970 ja 1977.
artists.ben: He fled on the night of 19.09.1944 together with 12 companions to Sweden, rowing a rescue boat stolen from the Germans. Afterwards he first visited Kuressaare in May 1986, then again in 1991. He also visited Estonia in 1970 and 1977.

artists.b: Voldemar HAAS (1898, Tori – 1982, Tallinn) oli eesti teatrikunstnik ja pedagoog, kes on eesti lavakujundust rikastanud paljude tehniliste uuendustega (ringhorisont, projektsiooni- ja pilveaparaadid). Oli 1920. aastatel viljakas maastiku- ja 1970. aastatel linnavaatemaalija. Kunstihariduse omandas Haas Ado Vabbe ja Konrad Mägi juures Pallase kunstikoolis ning Tartu Ülikoolis joonistusõpetaja erialal. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/.
artists.ben: Voldemar HAAS (1898, Tori – 1982, Tallinn) was an Estonian theatre artist and pedagogue who enriched Estonian stage design with many technical innovations (cyclorama horizon, projection and cloud apparatuses). He was a prolific landscape painter in the 1920s and a painter of cityscapes in the 1970s. Haas received his art education under Ado Vabbe and Konrad Mägi at the Pallas Art School and studied drawing pedagogy at the University of Tartu. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/.

artists.b: 1912 astus Tallinna Eesti Kunstiseltsi joonistuskursustele, mis nimetati 1914. aastal Tallinna Kunsttööstuskooliks, õppis ka Nikolai Triigi ateljeekoolis kuni 1917. aastani, mil mobiliseeriti sõjaväkke. 1916 sai temast Eesti Kunstiseltsi liige ning 1917 kunstirühmituse Vikerla liige. Aastatel 1918–1921 töötas ta Paldiski reaalgümnaasiumis joonistusõpetajana. 1920. aastal asus Haavamägi elama Haapsallu, kus töötas Läänemaa ühisgümnaasiumis joonistus- ja kunstiajaloo õpetajana ning seejärel vabakutselise kunstnikuna.
artists.wdesc: Estonian sculptor, painter and graphic artist (1891-1964)
artists.ben: In 1912 he entered the drawing courses of the Estonian Art Society in Tallinn, which in 1914 were renamed the Tallinn School of Applied Art, and also studied at Nikolai Triik's studio school until 1917, when he was mobilised into the army. In 1916 he became a member of the Estonian Art Society, and in 1917 a member of the art group Vikerla. In 1918–1921 he worked as a drawing teacher at the Paldiski Realgymnasium. In 1920 Haavamägi settled in Haapsalu, where he worked as a teacher of drawing and art history at the Läänemaa joint gymnasium, and thereafter as a freelance artist.

artists.b: A. M. Hagen sündis Vijciemsis Liivimaal (tänap. Läti) mõisarentniku pojana. Õppis Cesise kreiskoolis ja Karl August Senffi ateljees Tartus (olles ka abiline), reisis 1820-1823 Saksamaal ja Šveitsis. 1826 oli kubermangugümnaasiumi ja 1826-1832 tütarlaste gümnaasiumi kunstiõpetaja ning 1838-1851 Tartu ülikooli joonistuskooli juhataja. Vene keisri tellimusel tegi sarja Soome saarte vaatemaale (C.D. Friedrichi mõjudega), sai 1837 Peterburi kunstiakadeemia liikme ja vabakunstniku nimetuse. Läks pensionile 1851, aga alates 1855 tegeles fotograafiaga Tartus.
artists.ben: A. M. Hagen was born in Vijciems in Livonia (present-day Latvia) as the son of a manor leaseholder. He studied at the Cēsis district school and in Karl August Senff's studio in Tartu (also working as his assistant), and travelled to Germany and Switzerland in 1820–1823. In 1826 he was an art teacher at the provincial gymnasium and in 1826–1832 at the girls' gymnasium, and in 1838–1851 he headed the drawing school of the University of Tartu. Commissioned by the Russian Emperor, he made a series of views of the Finnish islands (with influences of C. D. Friedrich), and in 1837 received the title of member and free artist of the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. He retired in 1851, but from 1855 engaged in photography in Tartu.

artists.b: The first professionally trained woman artist in Estonia; portraitist, trained in Dresden and Italy.
artists.ben: The first professionally trained woman artist in Estonia; portraitist, trained in Dresden and Italy.

artists.b: Oma õpingujärgsetel ametikohtadel Kultuuriministeeriumi Kunstide Peavalitsuse kujutava kunsti osakonna juhatajana (1952-55), Moskvas NSVL Rahvamajandusnäituse Eesti paviljoni peakunstnikuna (1961-64) ja ka vabakunstnikuna suutis Erika Haggi edukalt kohanduda nõukogude kultuurielu ideoloogiliste nõudmistega ning leida mõjukaid sõpru, kes aitasid realiseerida tema kunstnikuisiksuse ambitsioone. 1955 valmis täisfiguur tollasest primaballeriinist Helmi Puurist. Ka järgnevatel aastakümnetel pühendus Erika Haggi peamiselt eesti kultuuriisiksuste portreteerimisele. Tema loomingust meenuvad põhjamaisest graniidist August Jansen, Heino Eller, Tiit Kuusik ning Georg Otsa juubeliaastal 1977 Estonia fuajees avatud graniitbüst. Samuti on ta portreteerinud nimekaid sportlasi. Portreeloomingu kõrval huvitas skulptorit ka dekoratiivne žanr. Tema dekoratiivloomingust võiks esmalt nimetada Tallinna Kunstihoone esist haljasala kaunistavat tumedat graniittorsot “Meremehe pruut”. Erika Haggi skulptoriimidži juurde kuuluvad ka omaaegsed eesti revolutsionääride portreed (näiteks Olga Lauristin ja Juliane Tellmann), samuti tänaseks Kadriorust teisaldatud nõukogude kangelase Jevgeni Nikonovi madrusekuju. Erika Haggi loomingu paremik on koondunud peamiselt Eesti Kunstimuuseumi, Teatri- ja Muusikamuuseumi ning mitmete kultuuriasutuste kogudesse.
artists.ben: In her post-studies positions as head of the fine arts department of the Ministry of Culture's Central Board of Arts (1952-55), as chief artist of the Estonian pavilion at the USSR National Economic Achievements Exhibition in Moscow (1961-64) and also as a freelance artist, Erika Haggi succeeded in adapting well to the ideological demands of Soviet cultural life and in finding influential friends who helped realise the ambitions of her artistic personality. In 1955 she completed a full figure of the then prima ballerina Helmi Puur. In the following decades too, Erika Haggi devoted herself mainly to portraying Estonian cultural figures. Among her works one recalls the Nordic-granite pieces August Jansen, Heino Eller, Tiit Kuusik, and the granite bust of Georg Ots unveiled in the foyer of Estonia in his jubilee year, 1977. She has also portrayed well-known athletes. Alongside her portrait work, the sculptor was also interested in the decorative genre. Among her decorative works one might first mention the dark granite torso “Meremehe pruut” (“The Sailor's Bride”), which adorns the green area in front of the Tallinn Art Hall. Erika Haggi's sculptural image also includes portraits of Estonian revolutionaries of the time (for example Olga Lauristin and Juliane Tellmann), as well as the figure of the sailor Jevgeni Nikonov, a Soviet hero, which has by now been removed from Kadriorg. The best of Erika Haggi's work is concentrated mainly in the collections of the Art Museum of Estonia, the Theatre and Music Museum, and several cultural institutions.

artists.b: M.Hakk (sünd. 1947) on vabakutseline akvarellist kes töötab Eestis ja Prantsusmaal.Lôpetanud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia (end. ERKI) 1971 a. ruumikujunduse erialal.Töötas Eesti Tööstusprojektis , seejärel Helsingis Into Pyykkö ja Leena Kolineni arhitektibüroodes sisearhitektina. Al. 2008 Eesti Akvarellistide Ühingu (EAÜ) liige Al. 2015 Prantsuse Akvarellistide Ühingu (SFA) liige Vôtab pidevalt osa EAÜ ja SFA näitustest.
artists.ben: M. Hakk (b. 1947) is a freelance watercolourist who works in Estonia and France. Graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts (former ERKI) in 1971 in the speciality of interior design. Worked at Eesti Tööstusprojekt, then in Helsinki as an interior architect at the architectural offices of Into Pyykkö and Leena Kolineni. From 2008 a member of the Estonian Watercolour Society (EAÜ). From 2015 a member of the French Watercolour Society (SFA). Regularly participates in exhibitions of the EAÜ and SFA.

artists.b: 1928 siirdus Halliste Tallinna, kus töötas aasta jagu Jaan Koorti ateljees, õppides seal keraamikat ning pronksivalu. Koorti juurest lahkudes hakkas Halliste elatist teenima mööblidetailide valmistamise ning klaverivabrikule ornamentide graveerimisega. Oli Eesti Muuseumi Ühingu, Eesti Kujutavate Kunstnikkude Keskühingu juhatuse liige, Kujutava Kunsti Sihtkapitali Valitsuse liige ning Tallinna Kunstihoone ehituskomisjoni ning juhatuse liige. 1930. aastatel avanes kunstnikul võimalus täiendada end reisidega Venemaale, Soome, Itaaliasse, Prantsusmaale ja Saksamaale. II maailmasõja ajal elas kunstnik tagasitõmbununa, suviti viibis ta koos abikaasaga Pupastveres. Pärast sõja lõppu töötas skuptor mõnda aega Riikliku Kunstimuuseumi restauraatorina. Sõjajärgsed aastad olid kunstniku loomingus kõige viljakamad, põhiliseks töökohaks oli ateljee Lauristini tänavas Tallinnas.
artists.ben: In 1928 Halliste moved to Tallinn, where he worked for a year in Jaan Koort's studio, studying ceramics and bronze casting there. After leaving Koort he began earning his living by making furniture parts and engraving ornaments for a piano factory. He was a board member of the Estonian Museum Society, of the Central Union of Estonian Fine Artists, a member of the Board of the Fine Arts Foundation, and a member of the building committee and board of the Tallinn Art Hall. In the 1930s the artist had the opportunity to further his training through trips to Russia, Finland, Italy, France and Germany. During World War II the artist lived withdrawn from society; in the summers he stayed with his wife in Pupastvere. After the war ended the sculptor worked for some time as a restorer at the State Art Museum. The post-war years were the most productive in the artist's oeuvre; his main workplace was a studio on Lauristini Street in Tallinn.

artists.b: H. E. Hartmann õppis kunsti Tartus A.M.Hageni juures, Düsseldorfi kunstiakadeemias ja Münchenis. 1841–44 töötas ta Lätis Bērzaines kooliõpetajana, aastast 1845 Tartus joonistusõpetajana ja linnakassa raamatupidajana. 1845 sai Peterburi kunstiakadeemialt vabakunstniku nimetuse, aastast 1860 oli Õpetatud Eesti Seltsi kogude konservaator. Maalis portreid ja maastikke, eriti oluline on ta Estica- teemaline graafika. Hartmanni puulõiked eestlastest ilmusid väljaannetes: Talurahva Postimees, Tartu Postimees, Das Inland (saksa k), Pasaule (läti k) jm.
artists.ben: H. E. Hartmann studied art in Tartu under A. M. Hagen, at the Düsseldorf Academy of Arts and in Munich. In 1841–44 he worked in Latvia as a schoolteacher in Bērzaine, from 1845 in Tartu as a drawing teacher and city treasury accountant. In 1845 he received the title of free artist from the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts, and from 1860 he was conservator of the collections of the Learned Estonian Society. He painted portraits and landscapes, but especially significant is his Estica-themed graphic art. Hartmann's woodcuts of Estonians appeared in the publications: Talurahva Postimees, Tartu Postimees, Das Inland (in German), Pasaule (in Latvian), etc.

artists.b: Õppinud maalriametit, saabus G. F. Schlater 1828 Riiast Tartusse, kus asutas 1832. aastal litograafiatöökoja. Peale olulise tegevuse graafika alal tegutses oli ka maalikunstnik ning Tartu gümnaasiumi ja veterinaarinstituudi joonistusõpetaja. 1857 müüs oma litograafiapressi Louis Höflingerile ja hakkas fotograafiks.
artists.wdesc: Baltic German painter and graphic artist (1807-1888)
artists.ben: Having studied the painter's craft, G. F. Schlater arrived in Tartu from Riga in 1828, where in 1832 he founded a lithography workshop. In addition to his significant activity in the field of graphic art, he was also a painter and a drawing teacher at the Tartu gymnasium and the veterinary institute. In 1857 he sold his lithography press to Louis Höflinger and became a photographer.

artists.b: Woldemar Hau õppis oma isa ja Carl Ferdinand von Kügelgeni juures, lõpetas 1836 Peterburi kunstiakadeemia ja täiendas end pärast seda Saksamaal ning Itaalias. 1842 sai keiserlikuks õukonnakunstnikuks ja 1849 akadeemikuks. Oli Venemaa üks olulisemaid akvarellportreede meistreid.
artists.ben: Woldemar Hau studied with his father and with Carl Ferdinand von Kügelgen, graduated from the Petersburg Academy of Arts in 1836, and afterwards furthered his education in Germany and Italy. In 1842 he became an Imperial Court artist and in 1849 an academician. He was one of Russia's most important masters of watercolour portraits.

artists.b: Inga Heamägi (s. 1961 Viljandis) on lõpetanud Tallinna Kunstiülikooli graafika eriala. Ta on Eesti Vabagraafikute Ühenduse liige ning Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige. Isiknäitustega esinenud Eestis, Lätis, Soomes.
artists.ben: Inga Heamägi (b. 1961 in Viljandi) has graduated from Tallinna Kunstiülikool, majoring in graphic art. She is a member of the Eesti Vabagraafikute Ühendus and a member of the Eesti Kunstnike Liit. She has held solo exhibitions in Estonia, Latvia, Finland.

artists.b: Reet Heinla (sündinud 27. augustil 1952 Tallinnas) on eesti kunstnik, kelle looming keskendub peamiselt õlimaalidele. Ta on lõpetanud Tallinna Reaalkooli ja Tallinna Tehnikaülikooli ökonomisti erialal. Maalimisega alustas Heinla 2005. aastal, täiendas end erinevatel kursustel ning õppis akvarelli, pastelli ja õlimaali tehnikaid. Alates 2009. aastast on ta jäänud truuks õlivärvidele, kuna leiab, et need võimaldavad tal end kõige paremini väljendada. Ta on õppinud õlimaali Tartu Rahvaülikoolis ning alates 2014. aastast osalenud aktiivselt kunstistuudio “Suvi” tegevuses kunstnik Robert Suvi juhendamisel.
artists.ben: Reet Heinla (born 27 August 1952 in Tallinn) is an Estonian artist whose work focuses mainly on oil paintings. She graduated from Tallinna Reaalkool and Tallinn University of Technology with a degree in economics. Heinla began painting in 2005, furthered her education at various courses and studied the techniques of watercolour, pastel and oil painting. Since 2009 she has remained faithful to oil paints, as she finds that they allow her to express herself best. She has studied oil painting at the Tartu Popular University and, since 2014, has actively participated in the activities of the art studio "Suvi" under the guidance of artist Robert Suvi.

artists.b: Täiendas end  aastatel 1929–1930 Reimsis Institut Spécial de Peinture Décorative de Reimsis, mille lõpetas kuldmedaliga ja Pariisis École Nationale des Arts Décoratifsis, Académie Ransonis ja Conservatoire Nationale des Arts e Métiers's.
artists.ben: He/she furthered his/her studies in 1929–1930 in Reims at the Institut Spécial de Peinture Décorative de Reims, which he/she completed with a gold medal, and in Paris at the École Nationale des Arts Décoratifs, the Académie Ranson and the Conservatoire Nationale des Arts et Métiers.

artists.b: Mirjam Hinn (snd 1990) on lõpetanud Tartu Ülikooli maalikunsti õppetooli MA (2018) ja Tartu Kõrgema Kunstikooli (2014). Kunstiõpinguid alustas aastal 2010 Tartu Kunstikoolis. Tal on olnud mitmeid isikunäituseid, neist viimane “Hõljuvad perspektiivid”(2022) Itaalias, Montesarchios, varasemad peamiselt kodulinnas Tartus, näiteks “Tardunud helid” Tartu Kunstimajas (2018), “Kõrgepinge” Tartu Kunstimuuseumis (2019) ja “Tuhandesilmne saar” Tartu Kunstimajas (2021). Aktiivselt ühisäitustel osalemisega alustas 2011. aastal, esmalt Eestis, seejärel ka Soomes, Leedus, Itaalias ning Saksamaal. Dünaamilise ja abstraktse kujundikeelega maalikunstniku loomingus on saanud äratuntavaks värvipalett ning puhtad värvipinnad vastandumas pintslitõmbeis vonklevate pindadega. Kirkad ja kohati ebamaiselt tehislikud toonid, mis lausa helendavad, on saanud teoste kandvaks aktsendiks. Hinn on oma näitustel tihti ühendanud maalikunsti meediumi ka valguse installatsiooni ja helikunstiga, luues kogu näitusesaali ja erinevaid meeli hõlmavaid isikunäituseid. Tema varasema loomingu fookuses on olnud peamiselt heli ja valguse nähtused ja nende isiklik tõlgendus värvi ja kujundi keelde. Näitus “.
artists.ben: Mirjam Hinn (b. 1990) has completed an MA in painting at the University of Tartu (2018) and graduated from the Tartu Art College (2014). She began her art studies in 2010 at the Tartu Art School. She has held several solo exhibitions, the most recent of which, "Hõljuvad perspektiivid" (2022), was in Montesarchio, Italy; earlier ones were mainly in her home town of Tartu, for example "Tardunud helid" at the Tartu Art House (2018), "Kõrgepinge" at the Tartu Art Museum (2019) and "Tuhandesilmne saar" at the Tartu Art House (2021). She began actively participating in joint exhibitions in 2011, first in Estonia, then also in Finland, Lithuania, Italy and Germany. In the work of this painter, characterised by a dynamic and abstract visual language, a recognisable colour palette has emerged, along with clean fields of colour contrasted with surfaces winding with brushstrokes. Bright and at times unearthly artificial tones, which seem to glow, have become the defining accent of the works. Hinn has often, in her exhibitions, combined the medium of painting with light installation and sound art, creating solo exhibitions that encompass the whole exhibition hall and different senses. Her earlier work has focused mainly on the phenomena of sound and light and their personal translation into the language of colour and form. The exhibition "

artists.b: Õppis maalikunsti Viinis ja Roomas. Alates 1820 töötas Peterburis ja alates 1849 Tallinnas portretisti ja joonistusõpetajana. Loonud ka eestlaste portreid ning 8 vihku kivitrükiportreid Vene riigitegelastest, teadlastest ja kunstnikest ("Les contemporains", alates 1822, venekeelne väljaanne 1828) vararealismi e. biidermeierliku realismi vaimus (artiklite kogumik "Neli baltisaksa kunstnikku", Tallinn 1994, näituse kataloog "Vene valitsejad", Tallinn 2006)
artists.ben: Studied painting in Vienna and Rome. From 1820 worked in Petersburg and from 1849 in Tallinn as a portraitist and drawing teacher. Also created portraits of Estonians and 8 volumes of lithographic portraits of Russian statesmen, scholars and artists ("Les contemporains", from 1822, Russian-language edition 1828) in the spirit of early realism, i.e. Biedermeier realism (collection of articles "Four Baltic German Artists", Tallinn 1994, exhibition catalogue "Russian Rulers", Tallinn 2006)

grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design

artists.b: Pärast suurtükiväeakadeemia lõpetamist saadeti kaardiväe 3. suurtükibäebrigaadi koosseisul rindele. Kodusõja ajal võitles valgekaartlaste poolel ja evakueerus koos Wrangeli armeega Türki. 1922 tuli Eestisse, kus töötas algul saeveskis lihttöölisena, hiljem joonestajana põllumajandusministeeriumis ja joonistajana tekstiilivabrikus. Illustreeris raamatuid ja kujundas teatridekoratsioone ning postkaarte. Osales kohalikes vene kirjandusühingutes.
artists.ben: After completing the artillery academy he was sent to the front with the 3rd Artillery Brigade of the Guards. During the Civil War he fought on the White Guard side and evacuated to Turkey together with Wrangel's army. In 1922 he came to Estonia, where at first he worked as an unskilled labourer at a sawmill, later as a draughtsman at the Ministry of Agriculture and as a draughtsman at a textile factory. He illustrated books and designed theatre sets and postcards. He took part in local Russian literary societies.

artists.b: Sündinud 05.02.1851, Tartu; surnud 03.03.1912. Haridus: Sai maalikunsti alal Tartus algteadmisi K. von Kügelgenilt ja litograafia alal C. A. Shulzi töökojas. Jätkas õpinguid 1872–77 Düsseldorfi Kunstiakadeemias, sealhulgas 1874 E. von Gebhradti ja aastast 1875 E. Dückeri juures. Tegi õpimatku Vestfaali, Reini ülemjooksule ja Põhjamere saartele. Õppis lühikest aega Pariisis.
artists.ben: Born 05.02.1851, Tartu; died 03.03.1912. Education: Received basic knowledge in painting in Tartu from K. von Kügelgen and in lithography in C. A. Shulz's workshop. Continued studies 1872-77 at the Düsseldorf Academy of Art, including in 1874 with E. von Gebhardt and from 1875 with E. Dücker. Made study trips to Westphalia, the upper reaches of the Rhine and the North Sea islands. Studied briefly in Paris.

artists.wdesc: English painter, printmaker, pictorial satirist, social critic and editorial cartoonist (1697-1764)

artists.b: Kunstniku perekond opteerus 1920 Eestisse. A. Hoidre õppis 1933-1937 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis graafikat, lõpetas Riigi kõrgema kunstikooli 1941. Samal aastal mobiliseeriti Punaarmesse, võttis osa lahingutest ja oli kunstnike rindebrigaadis. 1944-1982 oli ERKI (EKA) õppejõud.
artists.ben: The artist's family opted for Estonia in 1920. A. Hoidre studied graphic art at the State School of Applied Arts in 1933-1937, graduated from the State Higher Art School in 1941. In the same year he was mobilised into the Red Army, took part in battles and was in the artists' front brigade. From 1944-1982 he was a lecturer at ERKI (EKA).

artists.b: 1862-64  Birkenruh maakonnagümnaasiumi õpetaja (Cesise lähedal)1864. aastast  Kuressaare progümnaasiumi (1865 - gümnaasiumi) vanade keelte ja saksa kirjanduse ülemõpetaja. Aktiivse ühiskonnategelasena võttis õpetaja juhtivalt osa linnapargi rajamisest, hoiukassa loomisest, tuletõrjeühingu asutamisest.Suurimad on Holzmayeri teened muististeuurijana. Tema juhatusel korraldati arheoloogilisi väljakaevamisi Kaarma maalinnal, Pöide ordulinuses jne. Tänu tema tegevusele olid Saaremaa ja Muhumaa 19. sajandi teisel poolel arheoloogiliselt üheks paremini uuritud alaks Baltimail.Saaremaa Uurimise Seltsi (Verein zur Kunde Oesels) asutajaliige, seltsi viitsepresident ja muuseumi juhataja  1867-1890.
artists.ben: 1862-64 teacher at the Birkenruh county gymnasium (near Cesis). From 1864 senior teacher of ancient languages and German literature at the Kuressaare progymnasium (from 1865 - gymnasium). As an active public figure, the teacher took a leading part in the establishment of the town park, the founding of a savings bank, and the establishment of a fire brigade society. Holzmayer's greatest merits are as a researcher of antiquities. Under his direction archaeological excavations were carried out at the Kaarma hill fort, the Pöide Order castle, etc. Thanks to his activity, Saaremaa and Muhumaa were, in the second half of the 19th century, one of the archaeologically best-studied areas in the Baltic provinces. Founding member of the Society for the Study of Saaremaa (Verein zur Kunde Oesels), vice-president of the society and curator of the museum 1867-1890.

artists.b: Õppis 1815-20 Tartu Ülikoolis sõjateadust, osales joonistuskooli töös. 1826 või 1827 valiti Turu Ülikooli joonistusõpetajaks, kuid loobus sellest. Elas kuni 1841 Tartus, kus maalis portreid. Sealt suundus Moskvasse, hiljem elas Tbilisis. ( V. Vaga, Kunst Tartus XIX saj., Tallinn, 1971; A. Lõugas, A. Allikvee, "Baltisaksa portreekunst Eestis 1750-1900", lk. 116 ja 150) Geboren im Gouvernement Orjol. Studierte Kriegswissenschaften an der Universität Dorpat und gleichzeitig das Zeichnen bei K. A. Senff. 1827 bewarb er sich um die Stelle des Zeichenlehrers an der Universität Åbo. Er schickte Probezeichnungen dorthin und wurde auch angenommen, trat jedoch die Stelle in Åbo nicht an. Lebte in Dorpat bis 1841. Von Zeit zu Zeit beschäftigte sich mit der Kunst, vor allem mit dem Porträt. Lebte nachmals in Moskau und Tbilisi.
artists.ben: He studied military science at the University of Tartu in 1815–20 and took part in the work of the drawing school. In 1826 or 1827 he was elected drawing teacher at the University of Turku, but declined the position. He lived in Tartu until 1841, where he painted portraits. From there he moved to Moscow, and later lived in Tbilisi. (V. Vaga, Kunst Tartus XIX saj., Tallinn, 1971; A. Lõugas, A. Allikvee, "Baltisaksa portreekunst Eestis 1750-1900", pp. 116 and 150) Geboren im Gouvernement Orjol. Studierte Kriegswissenschaften an der Universität Dorpat und gleichzeitig das Zeichnen bei K. A. Senff. 1827 bewarb er sich um die Stelle des Zeichenlehrers an der Universität Åbo. Er schickte Probezeichnungen dorthin und wurde auch angenommen, trat jedoch die Stelle in Åbo nicht an. Lebte in Dorpat bis 1841. Von Zeit zu Zeit beschäftigte sich mit der Kunst, vor allem mit dem Porträt. Lebte nachmals in Moskau und Tbilisi.

artists.b: OLI Algul moelehejoonistaja ja humor. illustr. autor. lÕI Ka anat.-joonised Iinimese ja hobuse anatoomia atlasele. Viljeles hiljem litot, oforti ja puugravüüri, samuti akv. ja külmnõela eri töötlusmeetodeid. Ta on loonud palju tarbegraafikat, eriti ekslbr., aga ka portreid, akte, interjööre jm. Tema stiil on intiimne, täpne, idülliline. tema maalilised litod kujutavad Itaalia  ja Venemaa reisimuljed. 1930. aastatel sümpatiseerisid talle natsid, kuid partei liikmeks ta ei astunud. Siiski tegi ta vastavas laadis töid.

1857-1875 Tartus tegutsenud litograaf, fotograaf ja ärimees, pärit Saksamaalt. 1857 omandas endise G. F. Schlateri litograafiatöökoja Tartus. Andis välja Tartu vaategraafikat ja muid trükiseid, valmistas portreid ja grupipilte, rakendas palju fotolitograafiat. L. Höflingeri fotoateljee asus Tartus, Promenaadi tänaval (Sukoffsky majas).
artists.ben: A lithographer, photographer and businessman active in Tartu from 1857-1875, originally from Germany. In 1857 he acquired the former G. F. Schlater lithography workshop in Tartu. He published views of Tartu and other prints, produced portraits and group pictures, and made much use of photolithography. L. Höflinger's photography studio was located in Tartu, on Promenaadi Street (in the Sukoffsky house).
