Exhibiting black and white flags of NATO member states, she was referring to the organisation's principles based on rules and clearly stated activities, where differences between members have been levelled out. Dripping cans of various coloured paint hung from the ceiling hint that a perfect system could never exist.

Murka's work often conveys a film-like seriality, best visible in her 16-piece series of paintings, exhibited together with video and installation at the show “Hairpower” (2010). The paintings depict a still from the 1928 French film “The passion of Joan of Arc”, where the heroine's hair is cut prior to her execution. This scene shows the humiliation of a person, but Murka adds other symbolic meanings to the hair, making it simultaneously repulsive and attractive.

For the show “Objects in Mirror Are Closer than They Appear” (2013) Murka painted an anonymous and taped-up object from every side, and with the positioning of the paintings, created an illusion reminiscent of a display case. The relation between reality and painting was also in focus in “Sisus” (2015), where Murka was working in deconstructing painting. In her eyes already the surface of a painting is a site of numerous compromises, enough to enhance its nuances. The process of painting becoming a painting is dependent on quotidian and earthly conditions, often by chance: what is the material, how many times the surface has been coated, etc. The series of multi-surfaced paintings “Minus” (In me) takes the viewer right inside the work, as the surface is reflective and the.
grp: school:Academy of Fine Arts of Helsinki

artists.b: 1979-84 Tallinna Kunstiülikool arhitektuur. 1986 Rühm T; 1988 Eesti Arhitektide Liit; 1990 Maalikunstnike Liit. 1991 Mosabäcka galerri, Helsingi; 1999 Sebra galerii; 2001 Pirkko-Lias Topelius, Helsingi.
artists.ben: 1979-84 Tallinn Art University, architecture. 1986 Rühm T; 1988 Estonian Union of Architects; 1990 Estonian Painters' Association. 1991 Mosabäcka gallery, Helsinki; 1999 Sebra gallery; 2001 Pirkko-Lias Topelius, Helsinki.

artists.b: Tartu raehärra ja maalikunstnik. Lõpetas 1876 Tartus gümnaasiumi, õppis kodulinnas Woldemar Friedrich Krügeri ja Julie Wilhelmine Hagen-Schwarzi juures õli- ja akvarellmaali. Jätkas kunstiõpinguid Viinis William Ungeri juures ning Berliinis Gustav Richteri juures. Aastatel 1880–1897 pidas Tartus pruulikoda. Sai 1881 Tartu kodanikuks ning oli kuni 1897. aastani linnavolinik. 1888–1889 oli Tartu raehärra. 1898–1920 töötas pangaametnikuna Pihkvas, Łódźis, Šiauliais ja Riias.  Maalinud õli ja akvarelltehnikas maastikke. Esinenud näitustel Tartus, Riias, Peterburis ja Moskvas. - Vikipeedia.
artists.ben: Tartu town councillor and painter. Graduated from the gymnasium in Tartu in 1876, studied oil and watercolour painting in his home town under Woldemar Friedrich Krüger and Julie Wilhelmine Hagen-Schwarz. Continued his art studies in Vienna under William Unger and in Berlin under Gustav Richter. Ran a brewery in Tartu from 1880 to 1897. Became a citizen of Tartu in 1881 and was a town councillor until 1897. Was a Tartu town councillor in 1888–1889. Worked as a bank official in Pskov, Łódź, Šiauliai and Riga from 1898 to 1920. Painted landscapes in oil and watercolour technique. Exhibited in Tartu, Riga, St. Petersburg and Moscow. - Wikipedia.

Eva Mustonen (1986) is an artist interested in the materiality of the artwork and storytelling through texts and visual images. By combining techniques of textile art and everyday objects, Mustonen often highlights personal stories. Her works can be seen as belonging to the feminist tradition, where private stories are also imbued with a political voice.

With the exhibition “Everyday Poetry” (2014) Mustonen described inward-looking existential themes. Working with textile, used objects and texts, she created fragmented narratives that at times converged into a larger series, at other times were no more than a singular signifier of a quotidian sentiment. In her solo show “Looks Promising” (2015) Mustonen exhibited tapestry alongside installation and text – together these three elements mapped out the rushed route from the beginning to the end-point. Mustonen often approaches weaving intuitively without a pre-prepared design, thus relinquishing the traditional time-consuming weaving process.

Mustonen's work is especially remarkable in its sensitivity towards craftsmanship and materials and their combination with everyday objects. The central theme of her exhibition “Diamond House” (2017) was home and a playful reconsidering of both that notion and the displayed materials. By combining women's clothing, household appliances, a tea set and cleaning products, Mustonen stages delicate micro dramas that provide a glimpse into the artist's everyday life.

Eva Mustonen studied textile design at Tartu Art College (BA, 2010), textile art at University of Gothenburg (2012, MA) and at the department of sculpture and installation at the Estonian Academy of Arts (MA, 2018). She has participated in group exhibitions in Estonia, Sweden and Lithuania. In 2019 she was a resident at the Rupert Residency Program. In 2014 she was awarded with the Young Textile Artist Award and in 2017 the Eduard Wiiralt Stipend. In 2021 Mustonen undertakes a residency at WIELS Contemporary Art Center.

artists.b: Sündis Tallinnas, õppis 7. keskkoolis ja 1962-1969 ERKI-s graafikat. Oli ANK 64 rühmituse asutajaliige. Töötas ajakirja "Noorus" toimetuses 1961-1962. Avaldas artikleid, kirjutas aforisme ja luuletusi.
artists.ben: Born in Tallinn, studied at the 7th Secondary School and in 1962-1969 graphic art at ERKI. Was a founding member of the ANK 64 group. Worked in the editorial office of the magazine "Noorus" in 1961-1962. Published articles, wrote aphorisms and poems.

artists.b: 1943–1945 õppis Ordžonikidze Mäe ja Metallurgia Instituudis ning jätkas õpinguid Leningradi Mäeinstituudi IV kursusel 1946 kolis Tartusse, kus leidis tööd joonestaja-konstruktorina Arhitektuurivalitsuse juures projekteerimisbüroos 1947–1951 õppis maali Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis Alfred Kongo käe all ning lõpetas õpingud Tallinnas 1953. aastal Eesti NSV Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis 1962–1977 töötas ta samas koolis õppejõuna, seejärel hakkas vabakunstnikuks.
Sündinud 13.12.1965. Haridus: 1993–1995 Magistratuur Eesti Kunstiakadeemias; 1994 Rootsi Kuninglik Kunstiülikool, graafikatehnikad; 1988–1993 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, graafika.
artists.ben:
Marko Mäetamm (1965) is an artist whose work is based on personal stories, used to create existentially absurd and critical caricatures. Mäetamm has represented Estonia in the Venice Biennale twice: in 2003 (under the pseudonym John Smith, together with Kaido Ole) and in 2007. His work is characterised by an interdisciplinary, series-oriented and narrative approach, where figurative image and text carry an equal weight.

In the 1990s Mäetamm's work was influenced by the Pop Art of the 1960s, the so-called yellow submarine aesthetics – at the time he created colourful and abundant compositions. That period was followed by black-and-white schematic pictograms: in the series “The Chemistry of Being” (2000) the artist explored themes like birth, death and religion and in the exhibition „Loser’s Paradise“ (2007) Mäetamm focused on family and everyday life.

A distinct chapter in Mäetamm's work is the joint project with Kaido Ole under the pseudonym John Smith (2001–2006). In 2003 they represented Estonia at the Venice Biennale with the project “Marko und Kaido”. The artists created a set of paintings and installations, blending fiction with autobiographical details of childhood and life in Eastern Europe. John Smith's work offered a self-critical view on Estonia and Eastern Europe.

In 2007 Mäetamm exhibited at the Venice Biennale in the Estonian pavilion a project titled “Loser's Paradise”, a great example of his period of contemplation on the role of being a father and husband. How to create art, have a job, be there for your family and afford a bank loan and how to do all of this in harmony so that everyone would be happy? The drawings, paintings and comics that at first glance seem carefree and fun, tell stories about everyday life and existential problems, covering up fears, traumas and violent fantasies. The confessional stories have been exaggerated to absurd – to desperate situation that can only be solved through suicide, cannibalism or passive-aggressive silence.

artists.b: Rein Mägar (1944) on vabakutseline akvarellmaalile pühendunud kunstnik. Ta lõpetas Leipzigi Graafika ja Raamatukunsti Kõrgkooli (1971) ja on töötanud kirjastustes (ER, Valgus, Bit) kunstilise toimetajana. Näitustel osalemist alustas plakatistina 1972 aastal, Kunstnike Liidu liige (1977), Eesti Kujundusgraafikute Liidu (1995) ja Eesti Akvarellistide Ühenduse liige alates 1998 aastast. Sellest peale on akvarelliloominguga esinenud kõikidel EAÜ näitustel ja alates 2012 ka Euroopa Akvarelliühenduste Konföderatsiooni (ECWS) poolt korraldatud akvarellifestivalidel. Omanäitusi on toimunud Vabaduse (2009, 2014), Draakoni (2020) ja Viinistu tünnigaleriides (2022), samuti paljudes kultuuriasutustes üle Eesti. Rein Mägar on kureerinud näitusi Würthi kunstigaleriis 2005-2017 ja EAÜ näitusi Pärnu UKM-is ning Võru Linnagaleriis, neist viimasel kolmel aastal ühiseid näitusi koos Soome akvarellistidega. Ettevalmistamisel on Eesti ja Soome akvarellistide ühisnäitus Kadrioru Galeriis 2023 aasta jaanuaris. Rein Mägar on koostanud ja avaldanud kolm akvarelliteemalist trükist: „Teekond akvarellidega“ (2014), „Eesti Akvarell 2018“ ja Eesti-Soome ühisnäituse kataloogi „Mets/Metsä“ (2022).
artists.ben: Rein Mägar (1944) is a freelance artist dedicated to watercolour painting. He graduated from the Leipzig Academy of Graphic Arts and Book Design (1971) and has worked as an art editor at publishing houses (ER, Valgus, Bit). He began participating in exhibitions as a poster artist in 1972, became a member of the Artists' Union (1977), a member of the Estonian Union of Design Graphic Artists (1995) and a member of the Estonian Watercolourists' Union from 1998. Since then he has presented his watercolour work at all EAÜ exhibitions and, from 2012, also at the watercolour festivals organized by the European Confederation of Watercolour Societies (ECWS). Solo exhibitions have been held at the Vabaduse (2009, 2014), Draakoni (2020) and Viinistu barrel galleries (2022), as well as in many cultural institutions across Estonia. Rein Mägar has curated exhibitions at the Würth art gallery from 2005-2017 and EAÜ exhibitions at the Pärnu UKM and the Võru City Gallery, the latter three years' exhibitions being joint exhibitions with Finnish watercolourists. A joint exhibition of Estonian and Finnish watercolourists is being prepared at Kadrioru Galerii for January 2023. Rein Mägar has compiled and published three publications on the subject of watercolour: "Teekond akvarellidega" (2014), "Eesti Akvarell 2018" and the catalogue of the Estonian-Finnish joint exhibition "Mets/Metsä" (2022).

artists.b: Õppis 1888–1889 Uderna ministeeriumikoolis, seejärel Tartus Pelbergi algkoolis ja 1891. aastal linnakoolis. Sai kunstialased algteadmised 1899–1902 Tartu Saksa Käsitööliste Seltsi joonistuskursustel. Jätkas kunstiõpinguid 1903–1905 vabakuulajana Peterburis parun Alexander Stieglitzi kunsttööstuskoolis, keskendus Amandus Adamsoni õpilasena puunikerdusele ja modelleerimisele. Läks 1907. aasta varasügisel Pariisi, elas kunstnike ja kirjanike koloonias La Ruche (Mesipuu), õppis Filippo Colarossi vabaakadeemias (Académie Colarossi) ja Académie de la Grande Chaumière'is joonistamist ning külastas kunstinäitusi ja muuseume. 1908–1910 elas Norras. 1911. aasta suve veetis Normandias Dieppe'is. Naasis 1912 Saksamaa kaudu kodumaale, Tartusse. Ta töötas joonistusõpetajana 1913 Tartu linnakoolis, 1914 kutsehariduse Seltsi õhtukoolis, aastast 1914, püsivamalt 1916-1919, pidas ateljeestuudiot. Tegutses 1919 Eesti Töörahva Kommuuni ja Lõuna-Eesti kunstikaitsetoimkonnas. Konrad Mägi oli 20. sajandi alguskümnendite värvitundlikumaid eesti maalijaid, kes kujundas oma käsitluslaadi kaasaja moodsa kunsti mõõdukaid suundi tõlgendades. Tema lemmikvärv oli kaadmiumpunane. Looduse kujutajana oli ta suuresti mõjutatav motiivist, uued loodusmuljed põhjustasid stiili muutumise ja panid aluse uuele loomejärgule. Alati pani Mägi maalidele ka taevast. Ahvenamaal lõi ta hapraid juugendlikke taimevinjette: "Kahekesi" (1908; tušijoonistus). Pariisis puutus ta kokku impressionismi, neoimpressionismi ja fovistide loominguga, mille mõjul tema värvikäsitus muutus.Ta Saaremaa–ainelised teosed on esimesed moodsad eesti loodusmaalid. Aastast 1918 võib märgata ekspressionismi mõju, mille vastuvõttu soodustas Mäe ülitundlikkus ja emotsionaalne reageering ärevatele aegadele. Itaalia-reisiga alanud uus loomejärk tõi rahunemise. Itaalias valmisid Mägi võluvaimad maalid. Kõrvuti looduspiltidega maalis ta lilli ja portreid. Enamasti kauni välimusega naisemodellid kajastavad juugendlikku iluideaali. Hilistes portreedes väljendub 1920. aastatel tõsinenud meeleolu.
artists.ben: He studied in 1888–1889 at the Uderna parish school, then in Tartu at the Pelberg elementary school, and in 1891 at the town school. He received his first basic knowledge of art in 1899–1902 at the drawing courses of the Tartu German Craftsmen's Society. He continued his art studies in 1903–1905 as an auditor in St. Petersburg at Baron Alexander Stieglitz's School of Technical Drawing, focusing, as a pupil of Amandus Adamson, on wood carving and modelling. In early autumn 1907 he went to Paris, lived in the artists' and writers' colony La Ruche (The Beehive), studied drawing at Filippo Colarossi's free academy (Académie Colarossi) and at the Académie de la Grande Chaumière, and visited art exhibitions and museums. In 1908–1910 he lived in Norway. He spent the summer of 1911 in Dieppe, Normandy. In 1912 he returned to his homeland, to Tartu, via Germany. He worked as a drawing teacher in 1913 at the Tartu town school, in 1914 at the evening school of the Society for Vocational Education, and from 1914, more permanently in 1916–1919, kept a studio. In 1919 he was active in the Estonian Working People's Commune and in the South Estonian Art Protection Committee. Konrad Mägi was one of the most colour-sensitive Estonian painters of the early decades of the 20th century, who shaped his manner by interpreting the moderate trends of contemporary modern art. His favourite colour was cadmium red. As a depicter of nature, he was greatly influenced by his motifs; new impressions of nature caused changes in his style and laid the foundation for a new creative stage. Mägi always included the sky in his paintings. On the Åland Islands he created delicate Art Nouveau plant vignettes: "Kahekesi" [Two Together] (1908; ink drawing). In Paris he came into contact with the work of the Impressionists, Neo-Impressionists, and Fauvists, under whose influence his treatment of colour changed. His works with Saaremaa motifs are the first modern Estonian landscape paintings. From 1918 onward the influence of Expressionism can be noticed, its reception being favoured by Mägi's extreme sensitivity and emotional response to troubled times. A new creative stage began with a trip to Italy, bringing calm. In Italy Mägi's most enchanting paintings were created. Alongside landscapes, he painted flowers and portraits. The mostly beautiful-looking female models reflect an Art Nouveau ideal of beauty. In his late portraits, the mood that intensified in the 1920s finds expression.

artists.b: Männi loobus 1960. aastail naturalistlikult detailirikkast laadist, eksperimenteerides uudsete materjalidega ning taotledes senisest erinevat plastilist vabadusastet. Ta oli üks esimesi raudkonstruktsioonide ja keevitatud raudskulptuuride loojaid. Huvitudes kaasaegsetest väljendusvõimalustest skulptuuris, lõi ta 1967. aastal Eesti esimese mobiili. Rütmilise ülesehitusega tinglikult lahendatud figuuridega resoneerib ta 1960. aastate teiste poole maalikunsti vallanud nn karmi stiiliga. Uute materjalide väljendusvõimalusi testivad 1970. aastail loodud plastmassist, babiidist ja tinast teosed. Erudeeritud õppejõuna oli Männi oluline teejuht paljudele 1970.–1980. aastail ellu astunud Eesti skulptoritele. Vormi esteetiliste ja tunnetuslike omaduste rõhutamine põimus tema loomingus huviga popkunsti vahendite vastu ja ready-made’i kasutamisega skulptuuris.
artists.ben: In the 1960s Männi abandoned a naturalistic, detail-rich style, experimenting with novel materials and seeking a degree of plastic freedom different from before. He was one of the first to create iron constructions and welded iron sculptures. Interested in contemporary means of expression in sculpture, he created Estonia's first mobile in 1967. With their rhythmic construction of conventionally rendered figures, his works resonate with the so-called hard style that dominated painting in the latter half of the 1960s. Works created in the 1970s from plastic, babbitt metal and tin test the expressive possibilities of new materials. As an erudite lecturer, Männi was an important guide for many Estonian sculptors who began their careers in the 1970s–1980s. In his work, the emphasis on the aesthetic and perceptual qualities of form was interwoven with an interest in the means of pop art and the use of the ready-made in sculpture.

artists.b: Õppis 1914–1916 Peterburi ülikooli ajaloo-keeleteaduskonnas ja 1924–1928 Tartu ülikooli õigusteaduskonnas. 1916–1917 oli I maailmasõjas, 1917–1918 sõjavangis Austrias, 1918–1919 teenis Arhangelskis Briti Põhjakorpuse staabis. 1919–1921 Eesti Vabariigi sõjaväeline esindaja, 1921–1923 chargé d’affaires Leedus. 1923–1927 Välisministeeriumi poliitilise osakonna juhataja, 1924–1925 chargé d’affaires Pariisis ja Brüsselis ning 1926 Moskva saatkonna nõunik. 1927–1931 välisministri abi. 1931–1934 saadik Itaalias ja Šveitsis ning alaline esindaja Rahvasteliidu juures, 1934–1971 saadik Inglismaal.
artists.ben: Studied 1914–1916 at the Faculty of History and Linguistics of the University of St. Petersburg and 1924–1928 at the Faculty of Law of the University of Tartu. Took part in the First World War in 1916–1917, was a prisoner of war in Austria in 1917–1918, and served in 1918–1919 at the staff of the British North Russia Corps in Arkhangelsk. 1919–1921 military representative of the Republic of Estonia, 1921–1923 chargé d'affaires in Lithuania. 1923–1927 head of the political department of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 1924–1925 chargé d'affaires in Paris and Brussels, and in 1926 counsellor at the Moscow legation. 1927–1931 assistant to the Minister of Foreign Affairs. 1931–1934 envoy to Italy and Switzerland and permanent representative to the League of Nations, 1934–1971 envoy to England.

artists.b: Ants Mölder (1939–2009) tegutses modernistliku skulptorina aktiivselt 1970. ja 1980. aastatel. Talle omane mänguline suhe poolabstraktsete vormidega viis katsetama erinevate materjalidega, millest alumiinium ja epoksüvaik ilmestasid Eesti skulptuuris just 1970. aastaid. Ants Mölder on loonud dekoratiivseid vorme ja figuure ka puust ja marmorist. Erilist tähelepanu on pälvinud tema mahagonskulptuurid. Väikeseformaadilised mitmesugustes tehnikates loodud joonistused avavad vaatajale skulptori mõtteskeemid ajast, mis eelnes ühe või teise skulptuuri valmimisele. Olulise osa Ants Mölderi loomingust moodustavad mälestusmedalid, auhinnad ja väikevormid. Eesti avalikus ruumis on 1970. aastail tema loodud Teise maailmasõja monumendid.
artists.ben: Ants Mölder (1939–2009) was active as a modernist sculptor mainly in the 1970s and 1980s. His characteristic playful approach to semi-abstract forms led him to experiment with various materials, of which aluminium and epoxy resin were especially characteristic of Estonian sculpture in the 1970s. Ants Mölder has also created decorative forms and figures from wood and marble. His mahogany sculptures have received special attention. Small-format drawings made in various techniques reveal to the viewer the sculptor's schemes of thought from the time preceding the completion of one or another sculpture. Memorial medals, awards and small forms make up a significant part of Ants Mölder's oeuvre. Second World War monuments created by him in the 1970s can be found in Estonia's public space.

artists.b: Tema looming on jagunenud mitmesse erinevasse ajastusse. 1950. aastail valminud skulptuurid kuuluvad tollase realistliku laadi paremikku (Ühistööks abikaasa Signe Mölderiga jääb tänaseks teisaldatud V.I. Lenini monument Jõhvis (koos Enn Roosiga). Arseni Möldri väljapaistvamaks monumentaalteoseks jääb N. Pirogovi klassitsistlikus orderis teostatud monument Tartus (1952, koos Juhan Raudsepaga), F.R. Kreutzwaldi mälestusmärgi pronksreljeef „Assamalla lahing” 1957, mitmed väärismaterjalides teostatud mälestustahvlid jpm. Tema vabaskulptuuride paremik („Vormija” (1950, pronks 1964), „Teatejooksjad” (pronks, 1956), ). 1960. aastail liitus ta Eesti skulptuuri haaranud modernismilainega, mitmed kammerlikumad tööd šamotist, epoksüüdvaigust, puust ja metallist äratavad tähelepanu kas ilusa puhta dekoratiivse vormikultuuriga või siis on taotluslikult humoristlikud („Järjekord” (1969, EKM), „Staadionil” (1969), „Kanapere” (1978) jt). Arseni Möldri loomingus on oluline roll tema naiiv-humoristlikel ehetel. Väike osa viimastest on leidnud koha Tarbekunsti- ja Disainimuuseumis.
artists.ben: His work is divided into several different periods. The sculptures created in the 1950s belong to the best of the realistic style of the time (a joint work with his wife Signe Mölder remains today's relocated V.I. Lenin monument in Jõhvi (together with Enn Roos). Arseni Mölder's most outstanding monumental work remains the monument to N. Pirogov executed in a classicist order in Tartu (1952, together with Juhan Raudsepp), the bronze relief "Battle of Assamalla" of the F.R. Kreutzwald memorial, 1957, several memorial plaques executed in precious materials, and more. The best of his free-standing sculptures ("The Moulder" (1950, bronze 1964), "Relay Runners" (bronze, 1956)). In the 1960s he joined the wave of modernism that swept Estonian sculpture, several more chamber-scale works in chamotte, epoxy resin, wood and metal attract attention either with beautiful pure decorative form culture or are deliberately humorous ("The Queue" (1969, EKM), "At the Stadium" (1969), "Hen Family" (1978), etc.). In Arseni Mölder's oeuvre his naive-humorous jewellery pieces play an important role. A small portion of the latter has found a place in the Museum of Applied Art and Design.

artists.b: Photographer of thresholds, empty rooms and the edge of the visible.
artists.ben:
Krista Mölder (1972) is an artist whose work focuses on space and the experience of the viewer. Her photos and videos are full of potential – contours of perspectives and outlines of possibilities. She is primarily interested in what remains outside or beside the image.

Mölder has studied geography and has applied that experience to directly mapping various phenomena, observations, and ideas, while presenting them in a visually structured manner. The aim of one of her first series “Landmarks” (2007) was to explore the possibilities of poetic language of space and photography. This is not unlike the photo series “Inter-Space” (2016), depicting landscapes in a non-three-dimensional way, balancing between painting and photography. These images, photographed from a bird's-eye view seem to map the impossible, while casting doubt on the veracity of photography.

In 2010 Mölder was chosen to participate in the project “European Eyes on Japan. Japan Today, vol. 13”, organised by the EU–Japan Fest. As part of the project Mölder stayed at a residency in Akita, which later led to an exhibition. Japanese architecture, for example the buildings of the architect Seiichi Shirai in the forests of the Akita region made an impact on Mölder's sense of space. Stemming from that, her imagery displays man-made and natural forms that are reduced to almost two-dimensional fields of colour in the wider whole of her work. In her wide-frame snapshots, an abundance of details are revealed to the keen eye, however, these are photographed in a way that does not leave an impression of exaggeration.

Mölder takes photos on a medium format camera and mostly does not manipulate her work digitally. With great sensitivity Mölder finds photographic and aesthetic still lifes in parks and gardens as well as in the city and in living and working spaces. Windows, doors and other liminal spaces are a recurring motif in Mölder's work. Mostly, these spaces are viewed from the inside out, so that the viewer is “here”, in the space with the artist.

artists.b: Eesti Kunstimuuseumi skulptuurikogus on mõningad tema sõjajärgsete aastate realistlikud olustikuskulptuurid, portreed ja keraamilist pisiplastikat. Tema mitmetest aiaskulptuuridest on tuntuim “Mõtted Pandiverest” Nõmmel Kristjan Raua majamuuseumi aias. Signe Mölder on loonud ka avalikke skulptuure ja monumentaalplastikat. Koos Arseni Möldri ja Enn Roosiga loodud Jõhvi V. I Lenini monument on tänaseks linnast teisaldatud. 1999. aastal paigaldati Tallinna Jüriöö parki tema loodud monument II maailmasõjas osalenud eesti sõjameestele.
artists.ben: The sculpture collection of the Art Museum of Estonia contains some of his realistic genre sculptures, portraits and small ceramic plastic works from the post-war years. Of his numerous garden sculptures the best known is "Thoughts from Pandivere" in the garden of the Kristjan Raud House Museum in Nõmme. Signe Mölder has also created public sculptures and monumental plastic works. The monument to V. I. Lenin in Jõhvi, created together with Arseni Mölder and Enn Roos, has by now been removed from the town. In 1999 a monument created by her to Estonian soldiers who took part in World War II was erected in Jüriöö Park in Tallinn.

artists.b: Pärit Rakverest, õppis "Pallases" 1927-1936 ning lõpetas selle N. Triigi õpilasena. Täendas end aasta hiljem Pariisis, Berliinis ja Dresdenis. Töötas 1940-1965 oma kodulinna Rakvere teatris lavakujundajana: kujundas umbes 150 lavastust. Ta oli hea professionaalse tasemega maalija, kes esines ka vabariiklikel näitustel.
artists.ben: From Rakvere, studied at "Pallas" 1927-1936 and graduated as a student of N. Triik. He furthered his education a year later in Paris, Berlin and Dresden. From 1940-1965 he worked as a stage designer at the theatre of his home town Rakvere: he designed about 150 productions. He was a painter of good professional level, who also exhibited at national exhibitions.

artists.b: Aastast 1877 tegutses Tartus joonistusõpetaja ja portreemaalijana, 1883–1908 juhatas Tartu Saksa Käsitööliste Seltsi joonistuskursusi. R. von zur Mühleni käe all on kunsti õppinud M. Pukits, K. Mägi, J. Koort, A. Tassa, eraõpilasena K. Raud. 1901 sai Peterburi KA-lt vabakunstniku nimetuse. Oma kunstikäsitluselt oli R. von zur Mühlen lähedane Düsseldorfi koolkonna realistidele. Tuntud peamiselt hea karakteerimisoskusega portretistina. Graafikaloomingu paremiku moodustavad Tartu eluolu kajastavad pliiatsijoonistused ja litosari Dorpater Skizzen (1885).
artists.ben: Since 1877 he worked in Tartu as a drawing teacher and portrait painter, and from 1883 to 1908 he directed the drawing courses of the Tartu German Craftsmen's Society. Under R. von zur Mühlen, M. Pukits, K. Mägi, J. Koort and A. Tassa studied art, as did K. Raud as a private pupil. In 1901 he received the title of free artist from the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts. In his artistic approach R. von zur Mühlen was close to the realists of the Düsseldorf school. He is known mainly as a portraitist with good characterisation skills. The best of his graphic works are pencil drawings reflecting Tartu life and the lithograph series Dorpater Skizzen (1885).

artists.b: Õppis 1913–1916 Eesti Kunstiseltsis ja Ants Laikmaa ateljeekoolis. 1917–1918 asutas koos B. Tomasbergi, O. Kallise ja A. Krimsiga ühingu Vikerla. 1919 panustas kunstivara päästmisse ja kogus kokku Vabadussõjas langenud B. Tomasbergi pärandi. 1920 ilmus Tartus tema 10-leheline linoollõigete album Primeurs. 1921 siirdus Pariisi, kus elatus juhutöödest.
artists.ben: Studied in 1913–1916 at the Estonian Art Society and at Ants Laikmaa's studio school. In 1917–1918, together with B. Tomasberg, O. Kallis and A. Krims, founded the society Vikerla. In 1919 contributed to the rescue of art treasures and collected the legacy of B. Tomasberg, who had fallen in the War of Independence. In 1920 his 10-sheet album of linocuts Primeurs was published in Tartu. In 1921 he moved to Paris, where he made a living from odd jobs.

artists.b: Õppis Jenas, Göttingenis ja Erlangenis teoloogiat. 1790. aastal asus Dresdeni Kunstiakadeemiasse akadeemik Chr Klengeli juurde maali õppima. Pärast korduvat Itaalias viibimist asus ta elama Stuttgardi, kus temast sai kunstikooli õpetaja ja kuninglik õukonnakunstnik.
artists.ben: Studied theology in Jena, Göttingen and Erlangen. In 1790 he entered the Dresden Academy of Art to study painting under academician Chr. Klengel. After repeated stays in Italy he settled in Stuttgart, where he became a teacher at the art school and royal court painter.

artists.b: On sündinud Tartus (1972). Lõpetanud TÜ õpetajakoolituse (2001), TÜ filosoofiateaduskonna maalikunsti eriala (1999), Tartu Kunstikooli (1992). Tartu Kõrgema Kunstikooli maalimise õppejõud alates 2001-2009. Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 2005. Tartu Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 2000. Näitustel esinenud alates 1997.
artists.ben: Born in Tartu (1972). Graduated from the University of Tartu teacher training programme (2001), the painting specialty of the Faculty of Philosophy of the University of Tartu (1999), the Tartu Art School (1992). Lecturer in painting at the Tartu Art College from 2001-2009. Member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 2005. Member of the Tartu Artists' Association since 2000. Has exhibited since 1997.

artists.b: Karl-Kristjan Nagel (s. 1977) on lõpetanud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia maali erialal (1999). Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 2011. a.
artists.ben: Karl-Kristjan Nagel (b. 1977) graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts in painting (1999). Member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 2011.

artists.b: Naive painter of wide, animal-populated landscapes; the most reproduced living Estonian artist.
artists.ben: Naive painter of wide, animal-populated landscapes; the most reproduced living Estonian artist.

artists.b: Üldhariduse sai ta Tartu Poeglaste Gümnaasiumis. 1937. aastal asus kunstikooli Pallas, kus õppis Villem Ormissoni maaliklassis. Olnud vahepeal aasta sõjaväes, jätkas 1940. aastal õpinguid Aleksander Vardi ateljees. 1941-1942 oli rindel ja jätkas õpinguid 1943. aastal kuni Pallase kunstikooli sulgemiseni.
artists.ben: He received his general education at the Tartu Boys' Gymnasium. In 1937 he entered the Pallas art school, where he studied in Villem Ormisson's painting class. Having spent a year in the army in between, he continued his studies in 1940 in Aleksander Vardi's studio. In 1941–1942 he was at the front, and continued his studies in 1943 until the closure of the Pallas art school.

artists.b: Naima Neidre (1943) on pikka aega kõrgel tasemel tegutsenud graafik, illust- raator ja akvarellist, kelle ülimalt tundliku visuaalse käekirjaga teosed põimivad lugusid loodusest, merest ja inimestest. Neidre on lõpetanud ERKI graafika eriala (1971) ja osalenud arvukatel näitustel nii Eestis kui ka rahvusvaheliselt. Tema teoseid leidub paljudes (era)kogudes ning ta on pälvinud mitmeid tunnustusi, sh Kristjan Raua preemia (2004). Neidre on Eesti Vabagraafikute Ühenduse liige ja Eesti Kunstnike liidu auliige.
artists.ben: Naima Neidre (1943) is a graphic artist, illustrator and watercolourist who has long worked at a high level, whose works, marked by an extremely sensitive visual style, weave together stories of nature, the sea and people. Neidre graduated from ERKI in graphic art (1971) and has participated in numerous exhibitions both in Estonia and internationally. Her works can be found in many (private) collections, and she has received several honours, including the Kristjan Raud Prize (2004). Neidre is a member of the Estonian Association of Free Graphic Artists and an honorary member of the Estonian Artists' Association.

artists.b: Kaljuvee on töötanud Rakvere MEKi juhatajana 1980–1986, Rakvere rajooni Täitevkomitee esimehena 1987–1990, Lääne-Viru maavanemana 1990–1992, Kunda Nordic Tsemendi juhatuse liikmena 1992–1994 ja nõukogu esimehena 1994–1999, Eesti Hoiupanga Ida regiooni direktorina ja peadirektori asetäitjana 1994–1998 ning Eesti Põlevkivi juhatuse liikmena 1999–2006 ja juhatuse esimehena 2006–2007.
artists.ben: Kaljuvee worked as the director of the Rakvere MEK from 1980–1986, as chairman of the Rakvere district Executive Committee from 1987–1990, as governor of Lääne-Viru county from 1990–1992, as a board member of Kunda Nordic Tsement from 1992–1994 and as chairman of the supervisory board from 1994–1999, as director of the Eastern region and deputy director general of Eesti Hoiupank from 1994–1998, and as a board member of Eesti Põlevkivi from 1999–2006 and as chairman of the board from 2006–2007.

artists.b: Stanislav Netšvolodov (s. 1935 Ukrainas) on Eesti skulptor, medali- ja maalikunstnik. Ta on lõpetanud Kiievi Ehitusinseneride Instituudi arhitektuuri erialal. Netšvolodov on loonud pronks-, puu- ning kiviskulptuure ja monumente ning tegeleb ka maalikunsti ja graafikaga. Netšvolodovi lemmikharrastus on medalikunst, ta on mitmete Tartu Ülikooli medalite (sh ülikooli audoktori medali ja Skytte medali) autor. Skulptuuri-alal tegutseb Netšvolodov alates 1962. aastast. 2002. aastal pälvis Stanislav Netšvolodov Anton Starkopfi nimelise kunstipreemia. Ta on Eesti Kunstnile Liidu ja F.I.D.E.M.-i liige.
artists.ben: Stanislav Netšvolodov (b. 1935 in Ukraine) is an Estonian sculptor, medallist and painter. He graduated from the Kiev Institute of Civil Engineers with a degree in architecture. Netšvolodov has created bronze, wood and stone sculptures and monuments and also works in painting and graphic art. Netšvolodov's favourite pursuit is medal art; he is the author of several medals of the University of Tartu (including the university's honorary doctorate medal and the Skytte Medal). Netšvolodov has been active in sculpture since 1962. In 2002 Stanislav Netšvolodov was awarded the Anton Starkopf Art Prize. He is a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and F.I.D.E.M.

artists.b: Lõpetas 1926 Viljandi Eesti Haridusseltsi Tütarlaste Gümnaasiumi 1928. aasta algul astus ta Kõrgemasse Kunstikooli Pallas, kus õppis maali esialgu Nikolai Triigi, siis Ado Vabbe ateljees. Kooli lõpetas ta 1936. aastal koos Johannes Võerahansu, Richard Sagritsa, Karl Pärsimäe ja Ellinor Aikiga.
artists.ben: Graduated in 1926 from the Viljandi Estonian Education Society Girls' Gymnasium. At the beginning of 1928 he entered the Higher Art School Pallas, where he studied painting initially in Nikolai Triik's studio, then in Ado Vabbe's studio. He graduated from the school in 1936 together with Johannes Võerahansu, Richard Sagrits, Karl Pärsimägi and Ellinor Aikas.

artists.b: Tõnu Noorits, PhD (s.1952 Tartus) lõpetas Tartu Ülikooli 1975.a. bioloogina. Doktorikraadi kaitses 1984.a. Fotokunstiga tegeleb aastast 1982. 1992.a. rajas koos Silver Vahtrega disaini- ja kunstiseltsi KYNA, kus tegeleb foto-lavastuste, kujundamise ja kirjastamisega. Ta on mitmekülgne looja ning tema tööd – portreed, aktid, fotolavastused, abstraktsed maastikud – sisaldavad tihti ootamatuid nägemusi. Fotodele on iseloomulik kõrge pildikultuuur ja perfektne teostus. Möödunud sajandi lõpukümnendite Euroopa fotosalongides oli ta enim eksponeeritud Eesti autor. Tal on olnud 35 isiknäitust erinevates riikides – Austrias, Belgias, Itaalias, Lätis, Prantsusmaal, Rootsis, Saksamaal, samuti 12 grupinäitust.
artists.ben: Tõnu Noorits, PhD (b. 1952 in Tartu) graduated from the University of Tartu in 1975 as a biologist. He defended his doctoral degree in 1984. He has worked in photographic art since 1982. In 1992, together with Silver Vahter, he founded the design and art society KYNA, where he engages in photo-staging, design and publishing. He is a versatile creator, and his works – portraits, nudes, staged photographs, abstract landscapes – often contain unexpected visions. His photographs are characterised by a high pictorial culture and perfect execution. In the final decades of the last century he was the most exhibited Estonian author in European photo salons. He has had 35 solo exhibitions in various countries – Austria, Belgium, Italy, Latvia, France, Sweden, Germany, as well as 12 group exhibitions.

artists.b: Arreteeriti 26. aprillil 1941, Kirovi oblasti NKVD sõjatribunal määras talle 25. juulil 1941 § 58-13 alusel mahalaskmise koos kogu vara konfiskeerimisega. Teadaolevalt lasti maha 1. septembril 1941 kell 18.15.
artists.ben: He was arrested on 26 April 1941; on 25 July 1941 the NKVD military tribunal of Kirov Oblast sentenced him to death by shooting under § 58-13, together with confiscation of all property. He is known to have been shot on 1 September 1941 at 18.15.

artists.b: MM-pronks ja 1924. aasta olümpialane Noormägi  one esimese Eestist olümpiale jõudnud puudega sportlane. Nimelt oli ta kurttumm (Eesti Spordileht: "Kurttumm, ei kuule ega kõnele, sellevast aga tubli tõstja!"), kes jõudis spordi juurde tänu Georg Lurichile. Lurich külastas nimelt Vändra kurttummade kooli just sel ajal, kui Noormägi seal õppis.
artists.ben: World championship bronze medallist and 1924 Olympian Noormägi was the first athlete with a disability from Estonia to reach the Olympics. Namely he was deaf-mute (Eesti Spordileht: "Deaf-mute, he neither hears nor speaks, but nevertheless a fine weightlifter!"), who came to sport thanks to Georg Lurich. Lurich indeed visited the Vändra school for the deaf-mute precisely at the time when Noormägi was studying there.

Kristina Norman (1979) is an artist whose interdisciplinary work includes video installations, sculptural objects, and interventions in the city space, as well as documentaries and performance. Norman's artistic practice is context-focused and she works with themes that relate to ideologies, controversial political processes and the sore points of history, looking for ways to approach polarising subject matter beyond mutually exclusive narratives.

A notable part of Norman's work addresses the collective memory and identity through monuments. One of her most well-known projects “After-war” represented Estonia at the 53rd Venice Biennale in 2009 (curated by Marco Laimre). The work was based on the story of the Bronze Soldier, a monument to the Soviet army that the Estonian government had removed from Tallinn city centre in 2007, which was then replaced by a golden replica of the statue by Norman. Through this intervention the artist was looking for ways to use the golden monument to draw attention to the various groups living in Estonia who do not share the same historic memory. “After-war” was based on Norman's several previous projects addressing the Bronze Soldier, such as the film “Monolith” (2007), and the installation “Community” (2007) that consists of souvenir size figurines of the Bronze Soldier, painted in the colours of various pop culture characters.

This was followed by the film “A monument to please everyone” (2011) looking at the process of putting up the monument to commemorate the Estonian War of Independence. The film focused on the reorganising of the landscape of Estonian collective memory and correlating it to the nation-focused narrative immediately after the Bronze Soldier was moved. This was also a project for the people in power to establish their political will  that came to divide the mostly Estonian-speaking public regarding the monument's name and meaning (a monument to freedom or a statue to victory) as well as its aesthetic qualities. Following the young patriotic authors of the monument and the politicians who directed them, the film shows the behind-the-scenes of the process.

Her following works “0.8 square metres” (2012) and “Common Ground” (2013) also address perpetuating or erasing collective memory, tied together into a trilogy by an artistic exploration of spatial aspects of remembering and relying on historic parallels. In 2014 Norman took part in the 10th Manifesta Biennial in St. Petersburg (curated by Kasper König and Joanna Warzsa) with the public sculpture project “Souvenir” (2014) and a video installation “Ir.

artists.b: Post-internet artist working with image ecology, biotech and the digital creature.
artists.ben:
Katja Novitskova (1984) deals in her work with the depiction of evolutional development, using internet as the source of visual data. In the early 2010s, she was among the first artists, who took post-internet for subject matter and designed its aesthetics. Novitskova’s

situates in the crossing of visual culture and science fiction, inducing discomfort and enstrangement by blending futuristic fantasy with everyday reality. In general, Novitskova works in installative method, using photo-sculptures as her main medium.

” is a pioneering handbook, which offers solutions for coping with the situation in which internet has become a pre-condition and therefore the senses of a human-being are flooded with signs. In 2017, Katja Novitskova represented Estonia in 57th Venice Biennial with the exhibition “

”, which focused on the digital culture of contemporary times, looking back at it from a science-fictional position, when the world as we know it today, didn’t exist. That brought up questions of recognizing the hi-tech reality – who dares to say that the actual life is fantastic film and future is now?

artists.b: Sündinud 06.12.1964. Haridus: 1985–1992 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, graafika, magistrikraad.
artists.ben: Born 06.12.1964. Education: 1985–1992 Estonian Academy of Arts, graphic art, master's degree.

artists.b: Lõpetanud Tartu Ülikoolis ajaloo (1984) ja maali (1995 B.A. cum laude; 2017 M.A.) erilalad, läbinud samas filosoofia teadusmagistrantuuri. Õpetanud erinevates koolisüsteemides, sh olnud pikka aega Tartu Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis nii teoreetilistes (kaasaja kunsti loengud) kui praktilistes (maalikursused, loovjoonistamine jm) ainetes külalisõppejõud; Tartu Ülikoolis lugenud Lääne kaasaegse kunsti loengukursust magistrantidele. Teostanud monumentaalmaalinguid koolidesse, kureerinud ja kujundanud ca 10 teemanäitust, kirjutanud kunstist ligi 300 pikemat või lühemat vähem või rohkem interpreteerivat artiklit ja esseid, koostanud Lola Liivati loomingu kataloogi (2008) jt trükiseid, teinud kaaskunstnikega biograafilise aktsendiga tervik-intervjuusid ajakirjale Kunst.ee. LOOMING: Alates 1994 üle 30 isiknäituse, peamiselt Eestis, struktuurilt kontseptuaalsed tervikekspositsioonid koos vähema või rohkema kohaspetsiifilise ja ruumiinstallatiivse aktsendiga. Käsitleb läbi isikliku kogemuse universaalset ja eksistentsiaalset. Loomingus ühendab spontaansuse ja analüüsi. Elukestev protsess on eksperimendid maalikunsti väljendusvahenditega, inspireeritult moderni praktikaist ja kaasaja materjalidest.T.
artists.ben: Graduated from the University of Tartu with specialities in history (1984) and painting (1995 B.A. cum laude; 2017 M.A.), and completed a master's programme in philosophy there as well. Has taught in various school systems, including for a long time as a visiting lecturer at the Tartu Art College in both theoretical (lectures on contemporary art) and practical (painting courses, creative drawing, etc.) subjects; at the University of Tartu has given a lecture course on Western contemporary art to master's students. Has executed monumental paintings for schools, curated and designed approximately 10 thematic exhibitions, written nearly 300 longer or shorter, more or less interpretive articles and essays on art, compiled a catalogue of Lola Liivat's work (2008) and other publications, and made comprehensive biographically accented interviews with fellow artists for the magazine Kunst.ee. WORK: Since 1994, over 30 solo exhibitions, mainly in Estonia, structurally conceptual comprehensive expositions with a greater or lesser site-specific and spatial-installative accent. Addresses the universal and the existential through personal experience. Combines spontaneity and analysis in her work. A lifelong process is experimentation with the expressive means of painting, inspired by modernist practices and contemporary materials.T.

artists.b: 1936–1939 1936–1938 töötas ta Tartu Ülikooli didaktilis-metoodiline seminar, 1937–1940 kunstikooli Pallas joonistamise metoodika õpetaja, 1940 Konrad Mäe nimelise Riigi Kõrgema Kunstikooli direktori kohusetäitja, 1941 direktor, 1942–1943 Kõrgemate Kujutava Kunsti Kursuste õppejõud, 1943-1944 Pallase õppejõud.
artists.ben: 1936–1939 1936–1938 he worked at the didactic-methodological seminar of the University of Tartu, 1937–1940 teacher of drawing methodology at the art school Pallas, 1940 acting director of the Konrad Mägi State Higher Art School, 1941 director, 1942–1943 lecturer at the Higher Courses of Fine Art, 1943–1944 lecturer at Pallas.

artists.b: Esialgse kunstihariduse sai oma venna portselanimaalija Anton Oechsi käe all Regensburgis. 1795. aastast õppis Nürnbergis portselanimaalija K. Trosti juures ja siis Erfurtis portselanimaalija Bollermanni ning Dresdenis professor Klengeli juures. 1804. aastal kolis Jelgavasse. Õppis Tartu ülikooli joonistuskoolis Karl August Senffi juures. 1824. aastast töötas joonistusõpetajana Jelgava gümnaasiumis.
artists.ben: He received his initial art education under his brother, the porcelain painter Anton Oechs, in Regensburg. From 1795 he studied in Nuremberg under the porcelain painter K. Trost, and then in Erfurt under the porcelain painter Bollermann, and in Dresden under professor Klengel. In 1804 he moved to Jelgava. He studied at the drawing school of Tartu University under Karl August Senff. From 1824 he worked as a drawing teacher at the Jelgava gymnasium.

artists.b: Sculptor and installation artist of the transition years.
artists.ben:
Jüri Ojaver (1955) is mainly known as a sculptor and installation artist, however he also works with video and performance. Ojaver's research-based explorations look into material heritage from the past, often characterised by the absurd and existential dimension of randomness. His works that focus on memory and history are often site-specific.

Ojaver began his artistic career as a restorer, working with heritage protected objects in Tallinn Old Town. In the 1980s his sculptures were mostly figurative, using granite, marble and limestone. The changes in society in the 1990s made it possible to discuss events and subjects that were not publicly acknowledged during the Soviet period. Inspired by these developments Ojaver began creating site-specific installations, focusing on sites of memory and history.

The works “Niche. Image” (1993) and “Nonexistent Cemetery” (1994) that were exhibited at the annual exhibitions of the Soros Center for Contemporary Arts, Estonia, where they won Grand Prix, act as frames for something that, although physically absent, exists in the memory of people. The absence of matter while a mental image is present, is a universal issue, explorations of which positioned Ojaver as one of the most notable artists in Estonia after the country regained its independence.

Ojaver's international success is marked by his participation in the 1995 1st Gwangju Biennale in South-Korea with the work “Father. Son” (1995) In 1999 Ojaver represented Estonia at the Venice Biennale together with Peeter Pere and Ando Keskküla. Jüri Ojaver's work “Keystone” was a two-part waterproof plywood sculpture, exhibited in front of and in the garden of Palazzo Querini. The sculpture was based on the motif of spread legs, placed as a bridge over the canal in front of the palazzo. In the back garden of the palazzo viewers saw an upside down version of the sculpture, legs stretching towards the sky. Ojaver's bridge changed the spatial logic of the building, connecting the water gates of both shores and thus making the kitchen door into its main entrance.

artists.b: Ameerika kunstikriitik, poeet, romaanikirjanik, teadlane. Kunstiajaloo õppejõud Rice Ülikoolis USA-s, Kunstikriitika osakonna looja ja arendaja New Yorgi Kunstikoolis (School of Visual Arts in New York).
artists.ben:
Terje Ojaver (1955) is a sculptor, whose work includes abstract and figurative monumental painting, site-specific installations, performative paraphrases, classical sculpture, and video. She has also created notable monumental sculptures for public space.

In the 1990s Terje Ojaver mostly focused on site and material specific installations, characterised by a conceptual approach to nature. During the 3rd Annual Exhibition of Soros Center for Contemporary Arts, Estonia titled “Biotopia”, she exhibited the work “Bio-Top” (1994) on the columns in front of the entrance of the Tallinn Art Hall building, measuring the level of air pollution. At the open-air art centre Le vent des forêts Lahaymeix’ in Lorraine, France, Ojaver built massive protective planters around living trees (1998). At the Tallinn Botanic Garden the artist covered the ground with a ruffling carpet of natural grass, highlighting the unity of man and nature. In Kuressaare she released blocks of ice taken from the Kuressaare Castle pond in winter and preserved in a freezer, back into the pond in spring (2001), demonstrating the eternal cycles of nature. With the show “Dance of the deceived” (Petetute tants, 2009) Ojaver begun her series of replicas of large rocks, continuing it at the Sculpture Quadrennial Riga on the square of St Peter’s Church (2016), followed by a display of the rocks as floating pieces in Swan Pond in Kadriorg Park (2016), and later in Århus, Denmark (2019).

Ojaver's work ties together canons of classical sculpture and controversial technical or narrative solutions, blending high and low art. Her figure-based work (mostly using her own image) make up a significant part of her practice, telling stories of women's real and illusory positions, but also of herself as a wife, mother, daughter, her freedoms and obligations, strengths and resignations. Among these works we find “Blind” (Pime, 2011), “Awkward egg body” (Piinlik munakeha, 2015), “Self-portrait as burning fish” (Autoportree põleva kalana, 2014), “Self-portrait as a camel” (Autoportree kaamelina, 2012), “Self-Portrait as a tortoise” (Autoportree kilpkonnana, 2018). In creating these creatures as self-portraits Ojaver uses materials that during the past 50 years have been associated primarily with women artists: everyday objects, soft fabrics, etc. In her solo show “Stripclub” (Striptiisiklubi, 2015, Vabaduse Gallery) Ojaver exhibited “Madonna”, a work depicting a figure dressed in tarp, a bitter-looking woman, who will never be free of her burden. artists.b: Sündis tisleri perekonnas, omandas üldhariduse Nõmme Linna 1. algkoolis ja Tallinna Linna Poeglaste Reaalgümnaasiumis. Kunsti õppis 1931-1937 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis (dekoratiivmaal), 1938-1941 Riigi Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis (maal). Mobiliseeriti 1941 Punaarmeesse tööpataljoni, 1944 kuulus Jaroslavli eesti kunstnike kollektiivi. Pärast II maailmasõda õppis Moskva Kunstiakadeemias. Alates 1944 oli ERKI (TKÜ, EKA) õppejõud, 1993 emeriitprofessor.  E. Okas reisis teoseid luues 1958 Hollandis, Belgias ja Luksemburgis, 1961 Itaalias, 1962 Prantsusmaal, 1963 Jaapanis.

Õppis TPI-s (TTÜ, TalTech) 1968-1970 ehitust ning 1970-st ERKI-s (EKA) arhitektuuri. On loonud performance`e, installatsioone, graafikasarju, kitsasfilme jm. Graafikas kasutab sageli fotot ja filmikaadreid.
artists.ben: Studied construction at TPI (TTÜ, TalTech) 1968-1970 and from 1970 architecture at ERKI (EKA). Has created performances, installations, print series, short films etc. In graphic art he often uses photographs and film frames.

artists.b: Eduard Ole sündis 1898 Valgamaal Karula kihelkonnas Kaagjärve vallas Saibasoo talus. Ta õppis pastor Wühneri neljaklassilises kirikukoolis ja Valga linnakoolis. Kunstihariduse sai 1914-1918 Venemaal Penza erakunstikoolis (Peterburi Kunstide Akadeemia filiaal), mille lõpetas joonistusõpetaja kutsega. Pärast Eestisse naasmist töötas alates 1919 õpetajana Rakvere Reaalgümnaasiumis ja Õpetajate Seminaris, aastast 1922 Tartu tütarlastegümnaasiumis ning kommerts- ja kaubanduskoolis ja 1924–1936 Hugo Treffneri Gümnaasiumis; aastast 1936 Tallinna Prantsuse Lütseumis. 1923 oli E. Ole avangardistliku Eesti Kunstnikkude Ryhma asutajaliige, 1927. aastast kuulus Eesti Kujutavate Kunstnikkude Keskühingusse, hiljem oli ühingu aseesimees. E. Ole väisas korduvalt Pariisi, esmakordselt 1927. aastal. 1937. aastal reisis koos Juhan Raudsepaga Inglismaal, Belgias, Prantsusmaal, Itaalias ning Kesk-Euroopas. 1943 põgenes kunstnik Eestist Soome, alates 1944 elas Rootsis Lääne-Stockholmis Vällingbys ja töötas Põhjamaade Muuseumis. 1946. aastal võttis Ole koos Eduard Wiiraltiga ette reisi Lapimaale.
grp: school:Higher Art School at the Imperial Academy of Arts
artists.ben: Eduard Ole was born in 1898 in Valga County, Karula Parish, Kaagjärve Municipality, at the Saibasoo farm. He studied at pastor Wühner's four-grade church school and at Valga town school. He received his art education in 1914–1918 in Russia at the Penza private art school (a branch of the Saint Petersburg Academy of Arts), from which he graduated with the qualification of drawing teacher. After returning to Estonia, he worked from 1919 as a teacher at Rakvere Secondary School and the Teachers' Seminary, from 1922 at the Tartu Girls' Gymnasium and the Commercial and Trade School, and from 1924–1936 at Hugo Treffner Gymnasium; from 1936 at the Tallinn French Lyceum. In 1923, E. Ole was a founding member of the avant-garde Estonian Artists' Group; from 1927 he belonged to the Estonian Central Society of Visual Artists, later serving as the society's vice-chairman. E. Ole visited Paris repeatedly, for the first time in 1927. In 1937 he travelled together with Juhan Raudsepp to England, Belgium, France, Italy and Central Europe. In 1943 the artist fled Estonia for Finland; from 1944 he lived in Sweden, in Vällingby, West Stockholm, and worked at the Nordic Museum. In 1946, Ole, together with Eduard Wiiralt, undertook a trip to Lapland.

artists.b: Sündinud 25.02.1963. Haridus: Tallinna Kunstiülikool, lõpetanud 1992.
artists.ben:
Kaido Ole (1963) is one of the most well known contemporary Estonian painters, active in art since 1989, and a long time teacher at the Estonian Academy of Arts. Ole often models for his own paintings but also creates peculiar characters, recurring in various series and compositions. Ole's work is characterised by humour and self-irony and a critical sense of the absurd, stemming from his identity as an Estonian, an Eastern European, artist, and citizen.

Kaido Ole's solo exhibition “Basic” (2001) has been said to be one of the most notable Estonian solo shows of all times by the art historian Anders Härm. The leitmotif of the show was an anonymous subject, a basic human figure bubblehead, used to denote different hierarchies of power.

Also part of Ole's work is the project John Smith, a pseudonym he worked under together with Marko Mäetamm between 2001 and 2006. In 2003 they represented Estonia at the 50th Venice Biennale with “Marko und Kaido”, a work blending autobiography and fantasy. In this compilation of paintings and installations the authors tell the story of a German gene researcher who came to the Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic in the 1960s. Through the eyes of this character the artists present a self-ironic view on the dreams and aspirations of a small country in Eastern Europe.

In his solo exhibition “Handsome Hero and Plenty of Still Lifes” (2012) in the Great Hall of Kumu Art Museum, Ole exhibited paintings with the recurring motif of a wheel balancing on abstract combinations of material, forms and surfaces, which can be interpreted as a witty comment on balance in the contemporary world. In the show “Freaks” (2014) Ole developed his trademark anonymous stick figures into all kinds of Dadaist characters, turning his previously carefully constructed mythologies upside down.

artists.b: Helgi-Maret Olvet oli 1955–1964 Moskvas ja Tallinnas kujunduskunstnik, 1974–1975 Eesti Televisiooni peakunstnik ja 1976–1977 Eesti NSV Kohaliku Tööstuse Ministeeriumi peakunstnik, 1979–1986 ERKI joonistuskateedri vanemõpetaja, seejärel oli ta vabakunstnik. Tegeles eksliibrisekunsti ja vabagraafikaga.

Kirjanik; Õppis Penuja vallas Niitsaadu vallakoolis, hiljem täiendas end iseõppijana, 1871–77 ja 1891–92 elas Pöögle-Maie külakoolis, kus vend Jaan oli õpetaja. Töötas 1872 Pöögles vallakirjutaja abilisena, aastast 1873 Pornusel ja mujal kohtukirjutajana, hiljem Karksis, Pollis ja mitmes teises Mulgimaa vallas vallakirjutajana. Pidi 1893 vene keele oskamatuse tõttu kirjutajaametist lahkuma, töötas lühikest aega Viljandi Põllumeeste Seltsi ökonoomina, aastast 1894 Daugavpilsi lähedal Kalkune mõisas piiritusevabriku raamatupidajana, aastast 1898 Riias Phoenixi vagunivabrikus osakonnajuhatajana, 1901–04 Tartus Postimehe ärijuhina ja 1904–20 Liivimaa Hüpoteegi Seltsi pangaametnikuna. Kirjanduslikku tegevust alustas 1870. aastail tõlketööga ja koduloolise raamatuga „Kodu-kurukesest” (1878).
artists.ben: Writer; He studied at the Niitsaadu parish school in Penuja parish, later continued his education as an autodidact; in 1871–77 and 1891–92 he lived at the Pöögle-Maie village school, where his brother Jaan was a teacher. In 1872 he worked in Pöögle as an assistant to the parish clerk, from 1873 in Pornuse and elsewhere as a court clerk, later in Karksi, Polli and several other Mulgimaa parishes as a parish clerk. In 1893 he had to leave the clerk's profession due to lack of knowledge of Russian, worked briefly as economist for the Viljandi Farmers' Society, from 1894 as bookkeeper at the spirits factory at Kalkune manor near Daugavpils, from 1898 as department head at the Phoenix wagon factory in Riga, 1901–04 as business manager of Postimees in Tartu, and 1904–20 as a bank official of the Livonian Mortgage Society. He began his literary activity in the 1870s with translation work and the local-history book "Kodu-kurukesest" (1878).

artists.b: Enno Ootsing (s. 1940) on Eesti kunstielus osalenud 1964. aastast alates vabagraafiku, raamatukunstniku ja akvarellistina, kuuludes Eesti kunsti uuendusliikumises olulist kohta omanud rühmitusse ANK ’64.
artists.ben: Enno Ootsing (b. 1940) has taken part in Estonian art life since 1964 as a printmaker, book artist and watercolourist, belonging to the group ANK '64, which held an important place in the innovative movement of Estonian art.

artists.b: Segatehnikas töö kujutab kunstniku lapsepõlvekodu aknaraami Pärnus Mihkli tn 18. Aplikatsioon, pastell, pliiats, foto. Paremas ülaruudus peegeldub majakatus tuulelipuga ja kontuurina joonistatud hobune vankriga, all paremas nurgast koduaknast sissevaatava kunstniku peegeldus aknaklaasil.; Asukoht: Eesti; Vabatekstiline asukoht: administratiivne üksus; Pärnu;.

Õppis Viljandis E. Heine progümnaasiumis ja 1910–1914 Riia kunstikoolis. 1922. aastal täiendas end Berliinis ja Dresdenis. Töötas joonistusõpetajana mitmes Viljandi koolis, sh. A. Kamseni erakaubanduskoolis, 1914–1919 Viljandi kõrgemas algkoolis ja 1916–1926 Viljandi Eesti Haridusseltsi tütarlastegümnaasiumis, seejärel oli Tartu "Pallase" maaliklassi õppejõud ja 1929–1940 abidirektor. Aastatel 1927, 1930 ja 1937 oli V. Ormisson kunstiühingu "Pallas" esimees. V. OrmissonLoonud peamiselt maastikke ja natüürmorte. Varaseis teostes on märgata impressionismi ja Konrad Mäe loomingu mõju. Pärast Saksamaal käimist sugenes maalidesse ekspressionistlikke jooni, koloriit tumenes ja valdavaks sai rohekassinine toon. 1920. aastate II poolel muutus maastikukäsitlus õhu- ja valguseküllasemaks. V. Ormisson suri 5. aprillil 1941. Tema viimne puhkepaik on Viljandi vanal (Riia mnt) kalmistul.
artists.ben: He studied at E. Heine's progymnasium in Viljandi and in 1910–1914 at the Riga Art School. In 1922 he furthered his studies in Berlin and Dresden. He worked as a drawing teacher in several schools in Viljandi, including A. Kamsen's private trade school, in 1914–1919 at the Viljandi Higher Primary School, and in 1916–1926 at the girls' gymnasium of the Viljandi Estonian Education Society, after which he was a lecturer in the painting class of Tartu's "Pallas" and from 1929–1940 deputy director. In 1927, 1930 and 1937 V. Ormisson was chairman of the art society "Pallas". V. Ormisson created mainly landscapes and still lifes. In his early works the influence of Impressionism and Konrad Mägi's work can be seen. After a trip to Germany, Expressionist traits appeared in his paintings, the colouring darkened and a greenish-blue tone became predominant. In the second half of the 1920s his treatment of landscape became more airy and light-filled. V. Ormisson died on 5 April 1941. His final resting place is at the old cemetery of Viljandi (Riia mnt).

artists.b: Jaan Paavle oli eesti kirjanik ja kunstnik. Paavle andis välja kuus luulekogu, neist esimene oli 1972. aastal ilmunud "Vabaarmastus". 35-aastasena astus ta Tallinna kunstiinstituuti keraamikat õppima. 1990ndatel huvitus Paavle performance-kunstist. Ta õpetas Tallinna kunstikoolis lastele performance'it ning töötas Tarbekunsti- ja Disainimuuseumis valvurina. Jaan Paavle lõi keraamikat, maalis, kirjutas luuletusi, näidendeid, filmi- ja teatrikriitikat, tegi ise mõned filmid ning mängis mitme filmi massistseenides.
artists.ben: Jaan Paavle was an Estonian writer and artist. Paavle published six poetry collections, the first of which, "Vabaarmastus", appeared in 1972. At the age of 35 he entered the Tallinn Art Institute to study ceramics. In the 1990s Paavle became interested in performance art. He taught performance to children at the Tallinn Art School and worked as a guard at the Estonian Museum of Applied Art and Design. Jaan Paavle created ceramics, painted, wrote poems, plays, film and theatre criticism, made a few films himself and appeared in mass scenes of several films.

artists.b: Juhan Paberit (1917) on loonud 1960.–1970. aastatel rahutu dünaamikaga ning emotsionaalselt mõjuvaid mälestusmärke ja hauatähiseid. Tema valdavalt reljeefidena lahendatud mälestusmärgid on äratuntavad kauni maalilise pinnatöötluse järgi. Paberit on üks esiletõusvamaid reljeefi-skulptoreid Eestis. Ta oli valdavalt Tartu-keskne kunstnik, nii on Paberiti hauaskulptuurid suures osas Tartu kalmistutel; Teises maailmasõjas langenute mälestusmärgid asuvad Lõuna-Eestis (Elvas, Õisus, Kanepis), aga ka Paides. Portreeloomingus kasutas meelsasti keraamikat – olulise osa tema loomingust moodustavadki portreed – kunstniku suhe modelli on enamasti soe ja lüüriline. Paberit oli Teises maailmasõjas mobiliseeritud punaarmeesse, alustas skulptuuriõpinguid 1946. aastal Tartu Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis ning lõpetas ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi 1952. aastal skulptorina.
artists.ben: Juhan Paberit (1917) created restless, dynamic and emotionally powerful monuments and gravestones during the 1960s–1970s. His monuments, mostly executed as reliefs, are recognisable by their beautiful painterly surface treatment. Paberit is one of the most outstanding relief sculptors in Estonia. He was predominantly a Tartu-centred artist, and thus Paberit's gravestone sculptures are largely found in Tartu's cemeteries; the monuments to those fallen in the Second World War are located in South Estonia (in Elva, Õisu, Kanepi), but also in Paide. In his portrait work he gladly used ceramics – portraits indeed form a significant part of his oeuvre – the artist's relationship to the model is usually warm and lyrical. Paberit was mobilised into the Red Army during the Second World War, began his sculpture studies in 1946 at the Tartu State Art Institute, and graduated as a sculptor from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1952.

artists.b: Tõnis Paberit on lõpetanud Eesti Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi skulptuuri eriala. Ta on töötanud õppejõuna Tartu Ülikooli kunstide osakonnas, Konrad Mäe nimelises maaliateljees, Tartu Kunstikoolis ning on praegu kaasprofessor Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis Pallas. Tema põhisuunad loomingus on psühholoogiline portree, kontseptuaalne installatsioon ja monumentaalkunst ning retrospektsioon. Viimasel kümnendil on Paberit tegelenud turba ja mulla kasutusega skulptuuris.
artists.ben: Tõnis Paberit graduated from the Estonian State Art Institute in sculpture. He has worked as a lecturer in the art department of the University of Tartu, in the Konrad Mägi painting studio, at the Tartu Art School, and is currently an associate professor at the Pallas University of Applied Sciences. His main directions in creative work are psychological portraiture, conceptual installation and monumental art, as well as retrospection. Over the last decade Paberit has been working with peat and soil in sculpture.

artists.b: Mai Levin, Pärleid ühest erakogust. Teine osa. 2006. lk 11 (galerii "Rios"): "Palmse peretütred Olga ja Maria von der Pahlenid olid kunstiandelised. Vana...talunaine Maria von der Pahleni akvarellil on nähtavasti kuulunud mõisarahva hulka; portree kõneleb karakteriseerimisoskusest ja teatud koolitusest". Anu Allikvee: "Marie (Maria) Charlotte von der Pahlen (sünd. 18. XI 1852 Tallinnas) oli Diedrich von der Pahleni (1807-1894) tütar ja kunstnik Olga von der Pahleni (1856-1919) õde. Tema surmaaasta pole teada, kuid 1930 oli ta veel elus. (1930 koostati Genealogisches Handbuch der baltischen Ritterschaften ,Teil Estland). Kuna ta oli 1930 sünniaasta järgi otsustades juba 78 aastane, peaks ta surmaaeg langema 1930-sse aastatesse või 1940. aastate algusesse. Kunstileksikonides tema nime ei mainita, küll on seal andmeid Olga kohta. Kahjuks ei ole teada, kus Maria kunsti õppis. Võimalik, et neil oli õega ühine kodune kunstiõpetaja ning hiljem võis ta saada juhendust oma õelt Olgalt. Palmse mõisaga on Maria v.d. Pahleni seos üsna kaudne. Ta pärines küll Pahlenite suguvõsa  Palmse harust, kuid mitte otse Palmse mõisast. Tema isa Diedrich oli Voore (Forell) mõisa omanik, kelle isa, kunstniku vanaisa, Peter v.d. Pahlen (1777-1828) oli samuti Voore mõisnik. Alles Peter v. d. Pahleni isa, Arend Dietrich v. d. Pahlen (1738-1778) oli sündinud Palmses Palmse mõisa omaniku lapsena. Kuid noorema pojana ta sünnimõisa ei pärinud ning temast sai Koila (Koil) mõisa omanik Virumaal".
artists.ben: Mai Levin, Pearls from a Private Collection. Part Two. 2006. p. 11 (gallery "Rios"): "The Palmse daughters Olga and Maria von der Pahlen were artistically gifted. Old...the peasant woman in Maria von der Pahlen's watercolour has apparently belonged among the manor folk; the portrait speaks of a skill in characterisation and a certain training". Anu Allikvee: "Marie (Maria) Charlotte von der Pahlen (b. 18. XI 1852 in Tallinn) was the daughter of Diedrich von der Pahlen (1807-1894) and the sister of the artist Olga von der Pahlen (1856-1919). Her year of death is not known, but in 1930 she was still alive. (In 1930 the Genealogisches Handbuch der baltischen Ritterschaften, Teil Estland was compiled). Since, judging by her year of birth, she was already 78 years old in 1930, her death should fall in the 1930s or the early 1940s. Her name is not mentioned in art dictionaries, though there is information there about Olga. Unfortunately it is not known where Maria studied art. It is possible that the sisters had a common home art teacher, and later she may have received guidance from her sister Olga. Maria v.d. Pahlen's connection with the Palmse manor is rather indirect. She did descend from the Palmse branch of the Pahlen family, but not directly from the Palmse manor. Her father Diedrich was the owner of the Voore (Forell) manor, whose father, the artist's grandfather, Peter v.d. Pahlen (1777-1828), was likewise the owner of the Voore manor. Only Peter v.d. Pahlen's father, Arend Dietrich v.d. Pahlen (1738-1778), was born in Palmse as a child of the owner of the Palmse manor. But as a younger son he did not inherit his birth manor, and he became the owner of the Koila (Koil) manor in Virumaa".

artists.b: Põgenenud Soome kaudu Rootsi, lõpetas 1947. aastal Sigtuna Eesti Gümnaasiumi ja 1951. aastal Stockholmi Kõrgema Rakenduskunstikooli. Graafika erialal täiendas 1954-1955 Oslos Norra Rahvusliku Kunstiakadeemia graafikaklassis Chrix Dahli juures.
artists.ben: Fled through Finland to Sweden, graduated in 1947 from the Sigtuna Estonian Gymnasium and in 1951 from the Stockholm Higher School of Applied Arts. In the field of graphic art, from 1954-1955 he continued his studies in Oslo in the graphic art class of the Norwegian National Academy of Art under Chrix Dahl.

artists.b: Tiiu Pallo-Vaik (1941) on maalinud peamiselt lüürilisi, maheda koloriidiga portreid.
artists.ben: Tiiu Pallo-Vaik (1941) has painted mainly lyrical portraits with a mild colouring.

artists.b: Hille Palm õppis aastatel 1957–1962 Tartu Kujutava Kunsti Koolis ja seejärel Eesti Riiklikus Kunstiinstituudis, mille lõpetas 1972. aastal. Tema looming keskendub naisekeha ja tunnete ekspressiivsele kujutamisele. Palm on osalenud rahvusvahelistel näitustel ja saanud mitmeid tunnustusi, sealhulgas Kristjan Raua nimelise preemia 1985. aastal.
artists.ben: Hille Palm studied from 1957 to 1962 at the Tartu Art School and afterwards at the Estonian State Art Institute, which she graduated from in 1972. Her work focuses on the expressive depiction of the female body and emotions. Palm has participated in international exhibitions and received several awards, including the Kristjan Raud Prize in 1985.

artists.b: Sündinud 14.04.1937, Tallinn; surnud 27.04.2002. Haridus: 1957-1963 Eesti Kunstiakadeemia, keraamika, graafika, lõpetas graafik-plakatistina.

Lembit Palm (1944) viljeles 1970. aastatel peamiselt dekoratiivskulptuuri, huvitudes nii loomingu sümboolsest väärtusest kui ka vormi väljendusrikkusest. Tema figuratsioonid ning algvormidele taandatud dekoratiivskulptuurid on lahendatud nii pronksis kui ka tinas ja kivis. Samuti on ta loonud elava modelleeringuga karakteerseid portreeskulptuure. Ta on laiendanud oma loomingulisi võimalusi valdkondadesse nagu rahvusvahelised jää- ja lumeskulptuuri sümpoosionid ja võistlused ning võtnud osa linnaskulptuuri sümpoosionidest, kus lühiajalise tööprotsessi tulemusega paigutatakse linnaruumi peamiselt dolomiidist või puust taiesed.
artists.ben: Lembit Palm (1944) mainly cultivated decorative sculpture in the 1970s, interested both in the symbolic value of the work and in the expressiveness of form. His figurations and decorative sculptures reduced to primary forms have been rendered in bronze as well as in tin and stone. He has also created character portrait sculptures with lively modelling. He has extended his creative possibilities into fields such as international ice and snow sculpture symposiums and competitions, and has taken part in urban sculpture symposiums, where works, mostly of dolomite or wood, resulting from a short working process are placed in urban space.

artists.b: Priit Pangsepp (s. 1966 in Kohtla-Järvel) on üks Kursi koolkonna rajajaid. Pangsepp lõpetas Tartu Kunstikooli 1985. a. ning alustas näitustel osalemist aasta varem, 1984. Ta on Eesti Kunstnike Liidu ja Tartu Kunsntike Liidu liige alates 1992. a.
artists.ben: Priit Pangsepp (b. 1966 in Kohtla-Järve) is one of the founders of the Kursi school. Pangsepp graduated from the Tartu Art School in 1985 and began participating in exhibitions a year earlier, in 1984. He has been a member of the Estonian Artists' Association and the Tartu Artists' Association since 1992.

artists.b: Rudolf Johannes Paris oli Eesti kunstiajaloolane, -kriitik ja graafik. Ta lõpetas 1918 Tartu Kommertskooli, õppis 1916–1919 Tartus Konrad Mäe ateljees maalimist, 1919–1922 Kõrgemas Kunstikoolis Pallas maalimist ja graafikat. 1922–1925 jätkas õpinguid Saksamaal, peamiselt Weimaris Bauhausis, kus lõpetas seinamaali osakonna. Kunstiajaloo alal õppis 1919–1921, 1927–1931 Tartu Ülikoolis ja 1931 Helsingi Ülikoolis. Kuulus 1919 Lõuna-Eesti kunstikaitsetoimkonda. Oli 1920–1922 Postimehe kunsti- ja karikatuuriosakonna juhataja, 1925–1929 Pallase maali- ja analüütilise joonistamise õppejõud, 1932–1934 "Eesti entsüklopeedia" kunstiosakonna toimetaja ja kaasautor, 1935–1940 Riikliku Propaganda Talituse nõunik, ühtlasi 1938–1939 ajakirja Varamu kunstiosakonna toimetaja. Siirdus 1941 Saksamaale, elas Freudenstadtis, kus tegutses kunstniku ja kunstikriitikuna, tegi kaastööd ajakirjadele Tulimuld ja Mana. Avaldanud mitu olulist monograafiat (E. Wiiralt, A. Vabbe)
artists.wdesc: Estonian art historian and graphical artist (1896-1973)
artists.ben: Rudolf Johannes Paris was an Estonian art historian, critic and graphic artist. He completed in 1918 the Tartu Commercial School, studied in 1916–1919 in Tartu in Konrad Mägi's studio painting, in 1919–1922 at the Higher Art School Pallas painting and graphic art. In 1922–1925 he continued his studies in Germany, mainly in Weimar at the Bauhaus, where he completed the mural painting department. In art history he studied in 1919–1921, 1927–1931 at the University of Tartu and in 1931 at the University of Helsinki. He belonged in 1919 to the South Estonian art protection committee. He was in 1920–1922 head of the art and caricature department of Postimees, in 1925–1929 lecturer in painting and analytical drawing at Pallas, in 1932–1934 editor and co-author of the art department of "Eesti entsüklopeedia", in 1935–1940 adviser at the State Propaganda Office, at the same time in 1938–1939 editor of the art department of the magazine Varamu. In 1941 he moved to Germany, lived in Freudenstadt, where he worked as an artist and art critic, contributed to the magazines Tulimuld and Mana. He published several important monographs (E. Wiiralt, A. Vabbe)

artists.b: Anne Parmasto (s. 1952) on lõpetanud Eesti NSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi 1981. a. maalikunstnikuna (teatridekoraatori lisaeriala). Alates 1999. on Parmasto maalikunsti dotsent Tartu Ülikooli kultuuriteaduste ja kunstide instituudis. Parmasto on esinenud alates 1984. aastast 35 isiknäitusega Eestis, Saksamaal ja USA-s ning osalenud enam kui 300. grupi- ja ülevaatusnäitusel Eestis, Austrias, Belgias, Luksemburgis, Leedus, Itaalias, Rootsis, Saksamaal (sh ART COLOGNE), Soomes, Türgis, USA-s, Valgevenes, Venemaal.
artists.ben: Anne Parmasto (b. 1952) graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1981 as a painter (with a supplementary specialty in theatre decoration). Since 1999 Parmasto has been an associate professor of painting at the Institute of Cultural Sciences and Arts of the University of Tartu. Since 1984 Parmasto has held 35 solo exhibitions in Estonia, Germany and the USA and has participated in more than 300 group and overview exhibitions in Estonia, Austria, Belgium, Luxembourg, Lithuania, Italy, Sweden, Germany (incl. ART COLOGNE), Finland, Turkey, the USA, Belarus, Russia.

artists.b: Illimar Paul (s. 1945) alustas graafikaõpinguid Eesti Kunstiakadeemias (ERKI) 1964. aastal. Jätkas õpinguid Leipzigi Kõrgemas Graafika- ja Raamatukunsti Koolis, mille lõpetas diplomiga 1971. aastal. Osalenud enam kui 300 ühisnäitusel nii kodu- kui ka välismaal, isikunäitusi on toimunud 68. “Illimar Pauli 1970ndate hüperrealistlikus laadis serigraafiatehnikas linnavaated ei kuulu mitte ainult meie graafika klassikasse, vaid olid omal ajal ühed novaatorlikumad graafikateosed, seda nii tehnika kui ka kujutamisviisi poolest. Paul on oma loomingus kasutanud mitmeid tehnikaid – siiditrüki kõrval teisi graafikatehnikaid (linoollõige), aga ka akvarelli, värvilist pliiatsijoonistust, neid kokku miksinud, tulnud kahemõõtmelisest esitusviisist ruumi, teinud kolmemõõtmelisi kollaaže jne., kuid armastus detaili vastu on säilinud siiani. Enamgi veel: detail on talle alati tähendanud midagi väga isiklikku ja emotsionaalset.” Reet Varblane, 2015.
artists.ben: Illimar Paul (b. 1945) began his graphic art studies at the Estonian Academy of Arts (ERKI) in 1964. He continued his studies at the Leipzig Higher School of Graphic Arts and Book Design, from which he graduated with a diploma in 1971. He has taken part in more than 300 joint exhibitions both at home and abroad, and has had 68 solo exhibitions. "Illimar Paul's townscapes made in the hyperrealistic style of the 1970s in the serigraphy technique belong not only to the classics of our graphic art, but were at the time among the most innovative works of graphic art, both in terms of technique and manner of depiction. In his work Paul has used several techniques – besides silkscreen printing, other graphic techniques (linocut), but also watercolour, coloured pencil drawing, mixing them together, moving from a two-dimensional mode of presentation into space, making three-dimensional collages, etc., but his love of detail has survived to this day. Moreover, detail has always meant something very personal and emotional to him." Reet Varblane, 2015.
