artists.b: Sündis hilisema Valga erakoolipidaja Ferdinand Zeidleri tütrena. Sai hariduse Viiburis ja Valga eragümnaasiumis, lõpueksamid sooritas 1887 Tartus.1889-94 õppis Peterburis A. Stieglitzi kunsttööstuskooli, kooli stipendiaadina Pariisis portselanimaali ja Colarossi vaba-akadeemias joonistamist. 1908 täiendas end Londonis, Stuttgardis ja Viinis metallehistöö alal. Töötas 1897-1918 Petrogradi kunstikoolides õppejõuna. Asus 1918 Tallinna. Oli 1919-40 Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis metalli-, portselani-, akvarelli- ja joonistamise õppejõud. 1924-35 oli metallitöökoja juhataja ning arendas eriti filigraantehnikat.  1919-31 oli ka Tallinna saksa poeglaste eragümnaasiumis joonistusõpetaja. Asutas oma stuudio. 1920. aastail kuulus ARS-i, 1928-35 EKKKÜ-sse, 1938-39 EAKKK-sse, osales 1932 RaKü asutamsies. Siirdus 1940 Soome, 1941 Saksamaale, 1948 Rootsi.
grp: school:Saint Petersburg Stieglitz State Academy of Art and Design
artists.ben: She was born as the daughter of Ferdinand Zeidler, later a private school proprietor in Valga. She received her education in Viiburi and at the Valga private gymnasium, and passed her final examinations in 1887 in Tartu. From 1889–94 she studied at A. Stieglitz's School of Technical Drawing in St. Petersburg, and as a stipendiary of the school studied porcelain painting in Paris and drawing at the Académie Colarossi free academy. In 1908 she furthered her studies in metalwork in London, Stuttgart and Vienna. She worked as a lecturer at art schools in Petrograd from 1897–1918. In 1918 she moved to Tallinn. From 1919–40 she was a lecturer in metalwork, porcelain, watercolour and drawing at the State School of Applied Art. From 1924–35 she was head of the metal workshop and especially developed the filigree technique. From 1919–31 she was also a drawing teacher at the Tallinn German private gymnasium for boys. She founded her own studio. In the 1920s she belonged to ARS, from 1928–35 to EKKKÜ, from 1938–39 to EAKKK, and took part in the founding of RaKü in 1932. She moved to Finland in 1940, to Germany in 1941, and to Sweden in 1948.

artists.b: (ZED) Eduard Zentsik on sündinud 26. detsembril 1975 Sillamäel, Eestis. Eduard Zentsik on viljakas ja mitmenäoline eesti kunstnik. Tal on kujunenud mitu erinevat kunstilist isiksust ning ta ei seo ennast ühegi konkreetse stiili, tehnika või teemaga. Selle asemel segab ta omavahel erinevaid meediume ja žanre ning kummutab mänguliselt traditsioone. Zentsiku looming on mitmekülgne ja mahukas. Mõned tema ettevõtmistest, näiteks mõnevõrra kõhedusttekitav art brut’ sari, keskenduvad ihu füüsilistele metamorfoosidele. Teised, näiteks sümbolistlikud sürrealistlikud maalid, rõhutavad Zentsiku filosoofia spirituaalseid aspekte. Siin-seal kasutab kunstnik Pollocklikke värvipritsmeid või katsetab digitaalsete meediumitega. Zentsiku maalid sisaldavad avatud ruumi, maagilist reaalsust, milles olemid, esemed ja mõisted näiliselt vabalt valitud ajastutest ja kultuuridest täidavad mõistatuslikke eesmärke. Mitte ükski mütoloogia ega esoteeriline õpetus pole immuunne kunstniku delikaatsete manipulatsioonide suhtes – Zentsiku töös käib Zen käsikäes Tao, Krishna, Kristuse ja Olümpose jumalatega. Tegu pole siiski intellektuaalse mänguga. Need, kes soovivad Zentsiku koodi dešifreerida, avastavad su.
artists.ben: (ZED) Eduard Zentsik was born on 26 December 1975 in Sillamäe, Estonia. Eduard Zentsik is a prolific and many-faceted Estonian artist. He has developed several different artistic personas and does not tie himself to any single style, technique or theme. Instead he mixes different media and genres and playfully overturns traditions. Zentsik's oeuvre is diverse and extensive. Some of his undertakings, for example the somewhat eerie 'art brut' series, focus on the physical metamorphoses of the flesh. Others, such as the symbolist surrealist paintings, emphasise the spiritual aspects of Zentsik's philosophy. Here and there the artist uses Pollock-like splashes of paint or experiments with digital media. Zentsik's paintings contain an open space, a magical reality in which beings, objects and concepts, seemingly freely chosen from various eras and cultures, fulfil enigmatic purposes. No mythology or esoteric teaching is immune to the artist's delicate manipulations – in Zentsik's work Zen goes hand in hand with Tao, Krishna, Christ and the gods of Olympus. Yet this is not an intellectual game. Those who wish to decipher Zentsik's code will discover su.

Jevgeni Zolotko (1983) is an artist whose work centres on the relationship between the verbal and the material. In his site specific installations Zolotko highlights the universal traits of human nature, intergenerational sensitivity passed on through culture and religion and suppressed subconscious. The artist digs deep into the past preceding our collective consciousness.

One of Zolotko's first large scale installations, “One day of the state archivist life” (2011) presents an eternal moment. The cellulose book-shaped pressed objects on shelves create a time scale that includes logs by the archivist. On the background of this static scene we can hear the whole-encompassing compositions of Bach's register. In a similar approach, a series of time-stilled moments were presented in his six-act exhibition “Things” (2012) in which Zolotko opened the attic of Tartu Art House to visitors, offering them different views on this static environment over the course of three months. Zolotko has said that he approached things and materials in that space without purpose, maintaining their incidental, neutral meaning. The only thing the artist added was a sound piece by Helena Tulve – everything else was already there.

Zolotko's solo show “Lukewarm” was based on the idea of childhood being a time of purity and openness, however, the exhibition was not autobiographical. In this installation Zolotko was interested in the idea of lukewarm as in-betweenness, neutrality and balance, and transferred these notions to a light grey tonality that has become one of the signature colours in his work.

Zolotko has mostly avoided explaining his work, as he dislikes the anchoring effect words have. He thinks that the overflowing mass of text that rules the world is a sign of the beginning of an apocalypse. The site-specific installation “It's time to take ceilings down” (2015) covered the wall of the exhibition space with a grey mass and consists of pulverised/ground-up books and newspapers, accompanied by a low-frequency pulsing sound. Also part of the work, are specks of paper under a magnifying glass that allows the viewer to look more closely.

artists.b: Ivan Zubaka on sündinud Lääne-Ukrainas ja elab ning töötab Eestis alates 1982. aastast. Ta on Eesti Kujurite Ühenduse liige alates 1993. aastast ning Eesti Kunstnike Liidu liige alates 1997. aastast. Zubaka on loonud mitmeid avaliku ruumi teoseid, sealhulgas Igor Severjanini hauatähise, „Kaduviku mehed“ Rakvere teatri juures ja teostanud Tondipoiste mälestusmärgi taastamise. Zubaka on pälvinud mitmeid preemiaid, sealhulgas Tallinna ja Rakvere linna kunstipreemiad ning Viljandi linna teenetemärgi.
artists.ben: Ivan Zubaka was born in Western Ukraine and has lived and worked in Estonia since 1982. He has been a member of the Estonian Sculptors' Association since 1993 and a member of the Estonian Artists' Association since 1997. Zubaka has created several public space works, including the gravestone of Igor Severyanin, the "Men of Vanishing" ("Kaduviku mehed") near the Rakvere Theatre, and carried out the restoration of the Tondipoisid Memorial. Zubaka has received several awards, including art prizes from the cities of Tallinn and Rakvere and the Viljandi city medal of merit.

artists.ben: Otto Friedrich von Pistholkors IV (1789–1843) was the eldest son of the manor owner of Rutikvere (1754–1831) of the same name. He married Helene von Oettingen. He lost a leg through amputation while in military service, which is why he signed his pictures with a crutch mark. Bibl.: Gert von Pistohlkors. Woldemar I Conrad von Pistholkors (1755–1801), builder of today's Tartu City Museum, and his family background from the 17th to the 21st century. – Tartu Linnamuuseumi aastaraamat 2005/11, pp. 73–93.

artists.b: Vanemad Priidu ja Maria Hõispu. Lapsepõlvekodu Pihtla v. Vanamõisa k. Saare talus.Juhtis 1915/16 Danilovisse evakueeritud gümnasistina kuulsa liuvälja rajamist.1920. a. kevadtalvel sattus Peipsi ääres salakaubaveole kaasa aitamise tõttu kohtu alla ja mõisteti sunnitööle, kuid vabastati karistusest V-sõjas üles näidatud vapruse eest ning arvati reservi. ["Sakala" 21.04.1920.]II m.-sõja algul lahkus koos abikaasa ja väikes tütrega Argentiinasse.Suri samas neeruhaiguse tagajärjel.
artists.ben: Parents Priidu and Maria Hõisp. Childhood home at the Saare farm, Vanamõisa village, Pihtla parish. In 1915/16, as a gymnasium student evacuated to Danilov, he led the construction of the famous skating rink. In the spring/winter of 1920, he was put on trial for helping with smuggling near Lake Peipsi and sentenced to forced labour, but was released from punishment for bravery shown in the War of Independence and transferred to the reserve. ["Sakala" 21.04.1920.] At the beginning of World War II, he left for Argentina together with his wife and small daughter. He died there as a result of kidney disease.

Kristina Õllek (1989) is a visual artist working in the field of photography, video and installation, with a focus on investigating contemporary visual culture and display; its materiality as well as the actual mode of mediation of the representation process. In her practice she frequently uses situations when fact and fiction, synthetic and natural, copies and the original intertwine, becoming a hybrid object/matter to obtain fresh meaning.

She’s interested in stretching the boundaries of what can we see and use from an image and space, especially now in the age of rapidly developing and highly manipulative technology. Within her recent projects she’s been more interested in the notion of new technologies and geological matter, the connectivity of the spatial and ecological circumstances, as well the components and resources that enable such technologies to create today’s environment.

Her work is often site-sensitive and analyses the location and the format of exhibition-making, questioning the display and the politics of installation from the perspective of a historical museum to an online space and future archeology.

artists.b: Ülo Õun on mõjutanud tervet põlvkonda Eesti kujureid, ehkki pole kunagi õppejõuna töötanud. Temaga tuli Eesti 1970. aastate skulptuuri midagi olemuslikult uut: senikogematu sõbralik grotesk, mis väljendus nii skulptori loodud portreedes kui ka figuraalses vabaloomingus. Üllatav oli ka kaudselt Alberto Giacometti (1901–1966) hilist loomingut meenutav vaba modelleering. Tänu Ülo Õunale muutus Eesti skulptuur tunduvalt kommunikatiivsemaks. Teda köitis värv skulptuuris, vormide voolavus ja muutlikkus. Ülo Õuna töömeetod erines oluliselt kaasaegsete Eesti skulptorite vormitaotlustest. Tema skulptuuridel puudus enamasti tol perioodil Eesti skulptuuris üldiselt oluliseks peetud natuuri järgiv modelleering ja sellest tuletatud üldistus. Õuna portreede ja figuuride voolavad vormid valgusid omatahtsi. Ta eelistas lõpliku materjalina seni vahematerjaliks peetud kipsi ja värvis oma skulptuure eredate aniliinvärvidega, mis kahjuks on oma intensiivsuse praeguseks enamasti kaotanud. Ta püüdis tuua skulptuuri kvaliteete, mida on tavaliselt peetud omaseks teatrikunstile ja muusikale. Ülo Õun lõpetas 1966. aastal ENSV Riikliku Kunstiinstituudi ja oli pärast lühikest ametitööd Eesti Loodusmuuseumi taksidermistina kogu elu vabakunstnik.
artists.ben: Ülo Õun has influenced an entire generation of Estonian sculptors, even though he never worked as a teacher. With him came something essentially new to Estonian sculpture of the 1970s: a previously unencountered, friendly grotesque, which found expression both in the portraits created by the sculptor and in figurative free creation. Also surprising was a free modelling that indirectly recalled the late work of Alberto Giacometti (1901–1966). Thanks to Ülo Õun, Estonian sculpture became considerably more communicative. He was captivated by colour in sculpture, and by the fluidity and mutability of forms. Ülo Õun's working method differed significantly from the formal aspirations of contemporary Estonian sculptors. His sculptures generally lacked the nature-following modelling and the generalisation derived from it, which was generally considered important in Estonian sculpture of that period. The flowing forms of Õun's portraits and figures spread according to their own will. As a final material he preferred plaster, which had until then been regarded as an intermediate material, and he painted his sculptures with bright aniline colours, which unfortunately have by now mostly lost their intensity. He sought to bring into sculpture qualities usually considered to belong to theatre art and music. Ülo Õun graduated from the Estonian SSR State Art Institute in 1966 and, after briefly working as a taxidermist at the Estonian Museum of Natural History, was a freelance artist for the rest of his life.

artists.b: Alates 1963.a. töötas Georgi kudumisvabrikus, alates 1968.a. töökoja juhataja Viimistlusvabrikus. Üliliidulise konkursi ajalehe "Izvestia" laureaat, üleliidulise rahvamajandussaavutuste näituse pronks- ja kuldmedal, Läti NSV I järgi diplom puuvillaste kangaste kõrge kunstilise kujundamise eest baltivabariikide näitusel, osalenud vabariiklikel, üleliidulistel ja rahvusvahelistel näitustel.
artists.ben: From 1963 he worked at the Georgi knitting factory, from 1968 as head of workshop at the Finishing Factory. Laureate of the all-Union competition of the newspaper "Izvestia", bronze and gold medal of the all-Union exhibition of national economic achievements, first-degree diploma of the Latvian SSR for high artistic design of cotton fabrics at the exhibition of the Baltic republics, participated in republican, all-Union and international exhibitions.

artists.b: 1870 oli "Peredvižnikute" ühingu asutajaliige. Samal aastal astus vene akvarellistide ühingusse. Osales akadeemia näitustel, ülevenemaalisel näitusel Moskvas 1882 ja Pariisi maailmanäitusel 1867 ja 1878 ja Viinis 1873. Maalis asjalik-kaines laadis põhjavene metsi. Tema stiil baseerub analüütilisele loodusvaatlusele ning erakorselt täpsele ja naturalistlikule, võiks öelda lausa fotograafiat jäljendavale joonistusele. Jälgides tähelepanelikult iga detaili - olgu see siis lilleke või puuoks, ei kaota ta kunagi silmist tervikut. Esimene ofort pärineb 1853, kaks järgmist - 1864, 1870- 92 lõi 97 oforti, 1861-70 ka 22 litot.
artists.ben: In 1870 was a founding member of the "Peredvizhniki" society. In the same year joined the Society of Russian Watercolourists. Took part in the academy's exhibitions, in the All-Russian exhibition in Moscow in 1882 and in the Paris World Exhibitions of 1867 and 1878 and in Vienna in 1873. Painted north Russian forests in a matter-of-fact, sober manner. His style is based on analytical observation of nature and on exceptionally precise and naturalistic drawing, one could even say imitating photography. Carefully observing every detail - be it a flower or a tree branch - he never loses sight of the whole. His first etching dates from 1853, the next two - 1864, in 1870-92 he created 97 etchings, in 1861-70 also 22 lithographs.

Bita Razavi (1983) is a multidisciplinary artist whose practice is centered around observations on everyday situations and bringing the personal to the public sphere. She sheds light on the inner workings of social systems in relation to the political structures of various countries. She reacts to, and explores, the agency of the objects and the systems as they act upon her, and as she documents and records them.

(2011) at the Finnish Academy of Fine Arts, she carried out an artistic ceremony, in which she married the artist Jaakko Karhunen in reaction to worsened immigration policies, the rise of a populist right wing party and their introduction of lowering the funds for contemporary art. The project ended in 2017 with a public divorce ceremony. In 2020  Museum of Contemporary Art Kiasma obtained both works in the form of video installations and personal valuables in their collection.

Because of her experience of living in Iran, Estonia and Finland, Razavi is well equipped to reflect on the relationships of these cultures and on the perception of her heritage in the Western world. For instance, Razavi’s work “Pictures from Our Future, Pictures from Our Past” (2018) started from a situation on the street in Tartu where a young man said Razavi was a “picture of the future of Estonia”. In the series of photographs, we see Razavi embodying the average Estonian woman in various everyday roles. It also features photographs of empty country houses that have been abandoned, while dropping hints towards the radical social changes connected with the refugee crisis and urbanisation processes, but also the memory of the violent deportations in Estonia’s past.

Alongside her autofictional works, the installation “The Dog Days Will Be Over Soon” (2019) combining ready-made images from videogames and objects like PC hardware together with live moss and other plans, she points towards both the merging of artificial and natural materials, and the growing distance between humans and wild nature.
artists.wdesc: Iranian artist residing in Finland and Estonia (born 1983)

artists.b: Fred Kotkas (1986) on Eesti Kunstiakadeemia lõpetanud maalikunstnik ja illustraator, kelle introspektiivne looming keskendub inimese sisemaailmale ja seda kujundavatele teguritele. Tema väljenduslaad on kirev ja kujundlik ning seda saadab eneseirooniline hoiak, mis lisab tema töödele teatava mängulisuse.
artists.ben: Fred Kotkas (1986) is a painter and illustrator who graduated from the Estonian Academy of Arts, whose introspective work focuses on the inner world of the human being and the factors shaping it. His mode of expression is vivid and figurative, accompanied by a self-ironic attitude, which adds a certain playfulness to his works.

artists.b: Eetu Sihvonen (born 1994) will receive his BFA in sculpture at the Academy of Fine Arts, Helsinki by the end of 2019. Previously Sihvonen has studied in Aalto University, department of graphic design. His works have previously been shown in several group exhibitions in Finland.

artists.b: Elina Vitola (s. 1986) on noor Läti kunstnik, kes tutvustab end järgmiselt: “Maalimist olen lustlikult õppinud peaaegu kogu oma elu ning 2018. a. lõpetan oma magistriõpinguid Läti Kunstiakadeemias. Näitused, millest mul on olnud suurim rõõm osa võtta, on näiteks “Uue Ida lapsed” Tallinna Kunstihoones ja “Vaatamis- ja lugemistuba” Kogo galeriis Tartus. Hiljuti olen teinud mitmeid abstraktseid maale, kuid lähimas tulevikus plaanin maalida pastat.”.
artists.ben: Elina Vitola (b. 1986) is a young Latvian artist who introduces herself as follows: "I have been joyfully learning to paint for almost my entire life, and in 2018 I will complete my master's studies at the Art Academy of Latvia. The exhibitions I have had the greatest pleasure of taking part in are, for example, "Children of the New East" at the Tallinn Art Hall and "Viewing and Reading Room" at Kogo Gallery in Tartu. Recently I have made several abstract paintings, but in the near future I am planning to paint pasta."

artists.b: Tiina Sarapu on klaasikunstnik, kelle loomingus klaas on peamiselt installatsiooni- ja skulptuurimaterjal, ideetasandil aga vaheaste nähtava ja nähtamatu maailma vahel. Sageli on tema tööde lähtematerjaliks lehtklaas, millest pealtnäha lihtsa painutuse abil on saanud ruumiline vorm. Servad ja pinnad on neis ühtaegu iseseisvad, samas üksteisest sõltuvad elemendid ja moodustavad tänu klaasi läbipaistvusele keeruka mitmekihilisuse. Ruumilised klaasikihid on Sarapu teostes sageli aja kihtide tähenduses. Tiina Sarapu on õppinud Eesti Kunstiakadeemia klaasikunsti osakonnas, mille lõpetas 1996. aastal magistrikraadiga. Sellest ajast on ta olnud samas osakonnas õppejõuks, alates 2003. aastast dotsent. Ta on osalenud paljudel näitustel, sümpoosionidel ja workshopides nii kodu- kui välismaal. Tema teoseid on muuseumide ja erakogujate kollektsioonides. Sarapule on omistatud aunimetus “Tunnustatud klaasikunstnik 2004–2005” ja Kristjan Raua preemia 2007. Ta on pälvinud tunnustust mitmetel rahvusvahelistel klaasikunsti konkurssidel. (M. Bukovec)
artists.ben: Tiina Sarapu is a glass artist in whose work glass is primarily an installation and sculptural material, but on the level of ideas an intermediate stage between the visible and invisible world. Sheet glass is often the starting material for her works, from which, by means of a seemingly simple bending, a three-dimensional form has been created. The edges and surfaces in these are at once independent yet interdependent elements, and thanks to the transparency of the glass they form a complex multi-layeredness. The spatial layers of glass in Sarapu's works often carry the meaning of layers of time. Tiina Sarapu studied in the Department of Glass Art at the Estonian Academy of Arts, from which she graduated with a master's degree in 1996. Since that time she has taught in the same department, and has been a docent there since 2003. She has taken part in numerous exhibitions, symposia and workshops both at home and abroad. Her works are held in the collections of museums and private collectors. Sarapu has been awarded the honorary title "Tunnustatud klaasikunstnik 2004–2005" ("Recognised Glass Artist 2004–2005") and the Kristjan Raud Prize in 2007. She has received recognition at several international glass art competitions. (M. Bukovec)

artists.b: Madlen Hirtentreu (1993) on multidistsiplinaarne kunstnik, kelle looming hõlmab skulptuuri ja kohaspetsiifilisi installatsioone. Tal on omandanud bakalaureusekraadi Milano Disainiinstituudis (Instituto Europeo di Design’is) visuaalse kommunikatsiooni erialal ning magistrikraadi Eesti Kunstiakadeemias skulptuuris ja installatsioonikunstis. Hirtentreu loomingu jõukeskmeks on mälestused, ajalugu ja materiaalsuse uurimine, mille abil ta hajutab piire arheoloogia, spekulatiivse fiktsiooni ja tööstusesteetika vahel. Need skulptuurid ja installatsioonid võivad olla nii ajaloolised väljakaevamised kui ka oletuslikud tulevikunägemused. Tema tööd viitavad sageli puudumisele või kadunud kohalolule. Teostes kohtab tihti kummituslikke, hübriidseid ja fragmentaarseid kehi või mahajäetud struktuure, mis toovad esile tunde, et midagi on kunagi olemas olnud, kuid ei eksisteeri enam täielikult. Hirtentreu pakub alternatiivset vaadet ajaloole, nähes seda mitte kui fikseeritud minevikku, vaid kui pidevas tõlgendamises olevat protsessi. Ta käsitleb objekte ja materjale kui tundmatu tuleviku fossiile.
artists.ben: Madlen Hirtentreu (1993) is a multidisciplinary artist whose work encompasses sculpture and site-specific installations. She has earned a bachelor's degree in visual communication from the Istituto Europeo di Design in Milan and a master's degree in sculpture and installation art from the Estonian Academy of Arts. The driving force of Hirtentreu's work is memory, history and the exploration of materiality, through which she blurs the boundaries between archaeology, speculative fiction and industrial aesthetics. These sculptures and installations can be both historical excavations and speculative visions of the future. Her works often refer to absence or a lost presence. In her works one frequently encounters ghostly, hybrid and fragmentary bodies or abandoned structures, which evoke the feeling that something once existed but no longer exists fully. Hirtentreu offers an alternative view of history, seeing it not as a fixed past but as a process in constant interpretation. She treats objects and materials as fossils of an unknown future.

artists.b: Agate Tūna is a multidisciplinary artist from Riga, Latvia, specialising in the field of analogue and experimental photography. Her techniques include film soups, chemigrams, and photograms along with experiments in sound art. With her camera, Tūna plays the role as an investigator between reality and fiction, uncovering intriguing strangeness and compelling evidence, stimulating discussions about the blurred boundary between these two domains. Tūna delves deep into the influential role of imagery in shaping our beliefs by examining the complex, evolving interplay between technology and spirituality. Tūna’s educational background includes a BA degree in Arts from the Painting department at the Art Academy of Latvia, earned in 2020. In 2022, a two-year programme in Developing Photographic Language at ISSP School and more recently, in 2023, she graduated from an interdisciplinary MA programme POST at the Art Academy of Latvia. Tūna has participated in numerous exhibitions and art projects both in Latvia and internationally. Her solo-show, “The Order of Invisible Things,” took place at gallery DOM in Riga in 2022. She has also been part of group exhibitions such as ”
