works.d: Villem Reimann (portreemaal), 1954. 1/2 portreemaal eesti heliloojast ja muusikapedagoogist Villem Reimannist (1906 – 1992), kes istumas suure kirjutuslaua taga. Randeli kujutuslaad on psühholoogilis-realistlik – Reimann teeb mõtliku, pisut väsinud ilmega kirjatööd, tema ees suitseb tuhatoosis poolik sigarett ning taga paistab klaver. Ajastumärgiks on teenetemärk, mille toon ühtib laua iluliistuga, Reimanni rinnas. Maali koloriidis domineerivad soojad rohekaskollased ja pruunid toonid. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Villem Reimann (portrait painting), 1954. A 1/2 portrait painting of Estonian composer and music pedagogue Villem Reimann (1906 – 1992), sitting behind a large writing desk. Randel's mode of depiction is psychological-realistic – Reimann is engaged in writing with a thoughtful, somewhat tired expression, in front of him a half-smoked cigarette smoulders in an ashtray, and a piano can be seen behind him. A sign of the era is the medal of merit, whose tone matches the decorative moulding of the desk, on Reimann's chest. Warm greenish-yellow and brown tones dominate the colouring of the painting. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Eduard Oja (portreemaal), 1948. Omanäolise eesti helilooja, koorijuhi, muusikapedagoogi ja -kriitiku Eduard Oja (1905 – 1950) portreemaal on justkui tema loomingu kaalukaima osa, soololaulude peegeldus, mis on pea kõik äärmuseni dramaatilised ja valulikud. Sigaret käes, noodipaber ees lamab Oja voodis. Tema näost peegeldub eluraskus ning tervislikud probleemid, mis pärast II maailmasõda ainult süvenesid. Peamiselt saržikunstnikuna tuntud Randel on antud maali puhul kasutanud küll mõningaid karikatuurile omaseid võtteid, kuid teose üldtonaalsuses puudub eelnimetatud žanrile omane pila. Oja portree on ilmselt üks huvitavamaid ning mitmekihilisemaid ETMM-i maalikogusse kuuluvaid portreid. /teks
works.de: Eduard Oja (portrait painting), 1948. The portrait painting of the distinctive Estonian composer, choir conductor, music educator and critic Eduard Oja (1905 – 1950) is, as it were, a reflection of the most weighty part of his work, his solo songs, almost all of which are dramatic and painful to an extreme degree. Cigarette in hand, sheet music before him, Oja lies in bed. His face reflects the hardships of life and health problems, which only deepened after the Second World War. Randel, known mainly as a caricaturist, has in this painting used some devices characteristic of caricature, yet the overall tonality of the work lacks the mockery typical of that genre. Oja's portrait is probably one of the more interesting and multi-layered portraits belonging to the ETMM's painting collection. /text

works.d: Raimund Kull (portreemaal), dateerimata. 1/2 portree eesti heliloojast, dirigendist ja puhkpillimängijast Raimund Kullist (1882 – 1942) orkestrit juhatamas. Kulli ees dirigendipuldil lebab paks noodiraamat, mis lubab arvata, et ettekandmisel on täispikk kontsert. Kuna maali täpne dateering pole teada, siis võib orkestri näol tegemist olla nii Eesti mereväeorkestri kui ka Riigi Ringhäälingu sümfooniaorkestriga, mida mõlemaid Kull erinevatel ajaperioodidel juhendas. Maali koloriit on tume, kunstniku pintslilöök hoogne. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Raimund Kull (portrait painting), undated. A 1/2 portrait of the Estonian composer, conductor and wind-instrument player Raimund Kull (1882 – 1942) conducting an orchestra. In front of Kull, on the conductor's stand, lies a thick score book, suggesting that a full-length concert is being performed. Since the exact dating of the painting is not known, the orchestra depicted could be either the Estonian Navy Orchestra or the State Broadcasting Symphony Orchestra, both of which Kull directed at different periods. The painting's colour scheme is dark, and the artist's brushstroke is vigorous. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.de: In the lower part of the picture, a man's head, with a black bow tie at the neck. Black-framed glasses, double chin. The man holds up 2 hands with flowers, and among them also a naked woman with long hair.

works.d: Pildi vasakul poolel täispikkuses paksem mees, otsevaates, hoides käes püstolit, mis on suunatud paremale. Mees seisab puu all, mille otsast kukub lind alla, teispool puud on hirv. Mehe juurde on kirjutatud Artur Rinne, looma juurde: hirv, linnu juurde: kägu, püssi juurde: küti kuul ja joonistatud on käelaba.
works.de: On the left side of the picture a full-length, stouter man, in frontal view, holding a pistol aimed to the right. The man stands under a tree, from the top of which a bird is falling, on the other side of the tree there is a deer. Written next to the man: Artur Rinne, next to the animal: hirv [deer], next to the bird: kägu [cuckoo], next to the gun: küti kuul [hunter's bullet], and a hand is drawn.

works.de: The picture shows two men. The larger one is in costume, a cape over his shoulder, a sword at his belt. He has a full face, wearing glasses. On his right arm he holds a small man in a black suit and black bow tie. Both men's faces show laughter.

works.de: Bust portrait of a middle-aged man (bare-chested), his right hand raised, fist clenched and flexing a muscle. The man with black eyebrows, black hair, a white bow tie at the neck. On the muscle, a kiss mark.

works.de: The head of a young man with an elongated face and a grim gaze, together with two raised hands. The man has long black hair, a black robe.

works.d: Rahvariides sarvepuhuja (figuur), 1947. Mulgi kuues sarvepuhuja, kelle tagant paistavad teised rahvariietes laulupeolised ning punalippudega ehitud lauluväljak, mis on kui ajastu märk, sest alates 1947. aasta XII laulupeost, toimusid pidustused kommunistliku partei ja valitsuse range kontrolli all. Kusjuures, samal aastal tuli esmakordselt laulupidude ajaloos ettekandele Gustav Ernesaksa „Mu isamaa on minu arm“. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Horn blower in national costume (figure), 1947. A horn blower in Mulgi costume, behind whom other song festival participants in national costumes can be seen, as well as the Song Festival Grounds decorated with red flags, which serves as a sign of the era, since from the 1947 12th Song Festival onward, the festivities took place under the strict control of the Communist Party and government. Notably, that same year, for the first time in the history of the Song Festivals, Gustav Ernesaks's "Mu isamaa on minu arm" was performed. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d:
Alläärest paberi keskpaigani ulatub vanema mehe poolpöördes peafiguur. Mehe näol pikki hambaid paljastav irve. Suurel ninal paksud sarvraamidega kandilised prillid, mille kohal tihedad puhmaskulmud. Juuksepiir tugevasti taandunud. Otsmikul kortsud. Juuksed langevad kohevate lainetena kuklale.
Mehe kohal lamaskleb kelmikalt poolpaljas õhulisse salli mähkinud noor naine. Suure laiaservalise kübara alt näha vaid üks pikkade ripsmetega suletud silm, ninaaugud ja täidlased huuled. Pead kannab pikaks venitatud kael. Kaelas pärlid. Üks tikkkontsades jalgadest sirutatud alla, mehe pea poole, teine ülesse õhku. Üks kätest osutab sõrmega mehe peallaele, teine hoiab käes linti kirjaga: "8. jaanuar 1986
works.de:
A half-turned head-and-shoulders figure of an older man extends from the bottom edge of the paper to the middle of the sheet. On the man's face is a grin baring long teeth. On his large nose are thick, square, horn-rimmed glasses, above which are bushy eyebrows. His hairline is heavily receded. There are wrinkles on his forehead. His hair falls onto the nape of his neck in loose waves.
Above the man reclines, roguishly, a young woman, half-nude, wrapped in an airy scarf. Under her large wide-brimmed hat only one closed eye with long lashes, the nostrils and full lips are visible. Her head is borne on an elongated neck. On her neck are pearls. One of her feet, in spike heels, stretches downward, toward the man's head, the other upward into the air. One of her hands points a finger to the top of the man's head, the other holds a ribbon with the inscription: "8 January 1986

works.de: Mart Saar (portrait painting), 1918. The 3/4 realistic portrait painting of the composer, organist and founder of the national style of Estonian choral music, Mart Saar (1882 – 1963), is very modern and strikingly influenced by Western European art. The painting is enlivened by well-preserved, bright colour tones. Saar's facial expression and pose are psychologically finely worked out — this is not, so to speak, an official ceremonial portrait. Especially expressive are the sitter's large brown eyes, the wrinkle between his brows, his upturned moustache, and his arms crossed on his chest. An interesting nuance is added to the painting by the modern, brightly toned wallpaper pattern at the bottom edge of the painting. works.d: Anne Vabarna Setu rahvariietes (portreemaal), 1934. 1/3 portree 20. sajandi tuntuimast ja olulisimast Setu lauluemast Anne Vabarnast (1877 – 1964), kelle loomingu ja isiku vastu hakkasid folkloorikogujad ja haritlased huvi tundma 1920. aastate keskpaigas. Pulst on Vabarnat kujutanud vanaldase setu rahvarõivastes ja hiiglasliku rinnasõlega naisena, kelle isiksus jääb maalil pigem suletuks. Maali koloriidis domineerivad soojad tuhmid toonid, mis loovad mulje talumaja atmosfäärist. /tekst Liisi Aibel/
works.de: Anne Vabarna in Setu Folk Costume (portrait painting), 1934. A 1/3 portrait of the 20th century's most famous and important Setu song mother Anne Vabarna (1877 – 1964), whose creative work and personality began to attract the interest of folklore collectors and scholars in the mid-1920s. Pulst has depicted Vabarna as an elderly woman in Setu folk costume with an enormous chest brooch, whose personality remains rather closed off in the painting. Warm, muted tones dominate the colouring of the painting, creating an impression of the atmosphere of a farmhouse. /text by Liisi Aibel/

works.d: Adolf Vedro (portreemaal), 1936. Eesti helilooja ja Tallinna konservatooriumi muusikateoreetiliste ainete ning kontrabassiõppejõu Adolf Vedro (1890 – 1944) 1/2 portree on helgetes toonides, ajastu vaim peegeldub moonutatud perspektiivist ning laiast hajutatud pintslilöögist. Vedrot kujutatakse töösituatsioonis ehk süvenenult komponeerimas (umbes sel ajal valmis Vedrol näiteks võidupüha müsteerium „Jaani tulemine“ ühendkoorile ja sümfooniaorkestrile). /tekst Liisi Aibel/
works.de: Adolf Vedro (portrait painting), 1936. The 1/2 portrait of the Estonian composer and teacher of music-theoretical subjects and double bass at the Tallinn Conservatory, Adolf Vedro (1890 – 1944), is in bright tones, the spirit of the era reflected in the distorted perspective and broad, diffuse brushwork. Vedro is depicted in a working situation, that is, absorbed in composing (around this time, for example, Vedro completed the Victory Day mystery play "Jaani tulemine" for combined choir and symphony orchestra). /text Liisi Aibel/

works.d:
Adolf Vedro (portreemaal), dateerimata. 
Väikeseformaadiline realistlik 1/4 portreemaal eesti heliloojast ja Tallinna Konservatooriumi muusikateoreetiliste ainete ning kontrabassiõppejõust Adolf Vedrost (1890 – 1944) on puhaste vormidega ning väga viimistletud. Vedro ümmarguste prillide tagant paistev pilk on rahulik, kuid sisendusjõuline, väärikust loovad tema seljas olev frakk ning sirgeselgne poos. Maali tume koloriit tõstab Vedro heledates toonides ilmeka näo hästi esile. Tausta kujutamisel on kunstnik kasutanud geomeetrilisi vorme. 
Maal tagaküljel on portree Liina Reimanist.
works.de:
Adolf Vedro (portrait painting), undated.
A small-format realistic 1/4 portrait of Estonian composer and Tallinn Conservatory instructor of music theory subjects and double bass Adolf Vedro (1890 – 1944) is executed with clean forms and is very refined. The gaze visible behind Vedro's round glasses is calm yet compelling; dignity is created by the tailcoat he is wearing and his upright posture. The dark colouring of the painting brings out well Vedro's expressive face in light tones. In depicting the background, the artist has used geometric forms.
On the back of the painting is a portrait of Liina Reiman.

works.de:
Eduard Vedler in the role of Avdei Spiridonovich Mukoseyev in the production "Wedding with a Dowry" (character portrait), 1952. This is a character portrait of Eduard Vedler (1896 – 1975), an actor of the Tartu Workers' Theatre and the later Vanemuine Theatre, in the role of the collective farm brigade leader Mukoseyev in the Vanemuine Theatre's production "Pulmad kaasavaraga" ("Wedding with a Dowry"; author N. M. Dyakonov, directors Benno Mikkel and Enn Parve), which premiered in 1951. Vedler is depicted in Russian folk costume, surrounded by props, which presumably characterise his role in this production. The painting is made lifelike by the skilfully painted shadows and the stripe visible on Vedler's forehead, which apparently hints that a bald-headed wig was used for the actor's makeup.

works.d: August Kitzberg (portreemaal), 1946. Eesti kunstiväärtusliku draamakirjanduse rajaja August Kitzbergi (1855 – 1927) postuumselt maalitud portree kujutab kirjanikku kui vanemas eas väärikat härrasmeest. Kitzberg suunab vaatajatele läbitungiva pilgu jättes näoilme samal ajal suurte vuntside ja habemega varjatuks. Kui portreteeritava nägu on üpris realistlik ja detailitäpne, siis kiirete pintslilöökidega visandatud taust ja figuur on hajusamad ning intensiivsemad, tõmmates tähelepanu Kitzbergi näolt eemale ning muutes maali tuumani jõudmise keeruliseks. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: August Kitzberg (portrait painting), 1946. The posthumously painted portrait of August Kitzberg (1855 – 1927), founder of Estonian dramatic literature of artistic value, depicts the writer as a dignified gentleman in his older years. Kitzberg directs a penetrating gaze at the viewer, while his facial expression is at the same time concealed by his large moustache and beard. Whereas the sitter's face is quite realistic and precise in detail, the background and figure, sketched with quick brushstrokes, are more diffuse and intense, drawing attention away from Kitzberg's face and making it difficult to reach the core of the painting. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Liina Reiman (portreemaal), dateerimata. Eesti näitlejanna ja teatripedagoogi Liina Reimani (1891 – 1961) portreemaal on valminud ilmselt 1920. ja 1930. aastakümnete vahetusel, ajal mil Leps õppis Nikolai Triigi käe all Pallase kunstikoolis või siis vahetult pärast õpingute lõppu. Sellisele ajamäärangule vihjab maali tagaküljel olev püssiga meesakt, mis on valminud Lepsi koolitööna. Reiman oli samal ajal, 1925 – 1933, Vanemuise teatri näitleja. Portree on stiliseeritud, kergelt nurgelist vormide ja pastelse koloriidiga. Reiman hoiab süles puuviljakorvi ning kannab õlgadel moodsa mustriga salli. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Liina Reiman (portrait painting), undated. The portrait painting of Estonian actress and theatre pedagogue Liina Reiman (1891 – 1961) was likely completed at the turn of the 1920s and 1930s, at the time when Leps was studying under Nikolai Triik at the Pallas art school, or immediately after finishing his studies. Such a dating is suggested by a male nude with a rifle on the back of the painting, which was created as Leps' school work. At that time, 1925 – 1933, Reiman was an actress at the Vanemuine theatre. The portrait is stylised, with slightly angular forms and pastel colouring. Reiman holds a basket of fruit in her lap and wears a shawl with a modern pattern on her shoulders. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Gustav Laanekõrb (portreemaal), 1930. aastad. Estonia teatrimaja osaühisuse juhatuse esimehe Gustav Laanekõrbi portree mõjub suursuguselt, üsna suure tõenäosusega on see maalitud esindusportreeks. Laanekõrb istub kaunilt nikerdatud juugendstiilis toolil, taamal paistavad tooliga sarnaselt stiliseeritud kulissid. Maali laad on akadeemiline, jõuline ning täpne. /tekst Liisi Aibel/
works.de: Gustav Laanekõrb (portrait painting), 1930s. The portrait of Gustav Laanekõrb, chairman of the board of the Estonia Theatre House joint-stock company, has a grand effect, and it was quite probably painted as a representative portrait. Laanekõrb sits on a beautifully carved Art Nouveau-style chair, with similarly stylised stage wings visible in the background, matching the chair. The style of the painting is academic, vigorous and precise. /text Liisi Aibel/

works.d: Evald Aav (portreemaal), 1935. Ahase 1/3 pastellportree eesti heliloojast ja koorijuhist, esimese eesti rahvusliku ooperi „Vikerlased“ (1928) loojast Evald Aavast (1900 – 1939) on tagasihoidlikus hillitsetud laadis. Aava on kujutatud realistlikult ning ilma kunstipäraste liialdusteta – nii nagu ta on. Maali hele koloriit ning see, et kunstnik on kasutanud peamiselt nii-öelda mahakeeratud toone, lisab portreele teatava romantilise mõõtme. /tekst Liisi Aibel/
works.de: Evald Aav (portrait painting), 1935. Ahas's 1/3 pastel portrait of the Estonian composer and choir conductor, creator of the first Estonian national opera "Vikerlased" (1928), Evald Aav (1900 – 1939), is in a modest, restrained manner. Aav is depicted realistically and without artistic exaggeration – as he is. The bright coloring of the painting, and the fact that the artist has mainly used so-called subdued tones, adds a certain romantic dimension to the portrait. /text Liisi Aibel/

works.d: Ida Aav-Loo (al. 1937 Loo-Talvari) (portreemaal), 1939. Stiliseeritud romantilises laadis pastellportree Estonia ooperisolistist (koloratuursopran) Ida Aav-Loost (1901 – 1997) kujutab küpset ning eesmärgikindlat EW-aegset euroopalikku ideaalnaist, kelle naiselikkust rõhutavad pehmed vormid ning unistavalt kaugusesse suunatud pilk. Maali koloriit on mahedates, pisut hajutatud toonides. Tausta puhul on kunstnik Ahas kasutanud sama tooni, mida portreteeritava silmade puhul. Aav-Loo oli oma hiilgeajal, 1930. aastatel oodatud esineja nii Läti, Leedu, Soome kui ka Rootsi ooperilavadel, pärast emigreerumist 1944. aastal jätkas ta lauljakarjääri USA-s, Kanadas ning Austraalias. /tekst Liisi Aibel/
works.de: Ida Aav-Loo (from 1937 Loo-Talvari) (portrait painting), 1939. A stylized, romantic-style pastel portrait of Estonia opera soloist (coloratura soprano) Ida Aav-Loo (1901 – 1997), depicting a mature and purposeful European ideal woman of the era of the Republic of Estonia, whose femininity is emphasized by soft forms and a dreamily distant gaze. The colouring of the painting is in mild, somewhat diffused tones. For the background, the artist Ahas has used the same tone as for the sitter's eyes. Aav-Loo was, in her heyday in the 1930s, a sought-after performer on the opera stages of Latvia, Lithuania, Finland and Sweden; after emigrating in 1944 she continued her singing career in the USA, Canada and Australia. /text Liisi Aibel/

works.d: Raimund Kull (portreemaal), 1910ndad või 1920ndad aastad. 1/3 portreemaal silmapaistvast eesti dirigendist, heliloojast ja puhkpillimängijast Raimund Kullist (1882 – 1942) kujutab teda nooremapoolse keskealise mehena, kelle ametile vihjavad seljas olev must frakk ning hoogsalt seotud valge kaelaside. Maali valmimise ajal töötas Kull dirigendina Estonia teatris, olles samas ka Estonia muusikajuht. Maali taust, mille maalimisel on kasutatud laia pintslilööki ning selgeid värviüleminekuid, lisab portreele pisut rahvusromantilise mõõtme. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Raimund Kull (portrait painting), 1910s or 1920s. A 1/3 portrait painting of the outstanding Estonian conductor, composer and wind instrument player Raimund Kull (1882 – 1942) depicts him as a younger middle-aged man, whose profession is hinted at by the black tailcoat he is wearing and the vigorously tied white necktie. At the time the painting was made, Kull worked as a conductor at the Estonia theatre, while also being Estonia's music director. The background of the painting, in the painting of which a broad brushstroke and clear colour transitions have been used, adds to the portrait a slightly national-romantic dimension. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.dm: kõrgus: 136.0 cm; laius: 90.0 cm; kõrgus: 152.0 cm; laius: 105.0 cm
works.d: Evi Rauer Ljubov Jarovaja rollis K. Trenjovi "Ljubov Jarovajas" (karakterportree), 1954. Karakterportree Draamateatri näitlejannast Evi Rauerist (1915 – 2004) K. Trenjovi „Ljubov Jarovaja“ nimirollis. Realistlikus laadis portree erineb üsna oluliselt laadist, mille järgi kunstiajalugu Ilmar Malinit hilisemal ajal tunneb. Ilmselt on suureformaadiline portree valminud kooli (lõpu)tööna ajal, mil Malin õppis ERKI-s. Kunstnik kujutab Rauerit laval. Tema taga paistavad lavakujunduse osaks olnud puu, istepink ning kaks kaastegelast – meremehesärgis mees ning kaunilt ehitud kübaraga naisterahvas. Raueri Ljubov Jarovaja näoilme, mida valgustab akside vahelt prožektor, on uhke ja eneseteadlik. Maali
works.de: Evi Rauer in the role of Ljubov Yarovaya in K. Trenyov's "Ljubov Yarovaya" (character portrait), 1954. Character portrait of the Drama Theatre actress Evi Rauer (1915 – 2004) in the title role of K. Trenyov's "Ljubov Yarovaya". The portrait, in a realistic style, differs quite considerably from the style by which art history knows Ilmar Malin from a later period. The large-format portrait was apparently created as a (final) school work during the time when Malin was studying at ERKI. The artist depicts Rauer on stage. Behind her are visible a tree, a bench and two fellow characters that were part of the stage design – a man in a sailor's shirt and a woman beautifully adorned with a hat. Rauer's facial expression as Ljubov Yarovaya, lit by a spotlight coming through the wings, is proud and self-assured. The painting

works.t: Voldemar Haas, Fritz Matt, Albert Vahtramäe
works.d: Teatrikunstnikud (grupiportree), 1958. Grupiportree eesti teatrikunstnikest (maalil vasakult paremale) Fritz Mattist (1909 – 1992), Albert Vahtramäest (1885 – 1965) ja Voldemar Haasist (1898 – 1982), kujutab kunstnike teatri maalisaalis dekoratsioonikavandite osas nõu pidamas. Tagataustal paistavad kaks maalisaali töötajat, kes kõnealust dekoratsiooni värvivad. Ilmselt on tegu fiktsionaalse olukorraga, sest tegelikus elus Matt, Vahtramäe ja Haas ühtegi lavakujundust koos ei loonud. Lisaks töötasid nad maali valmimise ajal erinevates teatrites. Maali koloriidis domineerivad pruunid toonid, värvilaiguks on värvipottidest paistvad erksad dekoratsioonivärvid. Maali laadis on tuntavad vene realis
works.de: Theatre Artists (group portrait), 1958. This group portrait of the Estonian theatre artists (from left to right in the painting) Fritz Matt (1909 – 1992), Albert Vahtramäe (1885 – 1965) and Voldemar Haas (1898 – 1982), depicts the artists conferring on set design drafts in the theatre's paint shop. In the background two paint-shop workers can be seen painting the set in question. This is apparently a fictional situation, since in real life Matt, Vahtramäe and Haas never created a single stage design together. Moreover, at the time the painting was made they worked in different theatres. Brown tones dominate the painting's colour scheme, with a splash of colour provided by the bright set-painting colours visible in the paint pots. The painting's style shows traces of Russian Real

works.d: Vladimir Alumäe ja Hugo Lepnurm (kaksikportree), 1957. Kaksikportree viiuldajast Vladimir Alumäest (1917 – 1979) ja organistist Hugo Lepnurmest (1914 – 1999) kontserti andmas. Maali esiplaanil kujutatud Alumäe poos on dünaamiline ja nõtke, on arusaadav, et ta elab oma muusikale kaasa. Tagaplaanil kujutatud Lepnurm on reserveeritum, kuid tema kergelt Alumäe poole suunatud pea ja naerune suu vihjavad kahe muusiku kokkukõlavale koostööle ja musitseerimisaegsele usaldusele teineteise suhtes. Maali laad on realistlik ning portreteeritavad psühholoogiliselt läbitöötatud. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Vladimir Alumäe and Hugo Lepnurm (double portrait), 1957. A double portrait of violinist Vladimir Alumäe (1917 – 1979) and organist Hugo Lepnurm (1914 – 1999) giving a concert. Alumäe's pose, depicted in the foreground of the painting, is dynamic and supple; it is clear that he is living through his music. Lepnurm, depicted in the background, is more reserved, but his head slightly turned toward Alumäe and his smiling mouth hint at the two musicians' harmonious collaboration and mutual trust during music-making. The style of the painting is realistic and the sitters are psychologically well developed. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Aleksander Arder (portreemaal), 1948. Estonia solisti (bariton), kontsertlaulja ja muusikapedagoogi Aleksander Arderi (1894 – 1966) 3/4 portree kujutab Arderit suure musta tiibklaveri taustal kontserti andmas. Arderi võimas kehaehitus ei jäta kahtlust ka tema võimsa hääle suhtes. Maali keskpunktiks on laulja säravalt helesinised silmad, mis muudavad teose peaaegu et karikatuurseks. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Aleksander Arder (portrait painting), 1948. The 3/4 portrait of the Estonia soloist (baritone), concert singer and music pedagogue Aleksander Arder (1894 – 1966) depicts Arder giving a concert against the background of a large black grand piano. Arder's powerful physique leaves no doubt about his powerful voice either. The focal point of the painting is the singer's brilliantly light blue eyes, which make the work almost caricature-like. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.dm: laius: 37.0 cm; kõrgus: 45.5 cm; laius: 40.5 cm; kõrgus: 49.0 cm
works.d: Olga Lund (portreemaal), 1949. Randeli 1/3 portreemaal kujutab Estonia solisti (metsosopran, hiljem sopran) Olga Lundi (1912 – 1998) keskealise tõsiseilmelise daamina. Väärikust rõhutavad karusnahkne krae, värvitud huuled ja kunstipäraselt kujundatud kulmud, kuid tänu Randeli psühholoogilisele lähenemisele kumab läbi, et tegelikult on tegemist nii-öelda lihtsa inimesega, kellesse elukogemus ja sõja-aastad on nähtava jälje jätnud. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Olga Lund (portrait painting), 1949. Randel's 1/3 portrait painting depicts the Estonia [Theatre] soloist (mezzo-soprano, later soprano) Olga Lund (1912 – 1998) as a middle-aged lady with a serious expression. Dignity is emphasized by the fur collar, painted lips and artistically shaped eyebrows, but thanks to Randel's psychological approach it shines through that in fact she is a so-called simple person, on whom life experience and the war years have left a visible mark. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Karl Kalkun (portreemaal), 1956. 3/4 psühholoogilis-realistlik portreemaal Karl Kalkun seeniorist (1900 – 1978), kes pidas Vanemuise teatris inspitsiendi ja rekvisiitori ametit ning mängis aeg-ajalt samas ka kõrvalosi. Raud kujutab Kalkunit vanemapoolse ning tõsiseilmelise, kuid siiski krutskilise härrasmehena, kelle väljanägemist ilmestavad üpris edevad aksessuaarid – viltune barett, punaseruuduline sall, kuldne uurikett ning piip. Maali koloriidis domineerivad lillakashallid toonid. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Karl Kalkun (portrait painting), 1956. A 3/4 psychological-realistic portrait painting of Karl Kalkun senior (1900 – 1978), who held the position of stage manager and props master at the Vanemuine theatre and occasionally also played minor roles there. Raud depicts Kalkun as an elderly, serious-looking, yet still mischievous gentleman, whose appearance is enlivened by rather vain accessories – a tilted beret, a red-checked scarf, a golden pocket watch chain, and a pipe. Lilac-grey tones dominate the colouring of the painting. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Jüri Õunap (portreemaal), 1950. Lihtne rahulikus laadis 1/4 portreemaal eesti  kirjanikust Jüri Õunapist (1887 – 1960), kes on muuhulgas ka neljavaatuselise draama „Nostra Regio“ (1914) autor. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Jüri Õunap (portrait painting), 1950. A simple, calmly styled quarter-length portrait painting of the Estonian writer Jüri Õunap (1887 – 1960), who is, among other things, the author of the four-act drama "Nostra Regio" (1914). /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Gustav Ernesaks mererannal (portreemaal), 1954. Pateetiline 3/4 portreemaal koorijuhist ja dirigendist, laulupidude sümboltegelasest Gustav Ernesaksast (1908 – 1993) tormisel mererannal. Koorijuht vaatab süvenenud ilmel, justkui valget laeva oodates kaugustesse, mantlihõlmad ja lips tuule käes lehvimas. Maali koloriidis domineerivad tormisele ilmale vastavalt sinakashallid toonid, heledamad on vaid laineharjad ja Ernesaksale kutsuvalt mõjuv horisont. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Gustav Ernesaks on the seashore (portrait painting), 1954. A pathos-filled 3/4 portrait painting of the choirmaster and conductor Gustav Ernesaks (1908 – 1993), a symbolic figure of song festivals, on a stormy seashore. The choirmaster gazes into the distance with a pensive expression, as if awaiting a white ship, his coat lapels and tie fluttering in the wind. The painting's colour scheme is dominated, in keeping with the stormy weather, by bluish-grey tones, with only the wave crests and the horizon — appearing inviting to Ernesaks — rendered lighter. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.t: Jüri Järvet, Voitinski. 1963. Tammsaare, Panso: Inimene ja Jumal, Draamateater
works.d: Jüri Järvet Voitinskina Tammsaare-Panso „Inimeses ja Jumalas“ (karakterportree), 1963.  Näitleja Jüri Järvet (1919 – 1995) Voitinski rollis 1962. aastal Draamateatris esietendunud suurlavastuses „Inimene ja Jumal“ (lavastaja Voldemar Panso). Hallop kujutab Voitinskit hallipäise ja -ilmelise vanamehena, kelle kohta J. Müür vahetute muljete põhjal kirjutas: „Jüri Järveti Voitinski on peatükk omaette ja üksiksaavutusena võib-olla parim kogu lavastuses. Elad temaga kaasa – tahaksid seda allakäinud hädavarest kogu hingest naerda ja... samal ajal nutta tolle aja ja elu pärast, mis inimese nii sügavale viis.“ („Tähtede all sündinud tõde“, Sirp ja Vasar 08.06.1962). /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Jüri Järvet as Voitinski in Tammsaare-Panso's „Inimeses ja Jumalas“ (character portrait), 1963. Actor Jüri Järvet (1919 – 1995) in the role of Voitinski in the major production „Inimene ja Jumal“, which premiered at the Drama Theatre in 1962 (director Voldemar Panso). Hallop depicts Voitinski as a grey-haired and grey-faced old man, about whom J. Müür wrote based on his immediate impressions: „Jüri Järvet's Voitinski is a chapter of its own and as an individual achievement is perhaps the best in the entire production. You live along with him – you would want to laugh at this fallen wretch with all your heart and... at the same time weep for the time and life that drove a man so deep down.“ („Tähtede all sündinud tõde“, Sirp ja Vasar 08.06.1962). /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.t: Franz Malmsten, Jürka. 1963. Tammsaare, Panso: Inimene ja Jumal, Draamateater
works.d: Franz Malmsten Jürkana Tammsaare-Panso „Inimeses ja Jumalas“ (karakterportree), 1963. Näitleja Franz Malmsten (1905 – 1967) Jürka rollis 1962. aastal Draamateatris esietendunud suurlavastuses „Inimene ja Jumal“ (lavastaja Voldemar Panso). Hallop kujutab Jürkat pisut ehmununa ja tuhmiilmelisena. Tundub nagu Jürka hakkaks kohe midagi ütlema, kuid sõnad on keelele kinni jäänud. Iseloomulikuks aksessuaariks on tema tumesinine mütsilotu. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Franz Malmsten as Jürka in Tammsaare-Panso's "Inimeses ja Jumalas" (character portrait), 1963. The actor Franz Malmsten (1905 – 1967) in the role of Jürka in the major production "Inimene ja Jumal" which premiered in 1962 at the Drama Theatre (director Voldemar Panso). Hallop depicts Jürka as somewhat startled and dull-faced. It seems as if Jürka is about to say something, but the words have stuck on his tongue. A characteristic accessory is his dark blue cap. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Ruut Tarmo (portreemaal), 1966. Ekspressionismi-hõngulises laadis 3/4 portree eesti näitlejast ja lavastajast Ruut Tarmost (1896 – 1967) kujutab meest ajal, mil ta oli viimast aastat Draamateatri näitleja. Kokku oli Tarmo Draamateatriga seotud olnud peaaegu kolmekümne aasta vältel, tehes aeg-ajalt olude sunnil kõrvalepõikeid ka Vanemuisesse, Rändteatrisse ja Estoniasse. Maali taust on abstraktne ja koloriit kirju, kuid pastelsetes, mahakeeratud toonides. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Ruut Tarmo (portrait painting), 1966. This 3/4 portrait, expressionistically toned, depicts the Estonian actor and director Ruut Tarmo (1896–1967) at a time when he was in his last year as an actor of the Drama Theatre. Altogether Tarmo had been connected with the Drama Theatre for almost thirty years, occasionally, when circumstances required, making detours to the Vanemuine, the Travelling Theatre and the Estonia. The background of the painting is abstract and the colouring varied, but in pastel, subdued tones. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Aili Engelberg (portreemaal), 1950. Pikaaegse Draamateatri näitlejanna Aili Engelbergi (1897 – 1974) 1/3 portree on valminud ajal, mil Engelberg oli just teatrist lahkunud ning näitlejaametist loobunud. Uhkeldav kübar, sametkleit, üle õla visatud punane sall, ehted, kaunid lokid ning punaseks värvitud suu lisavad portreele glamuursust, kuid selle taga on näha väsinud ja oma hiilguse minetanud keskealist naist, kelle ilme rikkalike aksessuaaridega kokku ei sobi. Pigem nukrat üldilmet rõhutab ka maali taust, millel kunstnik on kasutanud erinevaid pruune ja rohelisi toone ning saavutanud neid toone kombineerides üsna „porise“ lõpptulemuse. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Aili Engelberg (portrait painting), 1950. The 1/3 portrait of Aili Engelberg (1897 – 1974), a long-time actress of the Drama Theatre, was made at a time when Engelberg had just left the theatre and given up the acting profession. A flamboyant hat, a velvet dress, a red scarf thrown over the shoulder, jewelry, beautiful curls and lips painted red add glamour to the portrait, but behind this one can see a tired middle-aged woman who has lost her former splendor, whose expression does not match the abundant accessories. The rather sad overall impression is also emphasized by the painting's background, on which the artist has used various shades of brown and green and achieved, by combining these tones, a rather „muddy“ final result. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Jaan Rääts (portreemaal), 1964. Groteski-maiguline ekspressiivne 1/3 portree heliloojast ja pedagoogist, Eesti nõukogudeaegse muusikaelu ühest juhtfiguurist Jaan Räätsast (s. 1932), kes töötas maali valmimise ajal Eesti Raadio helirežissöörina. Raamat on portreteeritavat kujutanud justkui vaese kunstniku prototüübina, kelle lohkuvajunud põsed ning mõtlik pilk pajatavad palavikulisest loometegevusest. Melanhoolsust loob maali tumesinine koloriit. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Jaan Rääts (portrait painting), 1964. A grotesque-flavoured expressive 1/3 portrait of the composer and pedagogue, one of the leading figures of Estonian Soviet-era musical life, Jaan Rääts (b. 1932), who at the time the painting was made was working as a sound director at Estonian Radio. The book has depicted the sitter as if the prototype of a poor artist, whose sunken cheeks and pensive gaze speak of feverish creative activity. The dark blue coloring of the painting creates melancholy. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Eino Tamberg (portreemaal), 1963. Eesti neoklassitsistliku helilooja Eino Tambergi (1930 – 2010) 3/4  portree, kujutab Tambergi noore jõulise kehaehitusega mehena, kes seisab geometriseeritud vormidega värvikireva monumentaalmaali taustal. Helilooja kannab esinemisfrakki, kuid taskusse pistetud käsi viitab sellele, et kunstnik on tabanud ta puhkehetkel, justkui liikumise pealt. Maali valmimise aastal esietendus Estonias Tambergi A. H. Tammsaare miniatuuril „Poiss ja liblikas“ põhinev lühiballett, mis jätkas lühiballettide buumi, mille aluseks oli olnud Tambergi 1960. aastal Vanemuises esietendunud ballett „Ballett-sümfoonia“. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Eino Tamberg (portrait painting), 1963. The 3/4 portrait of Eino Tamberg (1930 – 2010), Estonian neoclassicist composer, depicts Tamberg as a young man of vigorous build, standing against the background of a colorful monumental painting with geometrized forms. The composer wears a performance tailcoat, but the hand tucked into his pocket suggests that the artist has captured him in a moment of rest, as if caught mid-movement. In the year the painting was completed, Tamberg's short ballet „Poiss ja liblikas“, based on the miniature by A. H. Tammsaare, premiered at Estonia, continuing the boom of short ballets that had been founded by Tamberg's ballet „Ballett-sümfoonia“, which premiered at Vanemuine in 1960. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Olev Eskola (portreemaal), 1964. 3/4 portreemaal näitlejast Olev Eskolast (1914 – 1990), keda Polli kujutab istumas raudrüü taustal. Ajal, mil maal valmis, oli Eskola Draamateatri näitleja ning raudrüü võib olla vihje mõnele näitleja märgilise tähendusega rollile. Maali ilmestavad tumedad kontuurjooned ning läbiv hallikassinine koloriit. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Olev Eskola (portrait painting), 1964. A 3/4 portrait painting of the actor Olev Eskola (1914 – 1990), whom Polli depicts sitting against a background of a suit of armour. At the time the painting was made, Eskola was an actor at the Drama Theatre, and the armour may be an allusion to some role of iconic significance for the actor. The painting is enlivened by dark contour lines and a pervasive grey-blue colour scheme. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.t: Franz Malmsten, Jürka. 1963. Tammsaare, Panso: Inimene ja Jumal, Draamateater
works.d: Franz Malmsten Jürkana Tammsaare-Panso „Inimeses ja Jumalas“ (karakterportree), 1963. Näitleja Franz Malmsten (1905 – 1967) Jürka rollis 1962. aastal Draamateatris esietendunud suurlavastuses „Inimene ja Jumal“ (lavastaja Voldemar Panso). Hallop kujutab Jürkat pisut ehmununa ja tuhmiilmelisena. Tundub nagu Jürka hakkaks kohe midagi ütlema, kuid sõnad on keelele kinni jäänud. Iseloomulikuks aksessuaariks on tema tumesinine mütsilotu. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Franz Malmsten as Jürka in Tammsaare-Panso's "Inimeses ja Jumalas" (character portrait), 1963. The actor Franz Malmsten (1905 – 1967) in the role of Jürka in the major production "Inimene ja Jumal" which premiered in 1962 at the Drama Theatre (director Voldemar Panso). Hallop depicts Jürka as somewhat startled and dull-faced. It seems as if Jürka is about to say something, but the words have stuck on his tongue. A characteristic accessory is his dark blue cap. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.t: Alfred Rebane, Slopašev. 1963. Tammsaare, Panso: Inimene ja Jumal, Draamateater
works.d: Alfred Rebane Slopaševina Tammsaare-Panso „Inimeses ja Jumalas“ (karakterportree), 1963. Näitleja Alfred Rebane (1902 – 1986) Slopaševi rollis 1962. aastal Draamateatris esietendunud suurlavastuses „Inimene ja Jumal“ (lavastaja Voldemar Panso). Hallop kujutab Slopaševit iseäraliku habeme ja soenguga muremõtetes keskealise meesterahvana, kelle kohta J. Müür vahetute muljete põhjal kirjutas: „Alfred Rebase Slopašev on ju igati tore karakter oma suurvene šovinismis, omaenda suuruses ja laiuses. Poleks isegi midagi katki, kui ta oleks veel suurem ja laiem, lohmakam.„ („Tähtede all sündinud tõde“, Sirp ja Vasar 08.06.1962). /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Alfred Rebane as Slopashev in Tammsaare-Panso's "Inimene ja Jumal" (character portrait), 1963. Actor Alfred Rebane (1902 – 1986) in the role of Slopashev in the major production "Inimene ja Jumal" ("Man and God"), which premiered at the Drama Theatre in 1962 (director Voldemar Panso). Hallop depicts Slopashev, with his peculiar beard and hairstyle, as a middle-aged man lost in troubled thought, about whom J. Müür wrote based on direct impressions: „Alfred Rebase Slopašev on ju igati tore karakter oma suurvene šovinismis, omaenda suuruses ja laiuses. Poleks isegi midagi katki, kui ta oleks veel suurem ja laiem, lohmakam.„ ("Tähtede all sündinud tõde", Sirp ja Vasar 08.06.1962). /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Andres Särev (portreemaal), 1962. Eesti lavastaja, näitleja ja dramatiseerija (sh A. H. Tammsaare ja Oskar Lutsu romaanid) Andres Särevi (1902 – 1970) 3/4 portree on stiliseerivas laadis, kasutatud on antud ajastule iseloomulikke tumedaid figuuri kontuurivaid piirjooni. Särevit on kujutatud väärika ning enesekindla vanemaealise härrasmehena, kelle nii-öelda vana kooli mentaliteeti rõhutavad kaabu, jalutuskepp ning pisut edev punaseruuduline sall. Maali koloriit on tume, taust pruunikas-hall. Laiad pintslilöögid loovad mulje justkui oleks taust abstraktne, kuid lähemal vaatlusel on tegu siiski pigem kirju tapeedimustriga, mis sulab ühte seinal oleva maaliga. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Andres Särev (portrait painting), 1962. The 3/4 portrait of Andres Särev (1902 – 1970), Estonian director, actor and dramatist (including dramatizations of novels by A. H. Tammsaare and Oskar Luts), is in a stylized manner, using dark figure-outlining contour lines characteristic of the period. Särev is depicted as a dignified and self-confident elderly gentleman, whose so-called old-school mentality is emphasized by a hat, a walking cane and a slightly vain red-checkered scarf. The painting's coloring is dark, the background brownish-gray. The broad brushstrokes create an impression as if the background were abstract, but on closer inspection it is rather a colorful wallpaper pattern that blends together with a painting hanging on the wall. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Helmi Einer (portreemaal), dateerimata. Eesti kontsert- ja ooperilaulja (sopran) Helmi Eineri (1888 – 1968) õrnnaiselik 3/4 portree, mis on ilmselt valminud 1930. aastatel, mil ta oli Estonia külalissolist ja lühemat aega Tallinna Konservatooriumi pedagoog. Triik kujutab Einerit pisut nukrailmelise ja mõtlikuna vaatajaid silmitsemas. Nii Eineri näos kui ka taustal on näha laulja siidise kleidikanga roosakaslillat veiklust. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Helmi Einer (portrait painting), undated. The delicately feminine 3/4 portrait of the Estonian concert and opera singer (soprano) Helmi Einer (1888 – 1968), apparently made in the 1930s, when she was a guest soloist at Estonia [Theatre] and briefly a teacher at the Tallinn Conservatory. Triik depicts Einer with a slightly sorrowful and pensive expression, gazing at the viewers. Both in Einer's face and in the background, a pinkish-lilac shimmer of the singer's silky dress fabric can be seen. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.dm: laius: 66.0 cm; kõrgus: 82.0 cm; laius: 82.5 cm; kõrgus: 98.0 cm
works.d: Anna Ekston (portreemaal), 1957. Korolevi 3/4 portreemaal baleriinist, balletipedagoogist ning Tallinna Koreograafiakooli asutajast ja direktrissist Anna Ekstonist (1908 – 1992) on mõjutatud vene realismist. Ekstonit on kujutatud enesekindlas poosis – seisvana, käed risti rinnal, kerge muie suul. Kui Bržeska (ML 180) kujutas Ekstonit pigem kunstnikuhingena - baleriini ja lavastajana -, siis Korolevi Ekston on pigem perenaiselik, temast õhkub pedagoogilisust ja kindlakäelisust, mis on kindlasti olulised omadused inimesele, kes on ühe suure kooli asutaja ja direktriss. Maali koloriidis domineerib taustal kasutatud tumepunane. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Anna Ekston (portrait painting), 1957. Korolev's 3/4 portrait of the ballerina, ballet pedagogue and founder and directress of the Tallinn Choreography School Anna Ekston (1908 – 1992) is influenced by Russian realism. Ekston is depicted in a self-confident pose – standing, arms crossed on her chest, a slight smile on her lips. While Bržeska (ML 180) depicted Ekston rather as an artist's soul – as a ballerina and stage director –, Korolev's Ekston is rather housewifely, radiating pedagogical skill and a firm hand, qualities certainly essential for a person who is the founder and directress of a large school. Dark red, used in the background, dominates the painting's colouring. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.dm: laius: 64.5 cm; kõrgus: 85.5 cm; laius: 75.0 cm; kõrgus: 96.5 cm
works.d: Benno Hansen (portreemaal), dateerimata. Estonia solisti (bass) Benno Hanseni (1891 – 1952) 1/2 portree on realistlik, kuid märgatav on kerge nurgeline stilisatsioon. Hansen kannab esinemisfrakki ning kikilipsu. Tema pilk on kergelt etteheitev ning laubal murekorts. Maali koloriit on tume, domineerivad sinaka varjundiga mustad ja hallid toonid. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Benno Hansen (portrait painting), undated. The 1/2 portrait of Benno Hansen (1891–1952), Estonia soloist (bass), is realistic, though a slight angular stylisation is noticeable. Hansen wears a performance tailcoat and a bow tie. His gaze is slightly reproachful, with a worried wrinkle on his forehead. The colouring of the painting is dark, with dominant bluish-tinted blacks and greys. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.dm: laius: 73.0 cm; kõrgus: 92.0 cm; laius: 75.0 cm; kõrgus: 94.0 cm
works.d: Aino Talvi (portreemaal), 1968. Eesti näitlejanna ja operetilaulja Aino Talvi (1909 – 1992) 3/4 portree on sisult psühholoogilis-realistlik, laadilt lakooniline ja pisut stiliseeritud. Talvi istub tühja seina taustal lihtsal puust toolil ning vaatab sugereerival pilgul vaatajatele otse silma. Kuna taust on hele ja pretensioonitu, siis tõmbab Talvi erksinises kostüümis figuur kogu tähelepanu endale, tekitades enda isiksuse osas lähemat huvi. Ehkki maal on psühholoogiliselt läbitöötatud, ei jää muljet nagu kunstnik oleks juba „kõik ära öelnud“. Pigem muudab selline aus kujutamisviis Talvi isiksuse salapäraseks ja läbitungimatuks. Maali valmimise aastal töötas Talvi näitlejana Draamateatris nin
works.de: Aino Talvi (portrait painting), 1968. The 3/4 portrait of the Estonian actress and operetta singer Aino Talvi (1909 – 1992) is psychologically realistic in content, laconic and somewhat stylised in manner. Talvi sits on a simple wooden chair against a bare wall background and looks the viewer directly in the eye with a suggestive gaze. Since the background is light and unpretentious, Talvi's figure, in a bright blue costume, draws all attention to itself, arousing closer interest in her personality. Although the painting is psychologically well worked out, one does not get the impression that the artist has already "said it all". Rather, this honest manner of depiction makes Talvi's personality mysterious and impenetrable. In the year the painting was made, Talvi was working as an actress at the Drama Theatre and

works.d: Edgar Arro (portreemaal), 1969. Eesti helilooja ja organisti, peamiselt rahvaviisidel põhinevate väikevormide autorina tuntud Edgar Arro (1911 – 1978) 3/4 portree valmis pärast Arro heliloomingu laiemat taasavastamist 1968. aastal, mil helilooja andis välja esimese kuuest vihikust „Eesti rahvaviise“. Kuues vihikus oli kokku viiskümmend seitse eesti rahvaviisidel põhinevat väikevormi. Enne II maailmasõda oli Arro tuntud koori- ja levimuusika loojana, kuid need teosed olid riigikorra muutudes unustuste hõlma vajunud. Väli on Arrot kujutanud erkpunase ja -oranži tühja seina taustal, istumas lihtsal puust toolil. Helilooja nägu on tõsine ning poos mõnevõrra kramplik. Tema isiksus jääb vaatajatel
works.de: Edgar Arro (portrait painting), 1969. The 3/4 portrait of the Estonian composer and organist Edgar Arro (1911 – 1978), known mainly as the author of small forms based on folk tunes, was made after the wider rediscovery of Arro's musical work in 1968, when the composer published the first of six booklets of "Eesti rahvaviise" ("Estonian Folk Tunes"). The six booklets together contained fifty-seven small forms based on Estonian folk tunes. Before the Second World War, Arro was known as a composer of choral and popular music, but these works had sunk into oblivion as the state system changed. Väli has depicted Arro against a background of a bare wall in bright red and orange, sitting on a simple wooden chair. The composer's face is serious and his pose somewhat tense. His personality remains for viewers

works.d: Julius Põder (portreemaal), 1913. Eesti näitleja ja näitejuhi Julius Põderi (1889 – 1959) pisiformaadis 1/3 portree on loodud ajal, mil kunstnik ja portreteeritav olid kolleegid Karl Menningu juhitavas Vanemuise teatris. Lahtise pintslilöögiga realistlik portree kujutab Põderit sigaretti suitsetamas, suur sall boheemlaslikult ümber kaela seotud. Maali koloriidis domineerivad soojad oranžid ning neile vastanduvad rohekad toonid. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Julius Põder (portrait painting), 1913. The small-format 1/3 portrait of the Estonian actor and theatre director Julius Põder (1889 – 1959) was created at a time when the artist and the sitter were colleagues at the Vanemuine theatre led by Karl Menning. The realistic portrait, with loose brushwork, depicts Põder smoking a cigarette, a large scarf tied bohemian-style around his neck. Warm oranges dominate the painting's coloring, contrasted by greenish tones. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Samuel Saulus (portreemaal), 1970. Eesti flötisti ja flöödimuusikapropageerija Samuel Sauluse (1933 – 1990) 3/4 portree kujutab teda andmas flöödimuusika kontserti. Sauluse silmad on suletud ning poos virtuooslikult nõtke, justkui tantsiks ta oma muusikale kaasa. Pollile iseomaselt on nii figuur kui ka taust, millele on maalitud kõlakoridorid, sarnases, tume- ja helesiniste variatsioonidega koloriidis. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Samuel Saulus (portrait painting), 1970. The 3/4 portrait of the Estonian flutist and promoter of flute music Samuel Saulus (1933 – 1990) depicts him giving a flute music concert. Saulus's eyes are closed and his pose is virtuosically supple, as if he were dancing along to his music. As is characteristic of Poll, both the figure and the background, onto which sound corridors have been painted, are rendered in a similar colour scheme with dark and light blue variations. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Kuldar Sink (portreemaal), 1976. Modernistlikus laadis portreemaal ekstsertrilise loomuga eesti heliloojast ja flötistist Kuldar Sinkist (1942 – 1995), mis on loodud ajal, mil Sinki looming oli tugevasti mõjutatud kasahhi ja kirgiisi rahvamuusikast. Idapoolsete rahvaste rahvamuusika tõi Sinki heliloomingusse idaliku lõpmatult kestva aja mõiste ning vaba improvisatsiooni. Lilia Sink, kes oli selleks hetkeks juba muusiku eksabikaasa, kujutab meest istumas võrdlemisi tühjas, läikivate pindadega ruumis, mida täidavad päikesekollased geometriseeritud vormidega helgid ja varjud. Sinki iseloomustavad moekohased prillid ja habe ning peenikesed ja pikad jäsemed. Peegeldavate klaaside tagant paistvad
works.de: Kuldar Sink (portrait painting), 1976. A modernist-style portrait painting of the eccentric Estonian composer and flautist Kuldar Sink (1942 – 1995), created at a time when Sink's work was strongly influenced by Kazakh and Kyrgyz folk music. The folk music of the eastern peoples brought into Sink's musical creation the oriental notion of endlessly continuing time and free improvisation. Lilia Sink, who by that time was already the musician's ex-wife, depicts the man sitting in a fairly empty room with glossy surfaces, filled with sun-yellow, geometricised patches of light and shadow. Sink is characterised by fashionable glasses and a beard, and thin, long limbs. Visible from behind the reflective lenses

works.d: Riho Päts (portreemaal), 1971. 1/2 portreemaal heliloojast, koorijuhist, muusikapedagoogist ja silmapaistvast muusikapedagoogika edendajast Riho Pätsist (1899 – 1977), millel peatähelepanu tõmbab Pätsi geometriseeritud võrgustikuga kaetud ja psühholoogiliselt läbitöötatud nägu. Tema keha, mille puhul on Roode samuti geomeetrilisi vorme kasutanud, mõjub seevastu väga väikesena, peaaegu grotesksena. Pätsi taga paistab kummut, millele on asetatud kõrge vaas. Seetõttu võib arvata, et helilooja poseeris kunstnikule oma kodus, oma tugitoolis ja oma sisseharjunud mugavas asendis. Maali koloriit on värviküllane ja erk. Maali valmimise ajal töötas Päts viimast aastat Tallinna Pedagoogilise Instituudi
works.de: Riho Päts (portrait painting), 1971. A 1/2 portrait painting of the composer, choir conductor, music educator and outstanding promoter of music pedagogy Riho Päts (1899 – 1977), in which the main attention is drawn by Päts's face, covered with a geometricised network and psychologically well worked out. His body, in which Roode has likewise used geometric forms, appears by contrast very small, almost grotesque. Behind Päts a chest of drawers can be seen, on which a tall vase has been placed. One may therefore assume that the composer posed for the artist at his home, in his own armchair, in his own habitual, comfortable position. The painting's colouring is rich and vivid. At the time the painting was made, Päts was in his last year working at the Tallinn Pedagogical Institute

works.d: Ants Eskola Don Carlosena Schilleri „Don Carloses“ (karakterportree),  ̴ 1958.  Legendaarse näitleja Ants Eskola (1908 – 1989) karakterportree Don Carlose rollis 1958. aastal Draamateatris esietendunud Schilleri ajaloolises tragöödias „Don Carlos“ (lavastaja Leo Kalmet). Näidendi tegevus leiab aset 16. sajandi Hispaania õukonnas ning Eskola Don Carlos on riietatud ajastutruusse edevasse ja luksuslikku kostüümi, mis vihjab sellele, et tegemist on troonipärijaga. Samale vihjab ka Eskola kaugustesse suunatud kõrk pilk ning eneseteadlik poos. Maal on loodud realistlikus laadis ning detailidele suurt tähelepanu pöörates. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Ants Eskola as Don Carlos in Schiller's "Don Carlos" (character portrait), ̴ 1958. A character portrait of the legendary actor Ants Eskola (1908 – 1989) in the role of Don Carlos in Schiller's historical tragedy "Don Carlos", which premiered at the Drama Theatre in 1958 (director Leo Kalmet). The play's action takes place in the 16th-century Spanish court, and Eskola's Don Carlos is dressed in a period-accurate, vain and luxurious costume, which hints that this is the heir to the throne. The same is hinted at by Eskola's haughty gaze directed into the distance and his self-assured pose. The painting is created in a realistic manner, with great attention paid to detail. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.dm: laius: 76.5 cm; kõrgus: 95.0 cm; laius: 82.0 cm; kõrgus: 99.0 cm
works.d: Nigol Andresen (portreemaal), 1940. Kulkoffi portreteeritud  Nigol Andresen (1899 – 1985) on peamiselt tuntud kirjandus- ja teatrikriitiku ning dramaturgina (Hommikteater, Draamateater ja Tallinna Töölisteater), hiljem ka poliitiku ja ühiskonnategelasena. 1940. aastal, mil portree valmis, valiti Andresen Johannes Varese valitsuse välisministriks ning ühtlasi ka Rahvakomissaride Nõukogu esimehe I asetäitjaks. Ilmselt ongi Kulkoff oma maalil kujutanud pigem poliitikut kui teatritegelast. Sellele vihjab esmalt ametlik poos, laud ja laual olev punane vimpel ning pitseriga dokumendipaber Andreseni käes. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Nigol Andresen (portrait painting), 1940. Nigol Andresen (1899 – 1985), portrayed by Kulkoff, is mainly known as a literary and theatre critic and playwright (Hommikteater, the Drama Theatre and the Tallinn Workers' Theatre), and later also as a politician and public figure. In 1940, when the portrait was made, Andresen was elected Foreign Minister of Johannes Vares's government, and at the same time First Deputy Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars. Kulkoff has apparently depicted in his painting a politician rather than a theatre figure. This is hinted at first of all by the official pose, the table and the red pennant on it, and the sealed document paper in Andresen's hand. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.dm: laius: 65.0 cm; kõrgus: 81.0 cm; laius: 70.0 cm; kõrgus: 87.0 cm
works.d: Viktor Gurjev (portreemaal), 1978. 1/2 portreemaal Estonia solistist (tenor) ja koos Georg Otsaga massilauludega kontsertidel duette esitanud Viktor Gurjevist (1914 – 1985) kujutab teda hallipäise mehena, kelle sirgeselgne poos ja pisut kergitatud lõug annavad märku, et tegemist on eneseteadliku ja väärika härraga. Maali koloriit on tasakaalustatud, segunevad nii külmad kui soojad toonid, andes maalile rahuliku üldmulje. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Viktor Gurjev (portrait painting), 1978. This 1/2 portrait painting of Estonia soloist (tenor) Viktor Gurjev (1914 – 1985), who performed duets with Georg Ots at mass song concerts, depicts him as a grey-haired man whose upright posture and slightly raised chin indicate that he is a self-aware and dignified gentleman. The painting's colour scheme is balanced, mixing both cold and warm tones, giving the painting a calm overall impression. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Eugen Kapp (portreemaal), 1978. 1/3 pastellportree eesti heliloojast ja muusikapedagoogist Eugen Kapist (1908 – 1996), kelle kuulsaimate teoste hulka kuuluvad ooper „Tasuleegid“ (1945) ja ballett „Kalevipoeg“ (1947). Einmann on Kapi portree loonud ekspressionistlikus laadis kasutades nii tugev-erksaid värvitoone kui ka musti figuuri kontuurivaid piirjooni. Portree on stiliseeritud, Kappi kujutatakse vanemaealise kindlailmelise härrasmehena, kelle lipsu „kootud“ punane võib vihjata sellele, et helilooja näol oli tegemist ustava parteilasega ning endise NSVL Ülemnõukogu saadikuga. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Eugen Kapp (portrait painting), 1978. A 1/3 pastel portrait of Estonian composer and music pedagogue Eugen Kapp (1908 – 1996), among whose most famous works are the opera "Tasuleegid" (1945) and the ballet "Kalevipoeg" (1947). Einmann has created Kapp's portrait in an expressionist manner, using both strong, bright colour tones and black contour lines outlining the figure. The portrait is stylised, Kapp is depicted as an elderly gentleman with a firm expression, whose tie's "woven" red colour may allude to the fact that the composer was a loyal party member and a former deputy of the USSR Supreme Council. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Ants Jõgi, vana näitleja (portreemaal), 1978. Eesti draamanäitleja (töötanud Ugalas, Estonias ning Eesti Draamateatris), pisirollide meistri Ants Jõgi (1892 – 1983) 1/2 portree on teostatud ekspressiivselt, värvikasutus on julge, pastoosne ja rahutu. Jõgi istub tugitoolis ning toetub oma kepile. Ta on kujutatud psühholoogilise sügavusega, näojooned ning kehahoid peegeldavad elukogemust ja mõtlikku olekut. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Ants Jõgi, old actor (portrait painting), 1978. The 1/2 portrait of Estonian drama actor Ants Jõgi (1892 – 1983), who worked at Ugala, Estonia, and the Estonian Drama Theatre, a master of minor roles, is executed expressively, with bold, pastose and restless use of colour. Jõgi sits in an armchair, leaning on his cane. He is depicted with psychological depth, his facial features and posture reflecting life experience and a pensive state. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Velda Otsus Julia osas (karakterportree), 1946. Vanemuise esibaleriini Velda Otsuse (1913 – 2006) karakterportree Julia kostüümis on ilmselt maalitud kas käeharjutusena või siis ühismaalimisel ateljees. Sellest annab tunnistust asjaolu, et pea täpselt samasugune portree Otsusest on ka Eduard Einmannil (VIIDE ETMM9019/ML8). Otsuse portree on psühholoogiliselt läbitöötatud ning tema näol peegelduvad nii Juliale kui näitlejannale endale omased karakteristikud. Võrreldes Einmanniga on Teder keskendunud pigem figuurile ja näole, mitte niivõrd taustale ning Julia voogavale kleidile. Maali juurde kuulub kullatud põimikuga kaunistatud iluraam. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Velda Otsus in the role of Julia (character portrait), 1946. The character portrait of Velda Otsus (1913 – 2006), leading ballerina of Vanemuine, in the costume of Julia, was apparently painted either as a hand exercise or during a joint painting session in the studio. This is evidenced by the fact that an almost exactly identical portrait of Otsus also exists by Eduard Einmann (REF ETMM9019/ML8). Otsus's portrait is psychologically well worked out, and her face reflects characteristics typical both of Julia and of the actress herself. Compared to Einmann, Teder has focused more on the figure and face, rather than on the background and Julia's flowing dress. The painting is fitted with a decorative frame adorned with a gilded braid. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.dm: laius: 53.0 cm; kõrgus: 65.0 cm; laius: 55.5 cm; kõrgus: 68.0 cm
works.d: Salme Reek (portreemaal), 1980. Eesti Draamateatri näitlejannat Salme Reeki (1907 – 1996) on 1/2 portreel kujutatud mõtlikult, rahulikult, tagasihoidlikke värve kasutades. Näo kujutamisel on hoidutud kunstilistest liialdustest, otse ette vaatavat näitlejannat on jäädvustatud realistlikult. Kontrastina mõjub tumepunane pastoosne taust, mis on loodud ärevate pintslilöökidega. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Salme Reek (portrait painting), 1980. Salme Reek (1907–1996), an actress of the Estonian Drama Theatre, is depicted in a 1/2 portrait thoughtfully, calmly, using restrained colours. In depicting the face, artistic exaggerations have been avoided; the actress, gazing straight ahead, has been captured realistically. The dark red pastose background, created with agitated brushstrokes, provides a contrast. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Andres Särev (portreemaal), 1946. Kunstnik Halliste on Eesti lavastajat, näitlejat ja dramatiseerijat (sh A. H. Tammsaare ja Oskar Lutsu romaanid) Andres Särevit (1902 – 1970) portreteerinud ilmselt oma ateljees – sellele vihjavad põrandale asetatud maalid Särevi selja taga. Tundub, justkui oleks portreteeritav kunstnikule lihtsalt külla läinud – ilma kindla soovita end jäädvustada lasta. Särev istub mõtlikul ilmel ja sigaret näpus toolil, kust – tundub – tahaks ta justkui püsti tõusma hakata. Maali koloriit on kirju, kuid valitsevateks toonideks on sinakashallid, portreteeritava silmadega harmoneeruvad toonid. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Andres Särev (portrait painting), 1946. The artist Halliste has portrayed the Estonian stage director, actor and dramatizer (incl. of the novels of A. H. Tammsaare and Oskar Luts) Andres Särev (1902 – 1970) apparently in his own studio – this is hinted at by the paintings placed on the floor behind Särev. It seems as though the sitter had simply come to visit the artist – without any particular wish to have himself immortalised. Särev sits with a thoughtful expression and a cigarette in hand on a chair from which – it seems – he might be about to rise. The painting's colouring is varied, but the dominant tones are bluish-greys, tones that harmonise with the sitter's eyes. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Maastik väikese majaga (maastikumaal), 1944. Aovalguses maalitud sügisene maastik vanaaegse kooguga kaevu ja väikese majaga, mille juurde viib looklev tee.
works.de: Landscape with a small house (painting), 1944. An autumn landscape painted in morning light, with an old well with a sweep and a small house, to which a winding path leads.

works.d: Viktor Pedoste (portreemaal), 1968. Eesti kohtuniku ja usutegelase Viktor Pedoste (1892 – 1979) 1/3 pastellportree kujutab portreteeritavat juba väärikas eas härrasmehe ja austatud kohtunikuna. Nooremana, aastatel 1914 – 1922 oli Pedoste olnud Aleksander Nevski kiriku kooliõpetaja ja koorijuht Tartus. Eller on portreteeritavasse suhtunud sümpaatiaga, portree on lihtne, lakooniline ja sõbralik. Muidu tagasihoidlikkusse koloriiti lisab erksust punase tooni põimimine Pedoste ülikonna- ja lipsumustrisse ning ootamatult ka tema hallidesse juustesse. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Viktor Pedoste (portrait painting), 1968. The 1/3 pastel portrait of the Estonian judge and religious figure Viktor Pedoste (1892 – 1979) depicts the sitter already at a dignified age, as a gentleman and respected judge. As a younger man, in the years 1914 – 1922, Pedoste had been a schoolteacher and choirmaster at the Alexander Nevsky Church in Tartu. Eller has treated the sitter with sympathy; the portrait is simple, laconic and friendly. To the otherwise restrained colouring, vividness is added by the weaving of a red tone into the pattern of Pedoste's suit and tie, and unexpectedly also into his grey hair. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.dm: laius: 80.5 cm; kõrgus: 116.0 cm; laius: 86.0 cm; kõrgus: 120.0 cm
works.d: Veljo Tormis (portreemaal), 1978. Eesti helilooja Veljo Tormise (s. 1930) 3/4 portree tundub olevat maalitud suure sümpaatiaga. Portreteeritav istub veerandpöördes paremale toetades vasakut kätt maali vasakus nurgas olevale kirjutuslauale. Maali koloriit on pigem soe ning meeleolulist helgust toetab see, et kergelt muigav Tormis on pilgu pööranud otse vaatajate poole. Maali taust on rohekates toonides; tool, millel portreteeritav istub on kärtspunane. Taustaga ühes koloriidis on ka laual olevad visandlikult joonistatud raamatud. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Veljo Tormis (portrait painting), 1978. The 3/4 portrait of the Estonian composer Veljo Tormis (b. 1930) seems to have been painted with great sympathy. The sitter sits turned a quarter to the right, resting his left hand on a writing desk in the left corner of the painting. The colouring of the painting is rather warm, and the atmospheric brightness is supported by the fact that the slightly smiling Tormis has turned his gaze directly toward the viewers. The background of the painting is in greenish tones; the chair on which the sitter sits is scarlet red. The books on the table, drawn in a sketchy manner, are in the same colour scheme as the background. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Laine Mesikäpp (portreemaal), 1981. Eesti näitleja, leelotaja ning laulu- ja tantsupidude sümboltegelase Laine Mesikäpa (1917 – 2012) 3/4 portree on ülev –  Mesikäppa pole kujutatud mitte tavainimesena, vaid just lauluemana. Portreteeritav on riietatud Lihula rahvarõivastesse, peas tanu ja kaelas sõlgedest kee. Figuur on maalitud veerandpöördes paremale ning Mesikäpa pilk suunatud kaugusesse. Abstraktne taust on Bržeskale omastes lillakas-rohekates toonides. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Laine Mesikäpp (portrait painting), 1981. The 3/4 portrait of the Estonian actress, folk singer and symbolic figure of song and dance festivals Laine Mesikäpp (1917 – 2012) is sublime – Mesikäpp is depicted not as an ordinary person, but precisely as a lauluema (song mother). The sitter is dressed in Lihula folk costume, with a bonnet on her head and a necklace of brooches around her neck. The figure is painted in a quarter-turn to the right, and Mesikäpp's gaze is directed into the distance. The abstract background is in the purplish-greenish tones typical of Bržeska. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Ellen Laidre (portreemaal), 1974. Soololaulja (sopran) ja muusikapedagoogi Ellen Laidre (1916 – 1981) 1/3 portree on jõuline ja terav. Laidre ilme väljendab enesekindlust ja -teadlikust, tema silmad on suunatud sihiteadlikult kaugusesse. Maali koloriidis vastanduvad Laidre pluusikanga puhas helesinine ning tausta hajusam punakaspruun. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Ellen Laidre (portrait painting), 1974. The 1/3 portrait of the solo singer (soprano) and music pedagogue Ellen Laidre (1916 – 1981) is forceful and sharp. Laidre's expression conveys confidence and self-awareness, her eyes are directed purposefully into the distance. In the painting's colour scheme the pure light blue of Laidre's blouse fabric is contrasted with the more diffuse reddish-brown of the background. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d:
Portreemaal, 1980. 
Hoogsal ekspressiivses laadis 1/4 portreel koorijuhist ja heliloojast Gustav Ernesaksast (1908–1993) on laulupidude sümboltegelast kujutatud keskendunult, veidi – heas mõttes – hullunud pilgul, võib-olla just samal hetkel koori juhatamas. Maali koloriidis domineerivad külmad tumedad toonid, mida Okas on kasutanud ka Ernesaksa näo ilmestamiseks, ning mis loovad mulje nagu seisaks koorijuht keset tormi. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de:
Portrait painting, 1980.
In a vigorous expressive style, the 1/4 portrait of choirmaster and composer Gustav Ernesaks (1908–1993), the symbolic figure of the Song Festivals, depicts him focused, with a slightly – in a good sense – frenzied gaze, perhaps at the very moment of conducting the choir. The painting's colour scheme is dominated by cold, dark tones, which Okas has also used to render Ernesaks's face, creating the impression that the choirmaster is standing amid a storm. /text by Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Eino Tamberg (portreemaal), 1980. Eesti neoklassitsistliku helilooja Eino Tambergi (1930 – 2010) stiliseeritud ½ portree. Malin kujutab Tambergi vaatajatele suletuna, justkui tukkuvana. Maali geometriseeritud sinises koloriidis taust loob mulje nagu oleks helilooja mere ääres – ümbritsetud ranna kisast-kärast, kuid sellest hoolimata täiesti eraldi, omas maailmas. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Eino Tamberg (portrait painting), 1980. A stylised 1/2 portrait of the Estonian neoclassical composer Eino Tamberg (1930–2010). The painting depicts Tamberg as closed off to viewers, as if dozing. The geometricised blue-toned background of the painting creates the impression as if the composer were by the sea – surrounded by the noise and bustle of the shore, yet nonetheless completely apart, in his own world. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.de: Textile, embroidery threads; text on the verso; diameter 14 cm. The head of a middle-aged laughing woman in a frontal view; the painting is round, placed under the mount so that the portrait is tilted to the left; the woman has brown, shoulder-length curly hair, brown eyes, a broad face with high cheekbones; the background is colourful.

works.t: Heino Otto, Neeme. Eugen Kapp: ooper Tasuleegid
works.d: Heino Otto Neemena Eugen Kapi ooperis „Tasuleegid“ (karakterportree), dateerimata. Karakterportree Heino Ottost (1915 – 1982) Neeme rollis Kaarel Irdi lavastatud Eugen Kapi ooperis „Tasuleegid“, mis esietendus 1945. aastal Estonia teatris. Otto oli näitleja (Tallinna Töölisteater ja Vanemuine), ooperisolist (Estonia) ning osales ka balletilavastustes (samuti Estonias). Kitse loodud karakterportree kujutab Ottot üpris uhkeldavates rõivastes muinasaegse sõdurina. Pintslikäsitlus on vaba ja hoogne, koloriit tume. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Heino Otto as Neeme in Eugen Kapp's opera "Tasuleegid" ["Flames of Revenge"] (character portrait), undated. A character portrait of Heino Otto (1915 – 1982) in the role of Neeme in Eugen Kapp's opera "Tasuleegid", staged by Kaarel Ird, which premiered in 1945 at the Estonia Theatre. Otto was an actor (Tallinn Workers' Theatre and Vanemuine), an opera soloist (Estonia) and also took part in ballet productions (likewise at Estonia). The character portrait created by Kits depicts Otto in rather ostentatious attire as an ancient warrior. The brushwork is free and vigorous, the colour scheme dark. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Mart Saar (portreemaal), 1979. 1/3 saržilikus võtmes portree uuenduslikust eesti heliloojast Mart Saarest (1882 – 1963) on maalitud postuumselt. Raba portreemaal rõhutab eriliselt Saarele eriomaseid väliseid karakteristikuid nagu kiilas pea, ümmargused prillid ja silmatorkavalt aetud habe ning vuntsid. Maali koloriit on punakaslilla, huvitava aktsendi loob erksinine valgetriibuline lips. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Mart Saar (portrait painting), 1979. A 1/3 portrait in a sketch-like manner of the innovative Estonian composer Mart Saar (1882 – 1963) was painted posthumously. Raba's portrait painting particularly emphasizes the external characteristics typical of Saar, such as his bald head, round glasses and strikingly trimmed beard and moustache. The painting's colour scheme is reddish-purple, with an interesting accent created by a bright blue tie with white stripes. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Heino Vaks (portreemaal), 1950. Postuumselt loodud 1/2 portree näitlejast ja näitejuhist Heino Vaksist (1886 – 1943) kujutab teatritegelast istumas aksidevahelise kirjutuslaua ääres hoidmas käes suurt seina- või kavalehte, millele on kirjutatud „Libahunt“. Vaksi silmad on poolsuletud, suu poolmuigel ning ilme sõbralik. Maali koloriidis domineerivad pruunid ja punakad toonid, mis loovad sooja üldmulje. Vaks töötas näitleja ja näitejuhina Vanemuises, Estonias, Draamateatris, Rändteatris ning Narva Teatris. Tema teatriajalooalasest kollektsioonist sai alguse Eesti Teatri- ja Muusikamuuseumi teatriosakond. /tekst Liisi Aibel, 2013/
works.de: Heino Vaks (portrait painting), 1950. A posthumously created 1/2 portrait of the actor and stage director Heino Vaks (1886 – 1943) depicts the theatre figure sitting at a Biedermeier-style writing desk, holding in his hand a large poster or programme sheet on which is written "Libahunt". Vaks's eyes are half-closed, his mouth in a half-smile, his expression friendly. Brown and reddish tones dominate the painting's colouring, creating a warm overall impression. Vaks worked as an actor and stage director at Vanemuine, Estonia, the Drama Theatre, the Travelling Theatre and the Narva Theatre. His collection on theatre history became the foundation of the theatre department of the Estonian Theatre and Music Museum. /text Liisi Aibel, 2013/

works.d: Ida Urbel (portreemaal), 1946. Vanemuise ballettmeistri ja lavastaja Ida Urbeli (1900 – 1983) 3/4 portree on ilmselt maalitud kas käeharjutusena või siis ühismaalimisel ateljees. Sellest annab tunnistust asjaolu, et pea täpselt samasugune portree Urbelist on ka Eduard Einmannil (VIIDE ETMM6056/ML55). 1946. aastal lavastas Urbel Vanemuise teatris Prokofjevi „Romeo ja Julia“, võimalik, et maal on tehtud ajal, mil käis antud lavastuse prooviperiood. Teder kujutab Urbelit puhkehetkel suitsetamas. Laual olevas vaasis kõrguv lillebukett ning õunad vihjavad varasügisesele ajale – hooaja algusele. Võrreldes Einmannile kujutab Teder Urbelit helgemas meeleolus, pisut mõtliku kuid mitte kurvana. Maali
works.de: Ida Urbel (portrait painting), 1946. The 3/4 portrait of Vanemuine's ballet master and director Ida Urbel (1900 – 1983) was apparently painted either as a hand exercise or during joint painting sessions in the studio. This is evidenced by the fact that an almost identical portrait of Urbel also exists by Eduard Einmann (REFERENCE ETMM6056/ML55). In 1946 Urbel staged Prokofiev's "Romeo and Juliet" at the Vanemuine theatre, and it is possible that the painting was made during the rehearsal period of this production. Teder depicts Urbel smoking during a moment of rest. The bouquet of flowers rising from the vase on the table and the apples suggest early autumn – the start of the season. Compared to Einmann, Teder portrays Urbel in a brighter mood, slightly pensive but not sad. Painting
