works.de: Rizzoni, Aleksander (1836, Riga – 1902, Rome). Born into the family of an Italian merchant from Bologna who had settled in Riga. Brother of the artists Paul and Eduard Rizzoni. In the period 1852–62 studied at the Petersburg Academy of Arts under Bogdan (Gottfried) Willewalde. After 1866 lived permanently in Rome. The artist knew Pavel Tretyakov well, on whose commission he selected works of art for his collection. In 1866 was awarded the title of academician of the Academy of Arts, in 1868 the title of professor of painting. The range of subjects for his small genre paintings included small pictures of the life of Jews and Catholic clergy, everyday street life of Rome. The artist was deeply attached to the Eternal City. There are few artists in art history who [drew on] the subject matter of their works [in this way]

works.de: Zhukovsky, Stanislav (1873, Yendrikhovtsy, Grodno Governorate – 1944, Pruszków, near Warsaw). Born into a family of Polish nobility, from whom estates and noble rights had been taken for participation in the Polish uprising of 1863. Finished the Warsaw classical gymnasium, studied at the Białystok Real School. In 1892 went on his own to Moscow to study painting. Entered the Moscow School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture, which he finished in 1901 with a large silver medal and the title of professional artist for the painting "Moonlit Night". The artist was most influenced by the work of his teacher Isaac Levitan. From 1895 exhibited at exhibitions of the Society for Travelling Art Exhibitions, in 1902–03 was among the ranks of Mir Iskusstva. In 1903 participated in Russian Art[ists']

works.d: Kutšumov, Vassili (1788, Peterburi – 1959, Leningrad). Õppis 1910–16 Peterburi Kunstiakadeemia Kõrgemas kunstikoolis. Maali „Peeter I vaatab Veenuse kuju Suvepalees” eest sai diplomeeritud kunstniku nimetuse. Oli lähedane Mir Iskusstva kunstnikele, osales ka rühmituste Sõltumatute Ühing (1911–14), Kolmnurk (1908), AHRR (alates 1917) ja A. Kuindži Seltsi (1926–29) näitustel. Maalis ajaloomaale, maastikke, olustikulisi interjööre, töötas ka teatrikunstnikuna. „Peeter I Neeva kaldal” jätkab kunstniku Peeter I-le pühendatud ajaloomaalide rida, mille lineaarsuses ja kompositsiooni teatud teatraalsuses on tunda Mir Iskusstva kunstnike mõjutusi.
works.de: Kutšumov, Vassili (1788, Saint Petersburg – 1959, Leningrad). Studied 1910–16 at the Higher Art School of the Saint Petersburg Academy of Arts. Received the title of certified artist for the painting "Peter I Looking at a Statue of Venus in the Summer Palace". He was close to the Mir Iskusstva artists, and also participated in exhibitions of the groups Union of Independents (1911–14), Treugolnik (1908), AHRR (from 1917) and the A. Kuindzhi Society (1926–29). He painted historical paintings, landscapes, genre interiors, and also worked as a theatre artist. "Peter I on the Bank of the Neva" continues the artist's series of historical paintings devoted to Peter I, in whose linearity and a certain theatricality of composition the influence of the Mir Iskusstva artists can be felt.

works.de: Bakałowicz, Stefan (1857, Warsaw – 1947, Rome). Born into the family of a Polish artist and actress. In 1874–76 studied at the Warsaw drawing school, in 1876 entered the Petersburg Academy of Arts, where he studied under Vasily Vereshchagin and took private lessons from Pavel Chistyakov. Having won the competition for the grand gold medal and earned the title of professional artist, the artist traveled abroad in 1881 as an Academy of Arts stipendiary. Lived mainly in Rome, but also visited, among other places, North Africa and Paris. After becoming acquainted with the history of Pompeii and archaeological finds, an antiquity-reminiscent milieu came into the artist's work. As a salon artist who managed to please many, he sold his works successfully both in Italy and in Russia.

works.de: Clodt von Jürgensburg, Mihhail (1832, Petersburg – 1902, Petersburg). Descended from a family of artists belonging to the Baltic nobility. His father Konstantin cultivated woodcut as one of the first in Russia, Peter Clodt von Jürgensburg was a well-known sculptor, and the painter Mihhail Clodt was his cousin. As a boy studied drawing under Jan (Ivan) Khrutsky at the Petersburg Corps of Mining Engineers. Then continued, against his parents' wishes, his studies in the landscape painting class of the Petersburg Academy of Arts under Maxim Vorobyov. Finished the Academy of Arts in 1858 with a gold medal and the title of 1st degree professional artist. Traveled as a stipendiary to France, Switzerland and Italy, but in 1861 received, as an exception, permission from the Academy of Arts to re[turn home]

It disappeared early from view, but has served after Paul I's accession to the throne as a model for many artists, especially owing to the engraving by Ignaz Sebastian Klauber (1753/54-1817) that recorded the painting (1797). The portrait in the Kadriorg Art Museum represents Voille's type or may even have been painted by the artist himself. Paul held the portrait created in 1789 in high esteem, and after his accession to the throne in 1796 he had official portraits painted precisely after it. Käesoleval Peeter III portreel pole teada olevaid analooge, kuid mõõtude, käsitluslaadi, taustalahenduse ja ookerja sametiga kaetud hermeliinmantli poolest on ta Paul I portree vaieldamatu paarik.
Paul I, olles tõusnud 1796. a. troonile, kroonis kohe oma isa, 1762. a. tapetud Peeter III säilmed ning mattis need koos Katariina II-ga Petropavlovski katedraali. On tõenäone, et 1789. a. ei maalinud Voille mitte üksnes Pauli portreed, vaid ka selle paariku - Peeter III portree, võib-olla mõne miniatuuri järgi.
works.de:
This portrait of Peter III has no known analogues, but in terms of dimensions, manner of execution, background treatment, and the ochre velvet-covered ermine cloak, it is the undisputed pair to the portrait of Paul I.
Paul I, having ascended the throne in 1796, immediately had the remains of his father, Peter III, murdered in 1762, crowned, and buried them together with Catherine II in the Peter and Paul Cathedral. It is likely that in 1789 Voille painted not only the portrait of Paul, but also its pair – the portrait of Peter III, possibly after some miniature.

works.d: Keiser on kujutatud Preobraženski polgu mundris ja Püha Andrease ordeni lindiga ning hermeliinmantlis, millest paistab üle vasaku õla üsna vähe. Ikonograafiliselt on portree kõige lähemal J. G. Tannaueri täisfiguurportreele (1716, Moskva Kreml), kuid ei puudu kokkupuutepunktid ka L. Caravaque'i ("Peeter I Preobraženski polgu mundris", 1720. aastad, Venemaa Teaduste Akadeemia Presiidium, Moskva) ja I. N. Nikitini ("Peeter I", Riiklik Vene Muuseum, Peterburi) portreedega.
works.de: The Emperor is depicted in the uniform of the Preobrazhensky Regiment and with the ribbon of the Order of St. Andrew and an ermine cloak, of which very little shows over the left shoulder. Iconographically the portrait is closest to J. G. Tannauer's full-figure portrait (1716, Moscow Kremlin), but there are also points of contact with L. Caravaque's portrait ("Peter I in the Uniform of the Preobrazhensky Regiment", 1720s, Presidium of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow) and I. N. Nikitin's portrait ("Peter I", State Russian Museum, St. Petersburg).

works.d: Portree taustal ülal paremal kroon ja P. III. I. R. (Peter III Imperator Russiae). Keiser on kujutatud Püha Andrease ordeni lindi ja rinnatähega, ees ohvitseri rinnaplaat. Tüübilt on portree analoogiline täisfiguurportreega, mis kujutab äsja troonile tõusnud keisrit sõjaväelaagris (1762, Riiklik Vene Muuseum). Irina Mihhailovna Sahharova leiab oma Antropovi-monograafias (Moskva, 1974), et Peeter III-t sõjaväelaagris kujutav portree jäi signeerimata ja kunstniku ateljeesse keisri kiire surma tõttu; seda on maininud Antropov hilisemas palvekirjas Katariina II-le. Kolmnurkse mütsiga ning Preobraženski polgu keisri enda initsiatiivil uuendatud mundris esineb Peeter III ka mõnel teisel poolfiguur
works.de:
In the background of the portrait, upper right, a crown and P. III. I. R. (Peter III Imperator Russiae). The emperor is depicted with the ribbon and star of the Order of St. Andrew, and an officer's breastplate in front. In type the portrait is analogous to the full-length portrait
depicting the newly enthroned emperor in a military camp
(1762, State Russian Museum). Irina Mikhailovna Sakharova, in her Antropov monograph (Moscow, 1974), finds that the portrait depicting Peter III in a military camp remained unsigned and stayed in the artist's studio due to the emperor's sudden death; this has been mentioned by Antropov in a later petition to Catherine II. Wearing a tricorn hat and the uniform of the Preobrazhensky Regiment renewed on the emperor's own initiative, Peter III also appears in some other half-figure portrait

works.de:
Zarubin, Viktor (1866, Kharkov – 1928,
Leningrad). Graduated from the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics of Kharkov
University. From
1896 studied at the Petersburg Academy of Arts
in Arkhip Kuindzhi's landscape painting
class. In 1898 he graduated from the Academy of Arts
with the title of professional artist. In 1909
he was awarded the title of academician. In 1893–96 he lived
in Paris, where he studied at the Académie Julian under
Jules Joseph Lefebvre and Joseph Robert-
Fleury. Exhibited at the Paris Salon exhibitions.
Was a member of the Society of Russian Watercolourists,
from 1916 belonged to the Society of Wanderers (Peredvizhniki).
Also exhibited at the Academy of Arts'
Spring Exhibitions. In Soviet times worked
mainly on illustrating books.
His work shows a strong influence of the French
school of painting; also contemporary Russian artists

works.de:
Dubovskoy, Nikolai (1859, Novocherkassk
– 1918, Petrograd (Petersburg)).
Born into an ancient Cossack lineage, his father
was ataman of the Don Cossack Host. As a stipendiary
of the Don Cossack Host, he entered the Petersburg
Academy of Arts, where he studied under Mikhail
Clodt. Since Dubovskoy was not allowed to freely choose
the subject for the large gold medal competition painting,
he left the Academy of Arts in 1882. From 1884
he exhibited at the shows of the Society of Travelling Exhibitions.
After joining the society as a member
in 1886, he refrained from displaying his works
at other exhibitions. From 1895 he participated
in the work of the governing bodies of the Society of Travelling Exhibitions, reconciling
the elder and younger generations of the peredvizhniki. The artist's
work as a drawing teacher was significant. In 1898
he was awarded the title of academician

works.de: The Grand Duchess, later Empress, is depicted with the ribbon and star of the Grand Cross of the Order of St. Catherine. The portrait is based primarily on the full-length portrait by Alexander Roslin (1735-1808) (1777), which together with its pendant, the portrait of Grand Duke Pavel Petrovich (Paul I), is held in the State Hermitage. A number of half-figure portraits derive from this, the one closest to Roslin's being in the Vasily Tropinin Museum in Moscow. The oval portrait of Maria Fyodorovna (and its pendant, the portrait of Grand Duke Pavel Petrovich) painted by D. G. Levitsky (early 1780s), held in the Kuskovo State Ceramics Museum, also derives from Roslin's model, and has been copied by the famous engraver Gavriil Ivanovich Skorodumov (1754-1792) (Pavlovsk Palace Museum). works.de: Rizzoni, Aleksander (1836, Riga – 1902, Rome). Born into the family of an Italian merchant from Bologna who had settled in Riga. Brother of the artists Paul and Eduard Rizzoni. In the period 1852–62 studied at the Petersburg Academy of Arts under Bogdan (Gottfried) Willewalde. After 1866 lived permanently in Rome. The artist knew Pavel Tretyakov well, on whose commission he selected works of art for his collection. In 1866 was awarded the title of academician of the Academy of Arts, in 1868 the title of professor of painting. The range of subjects for his small genre paintings included small pictures of the life of Jews and Catholic clergy, everyday street life of Rome. The artist was deeply attached to the Eternal City. There are few artists in art history who [drew on] the subject matter of their works [in this way]

Makovsky, Vladimir (1846,
Moscow – 1920, Petrograd). Born into the family of
Yegor Makarov, a well-known Russian cultural figure and founder of the Moscow
School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture. In the years
1861–66 studied at the same school under Yevgraf Sorokin
and Sergei Zaryanko. In 1869 the Petersburg
Academy of Arts awarded him the title of free artist,
in 1873 the title of academician. He lived and worked
both in Moscow and in Petersburg. From 1893 a full member
of the Petersburg Academy of Arts, from 1894
a professor at the Academy of Arts. In the years
1894–96 rector of the Higher Art School
established at the Academy of Arts, and until 1918
also head of the genre painting studio.
Member of the Society of Travelling Exhibitions from 1872.

Arkhipov, Abram (1862, village of Yegorovo,
Ryazan governorate – 1930, Moscow).
Came from a peasant family in the Ryazan governorate.
He began his art studies with itinerant
icon painters, continuing in 1877 at the Moscow
School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture.
He studied there in 1877–83 and 1886–88 under Vasily
Perov, Vasily Polenov, Alexei Savrasov
and Vladimir Makovsky, and in 1884–86
studied at the Petersburg Academy of Arts. In 1887
he was awarded the large silver medal and the title of free artist
for the painting "Visiting the Sick".
In 1898 he was named academician.
From 1894 he worked for 25 years as head
of the life-study class at the Moscow School of Art.
In 1891 he joined the
Society of Travelling Exhibitions, exhibiting
paintings depicting peasant life. His 1896 journey to Europe

Milman, Adolf (1886, Chişinău – 1930,
Paris). Born into a large Jewish family.
In 1900 the family moved to Moscow, where he
entered the Moscow School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture.
From 1904 he studied in Ilya
Mashkov's studio, where he became friends with Robert
Falk and other future founders of the Knave of
Diamonds. From 1911 he was a member of the board of the Knave of
Diamonds group, exhibiting at their
exhibitions. In 1917 he left the association
and joined Mir Iskusstva. In 1912–17 he taught
at Mashkov's studio. In 1920 he fell ill
with encephalitis and, together with his French wife, moved
to Paris to be treated for it. In 1922 he
stopped painting, remaining paralyzed for the rest of his
life. Milman's work is poorly

the title of academician, and that same year he also

Kuna jäi varakult orvuks, oli sunnitud võõraste inimeste juures elades taluma alandusi, mis võisid mõjutada ta isiksuse kujunemist. Lihtrahva eluhoovuste pildikesi jäädvustas ta arvukates visandites. 1855. aastal alustas õpinguid Moskva maali-, skulptuuri- ja arhitektuurikoolis, kuhu võeti vastu igast seisuseist andekaid noori. works.de: Solomatkin, Leonid (1837, Sudzha, Kursk Governorate – 1883, St. Petersburg). Born into a poor peasant family. Having been orphaned early, he was forced to endure humiliations while living with strangers, which may have influenced the formation of his personality. He began his working life at the age of 13 as a shepherd and wagon driver in a trading caravan. Travelling around Russia, the young man saw declining villages, the urban poor, and human cruelty. He captured scenes from the life of common people in numerous sketches. In 1855 he began studies at the Moscow School of Painting, Sculpture and Architecture, which admitted talented young people from every estate. He went to live with the school's director N. pulm” ja 1. järgu kutselise kunstniku

regulaarselt osa kunstiakadeemia ja Peterburi
Kunstide Edendamise Seltsi näitustest.
Kuigi kunstnik töötas ka graafikuna,

kuulub vene realistliku maalikunsti
hilisemasse perioodi, mil impressionistide
loomingu olulisemaid väljendusvahendeid
– valgus ja värv, hakkasid mõjutama
realistide elulähedast kuju
works.de:
Golõnski, Vassili (1854, Beljaništši,
Tver Governorate – 1904). Studied successfully
in 1870–77 at the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts,
which he graduated with the composition "The Wedding
at Cana" and the title of first-class professional artist.
From 1880 he taught drawing at the
Kronstadt Realschule. He regularly took
part in exhibitions of the academy of arts and the St. Petersburg
Society for the Encouragement of the Arts.
Although the artist also worked as a graphic artist,
he is known mainly as a genre painter
who was particularly notable for works depicting
village life. "Grandfather with Grandchild"
belongs to the later period of Russian realist
painting, when the essential means of expression
of the Impressionists – light and colour – began
to influence the realists' lifelike depiction

works.de: In the ventilation opening of the hut's roof (formed by crossed rafters shaped like horse heads), a man's head, resting on his hands supporting his cheeks from both sides.

works.d: Ette paremale hüppav härg poolkülgvaates, pea pööratud alla, saba tõstetud.
works.de: A bull leaping forward to the right in half-side view, head turned down, tail raised.

works.d: Kaks seisvat meesfiguuri ülestõstetud parema käega vaates vasakule. All vasakul osa pöiast.
works.de: Two standing male figures with raised right hand, viewed to the left. Lower left part of a foot.

works.d:
Kolm seisvat meesfiguuri. Keskmine otse-, parempoolne vasakule vaates. Mõlemil parem käsi üles tõstetud. Vasakpoolne paremale vaates ja kaks kätt üles tõstetud.
Koosneb kolmest lahtisest lehest
works.de:
Three standing male figures. The middle one in frontal view, the one on the right facing left. Both have the right hand raised. The one on the left facing right with both hands raised.
Consists of three loose sheets

works.d: Mehe seisev figuur tagantvaates, jalad ära lõigatud paberilehe allservaga. Pea pöördes vasakule, mõlemad käed hoiavad paremal malakat. Lisaks kerge visand üksikust käest paremal.
works.de: A man's standing figure seen from behind, the legs cut off by the lower edge of the paper sheet. Head turned to the left, both hands holding a club on the right. In addition a light sketch of a single hand on the right.

works.d: Paremal künkal maja avatud ukse juures langetatud peaga põlvitav figuur. All vasakul mets. Üleval taevas üksikud tähed.
works.de: On the hill on the right, by the open door of a house, a kneeling figure with lowered head. Below on the left, a forest. Above in the sky, scattered stars.

works.d: Künkal viltuvajunud puutüve all istuv naisfiguur pea toetatud kätele, paremal kõrval maas kott. Üleval ja all üksikud langevad lehed.
works.de: Female figure sitting under a tree trunk slanted on a hill, head resting on hands, a bag on the ground to the right. Individual falling leaves above and below.

works.d: Kaks palja ülakehaga poollamavas asendis meesfiguuri. Parempoolsel vasak käsi tõstetud üle pea. Näod profiilis paremale.
works.de: Two male figures with bare upper bodies in a half-reclining position. The one on the right has his left hand raised above his head. Faces in profile facing right.

works.t: Mees mõõgaga. Visand teosele "Kalevipoeg Soome sepa juures"
works.d: Seisev meesfiguur otsevaates, paremas käes mõõk.
works.de: Standing male figure in frontal view, a sword in his right hand.

works.t: Mees mõõgaga. Visand teosele "Kalevipoeg Soome sepa juures"
works.d: Kaks seisvat meesfiguuri otsevaates (parempoolne väiksem) mõõgaga paremas käes. Suuremal vasak käsi hoogsalt ette toodud.
works.de: Two standing male figures in frontal view (the one on the right smaller) with a sword in the right hand. The larger figure's left hand brought forward energetically.

works.d: Kaks seisvat meesfiguuri otsevaates (parempoolne väiksem) mõõgaga paremas käes. Suuremal vasak käsi hoogsalt ette toodud.
works.de: Two standing male figures in frontal view (the one on the right smaller) with a sword in the right hand. The larger figure's left hand brought forward energetically.

works.d: Tugeva lapse alasti figuur poollamavas asendis toetumas paremale käele.
works.de: Naked figure of a sturdy child in a semi-reclining position, resting on the right hand.

works.d: Tugeva lapse figuur poollamavas asendis lauatükiga vasakus käes.
works.de: Sturdy child figure in a half-reclining position with a piece of a board in the left hand.

works.d: Neli (kaks ülal ja kaks all) istuvat naisfiguuri, pead profiilis vasakule alla.
works.de: Four (two above and two below) seated female figures, heads in profile facing down to the left.

works.d: Neli (kaks ülal ja kaks all) istuvat naisfiguuri, pead profiilis vasakule alla.
works.de: Four (two above and two below) seated female figures, heads in profile facing down to the left.

works.d: Selili lamav meesfiguur, vasak käsi asetatud pea alla, parem lebamas maapinnal.
works.de: Male figure lying on its back, left hand placed under the head, right hand resting on the ground.

works.d: Istuv naisfiguur alla paremale kallutatud peaga. Silmapiir madalal.
works.de: Seated female figure with head tilted down to the right. Low horizon.

works.d: Kaks kõrvuti istuvat naisfiguuri. Vasakpoolne vaatega paremala alla, vasak küünarnukk toetumas süles lebavale paremale käele. Parempoolne vaatega vasakule alla, käed asetatud risti sülle.
works.de: Two female figures sitting side by side. The left one facing down to the right, left elbow resting on the right hand lying in the lap. The right one facing down to the left, hands placed crossed in the lap.

works.d: Kolm seisvat meesfiguuri ülestõstetud parema ja keskele kokku asetatud vasaku käega.  All paremal varemed. Silmapiir madalal.
works.de: Three standing male figures with the raised right hand and the left hand brought together in the middle. Below, on the right, ruins. Low horizon.

works.d: Madalate pilvedega taeva taustal põlvili olev meesfiguur parema käe ja peaga toetumas kepile, vasaku käega maha.
works.de: Against a background of a sky with low clouds, a kneeling male figure supporting himself with his right hand and head on a staff, and with his left hand on the ground.

works.d: Madalate pilvedega taeva taustal põlvili olev meesfiguur parema käe ja peaga toetumas kepile, vasaku käega maha.
works.de: Against a background of a sky with low clouds, a kneeling male figure supporting himself with his right hand and head on a staff, and with his left hand on the ground.

works.d: Madalate pilvedega taeva taustal põlvili olev meesfiguur parema käe ja peaga toetumas kepile, vasaku käega maha.
works.de: Against a background of a sky with low clouds, a kneeling male figure supporting himself with his right hand and head on a staff, and with his left hand on the ground.

works.d: Sinise taeva taustal kolm tumedas riides harkisjalu seisvat meesfiguuri ülestõstetud parema käega. Vasak käsi keskmisel figuuril rinnale tõstetud, vasakpoolsel alla taha ja parempoolsele vasakule küljele üles tõstetud.
works.de: Against a blue sky background three male figures dressed in dark clothing, standing with legs apart, with the right arm raised. The left arm of the middle figure is raised to the chest, the left figure's is raised down and back, and the right figure's is raised up on the left side of the body.

works.d: Kolm seisvat meesfiguuri ülestõstetud parema käega. All paremal kiri: MEIE MAA / MULD / MEIE RAHVAS
works.de: Three standing male figures with raised right hand. Lower right text: MEIE MAA / MULD / MEIE RAHVAS

works.d: Kaks seisvat meesfiguuri ülestõstetud kätega ja vaatega paremale üles.
works.de: Two standing male figures with raised arms and gaze upward to the right.

works.d: Kolm seisvat meesfiguuri, kõigil parem käsi sirgelt üles sirutatud. Keskmine figuur otsevaates, kaks äärmist poolpöördes keskmise figuuri poole.
works.de: Three standing male figures, all with the right arm stretched straight up. The middle figure in front view, the two outer ones in half-turn towards the middle figure.

works.d: Kahe mehe figuurid (ülestõstetud parema käega), kolm käte, kaks jala, pea ja näo (osaline) kujutised
works.de: Figures of two men (with raised right hand), depictions of three hands, two legs, a head and a (partial) face

works.d: Seisva meesfiguuri (ülestõstetud parema käega), kahe käe (üks koos õlaga) ja nelja jala kujutised.
works.de: Depictions of a standing male figure (with the right hand raised), of two hands (one with a shoulder), and of four legs.

works.d: Kolm meesfiguuri ülestõstetud kätega (käed jäävad osaliselt lehelt välja). Jalgade kontuurid vähe nähtavad (kustutatud).
works.de: Three male figures with raised arms (the arms partly extend beyond the sheet). The outlines of the legs are barely visible (erased).

works.t: Paberirulli hoidvad käed / Käed. Visandid teosele "Viru vanne"
works.d:
a) Kolm kätt paberirulliga peos ja jalg tagantvaates.

b) Üleval vasakul ülestõstetud käsi, allpool kolm rusikasse surutud käe kujutist.
works.de:
a) Three hands with a paper roll in hand and a foot in rear view.

b) Upper left a raised hand, below it three depictions of a clenched fist.

works.t: Paberirulli hoidvad käed / Poolfiguur. Visandid teosele "Viru vanne"
works.d:
a) Kaks kätt paberirulliga peos. 

b) Poolfiguur tõstetud käega ja eraldi käekujutis.
works.de:
a) Two hands holding a roll of paper. 

b) Half-figure with a raised hand and a separate depiction of a hand.

works.d: Kolm seisvat meesfiguuri ülestõstetud kätega (käega osaliselt paberilt välja jäänud). Pea õlaga. Rusikas käsi.
works.de: Three standing male figures with raised arms (arm partially cut off by the edge of the paper). Head with shoulder. Fist hand.

works.d:
a) Kolm seisvat meesfiguuri, vasakpoolne ülestõstetud kätega vaates paremale, parempoolsed ülestõstetud parema käega vaates vasakule. 

b) Kolme figuuri kujutised.
works.de:
a) Three standing male figures, the left one with raised hands seen facing right, the right ones with raised right hand seen facing left.

b) Depictions of three figures.

works.d: Paremal kolm seisvat meesfiguuri ülessirutatud parema käega (käed osaliselt paberilt välja jäänud).
works.de: On the right, three standing male figures with raised right hand (hands partially outside the sheet).

works.d:
Ruudustikuga kaetud paberil kolm seisvat meesfiguuri, vasakpoolne välja joonistamata, parempoolsed ülessirutatud parema käega vaates vasakule.
All raskesti loetav tekst: FÜR ME... UND GERECHTIGKEIT
works.de:
On paper covered with a grid, three standing male figures, the one on the left not fully drawn, the ones on the right with the right arm raised, viewed toward the left.
Below, hard-to-read text: FÜR ME... UND GERECHTIGKEIT

works.d: Seisev mees ülestõstetud parema käega.
works.de: Standing man with his right hand raised.

works.d: Kaks seisvat meesfiguuri ülestõstetud kätega (parempoolsest figuurist osa paberilt välja jäänud).
works.de: Two standing male figures with raised arms (part of the right-hand figure left out of the paper).

works.d: Kaks seisvat meesfiguuri ülestõstetud kätega (parempoolsest figuurist osa paberilt välja jäänud).
works.de: Two standing male figures with raised arms (part of the right-hand figure left out of the paper).

works.d: Paremal ristkülikukujulisel tumedamal pinnal seisev meesfiguur ülestõstetud kätega.
works.de: On the right, on a rectangular darker surface, a standing male figure with raised arms.

works.d:
Vasakul seisev meesfiguur ülestõstetud parema käega. Fragmendid: kaks ülestõstetud käsivart, nende vahel pea, käsivars, kukal ja jalg.
All vasakul K. Raua tekst: See seisak
works.de:
Male figure standing on the left with the right hand raised. Fragments: two raised arms, between them a head, an arm, the back of the head and a leg.
Lower left, text by K. Raud: See seisak

works.d: Harkisjalu ja kummargil seisva meesfiguuri pool külgvaates vasakule, käed viidud vasakule umbes rinna kõrgusele. Labajalad joonistamata.
works.de: A half-view to the left of a man standing with legs apart and stooping, hands brought to the left approximately to chest height. Feet not drawn.

works.d: Harkisjalu seisev meesakt (poiss) otsevaates, pea pööratud vasakule alla.
works.de: Standing male nude (boy) with legs apart, frontal view, head turned down to the left.

works.d: Istuv figuur otsevaates ülestõstetud kätega sülesoleva kandle kohal.
works.de: Sitting figure in frontal view with raised hands over a kannel resting on the lap.

works.d:
a) Vasakul peopesadega kokkuasetatud ja ülestõstetud käed, vasak käsi otsevaates. Paremal samad käed näole asetatud, vasak käsi poolkülgvaates.

b) Visandid taluhoonetest.
works.de:
a) On the left, hands placed together palm to palm and raised, the left hand in front view. On the right, the same hands placed on the face, the left hand in half-profile view.

b) Sketches of farm buildings.

works.d: Mööda teed alt vasakult ülesse paremale astuvad figuurid tagantvaates.
works.de: Figures walking along a road from lower left to upper right, seen from behind.

works.d: Ees paremal istuv ja lamav figuur ning keskel kaks lamavat figuuri. Tagaplaanil puutüved ja tara.
works.de: In front on the right a sitting and a lying figure, and in the middle two lying figures. In the background tree trunks and a fence.

works.d: Seisev koerataoline loom külgvaates vasakule, pea keeratud paremale.
works.de: Standing dog-like animal in side view facing left, head turned to the right.

works.d: Maast üles tõusev tiibadega ja väikese lapsega süles naise figuur külgvaates vasakule. Paremal põõsas ja madalal silmapiiril kolm puud.
works.de: A winged female figure rising from the ground with a small child in her lap, in side view to the left. On the right a bush and on the low horizon three trees.

works.dm: lehe kõrgus: 80.0 cm; kujutise kõrgus: 54.0 cm; kujutise kõrgus: 56.0 cm; lehe laius: 75.0 cm
works.d: Sinistes toonides kujutatud kõnnivad mehe tänaval, grupp vasakul vaataja poole ja paremal - liigub eemale. Kolmel käes paberisarnane objekt, kahel mehel pikad juuksed ja teksasarnased püksid
works.de: In blue tones, men are depicted walking on the street, a group on the left facing the viewer and on the right - moving away. Three are holding a paper-like object, two men have long hair and jeans-like trousers

works.d: Lehe keskel avatud raamat. Selle taga ristatud labidas ja tõrvik. Kiri: "KILLIPE" (ülalt alla paremal all)
works.de: In the middle of the sheet an open book. Behind it a crossed spade and a torch. Inscription: "KILLIPE" (from top to bottom, lower right)

works.d: Lehe keskel kandle kujutis. Kandlel istub laululind, kahel pool kannelt kiri: Siuru. Kandle all rannal istuva rahvariides naise figuur eestvaates, pea toetatud kätele.
works.de: In the middle of the sheet the depiction of a kannel [zither]. A songbird sits on the kannel, on both sides of the kannel the text: Siuru. Below the kannel the figure of a woman in folk costume sitting on the shore, seen frontally, head resting on her hands.

works.d: Vasakul tumedas rüüs meesfiguur otsevaates pika maha toetuva odaga paremas käes. Pea ümber nimbus
works.de: On the left a male figure in dark robes, in frontal view, with a long spear resting on the ground in his right hand. A nimbus around the head

works.d: Lehe ülaosas käsi hoidmas küünlajalga küünlaga paberirull. All käsi hoidmas küünlajalga põleva küünlaga, vasakule jääb väike büst, selle all kirjutav käsi sulega. Pöördelt kumavad motiivid ähmastavad kujutatut.
works.de: In the upper part of the sheet a hand holding a candlestick with a candle and a roll of paper. Below a hand holding a candlestick with a burning candle, to the left a small bust, below it a writing hand with a pen. Motifs showing through from the verso blur the depiction.

works.d: Punase pliiatsiga visandatud voor viiest kahehobuse vankrist diagonaalselt lehe vasakust alanurgast parema serva keskele ja sealt ülaserva vasakusse nurka. Välja joonistatud 4 paari hobuseid ja 5 vankrit.
works.de: A convoy of five two-horse carts sketched in red pencil, diagonally from the lower left corner of the sheet to the middle of the right edge and from there to the upper left corner. 4 pairs of horses and 5 carts drawn in outline.

works.d: Pingil istuv paljasjalgne kõrvu katvate sirgete juustega meesfiguur hoiab keppi; teine paljasjalgne meesfiguur ustub maapinnal, käed lõua alla kokku pandud
works.de: A barefoot male figure with straight hair covering the ears sits on a bench holding a cane; another barefoot male figure sits on the ground, hands clasped under the chin

works.d: Seisva naise figuur ette vöökohale kokku asetatud kätega külgvaates vasakule. Temast paremal istub kass.
works.de: The figure of a standing woman with hands folded at waist level, in side view facing left. To her right sits a cat.

works.d: Keskel raamistuses seisva pikas kleidis naise figuur profiilis paremale, vasak käsi tõstetud, hoiab lille, parem käsi küünarnukist kõverdatud, hoiab lehte (raamatut?). Figuuri kohal kiri: EX LIBRIS. Raamistuse paremas ülanurgas päike, paremas alanurgas kolme õiega taim.
works.de: In the centre, within a frame, the figure of a woman in a long dress standing in profile to the right, left hand raised, holding a flower, right hand bent at the elbow, holding a leaf (a book?). Above the figure, the inscription: EX LIBRIS. In the upper right corner of the frame, a sun, in the lower right corner, a plant with three blossoms.

works.d: Lehe keskel raamistuses ovaal, milles asub küünlajalas põlev küünal kiirtega ümber leegi. Ovaali peal kiri: "EX LIBRIS", ovaali all: "ANTON RAS KÜÜNALT".
works.de: In the centre of the sheet, an oval within a frame, containing a candle burning in a candlestick with rays around the flame. Above the oval, an inscription: "EX LIBRIS", below the oval: "ANTON RAS KÜÜNALT".

works.d: Mustal põhjal helendavas nimbuses kroon, selle ümber on keerdunud madu.
works.de: On a black background, in a glowing nimbus a crown, around it a coiled snake.

works.d: Neli hõbedast ja kaks musta rinnanõela. Rinnanõelade peadeks stiliseeritud akantusemotiivid. Paigutatud on kahele poole kahte üksteise all asetsevat musta rinnanõela kaks üksteise all asetsevat hõbedast.
works.de: Four silver and two black brooches. The heads of the brooches feature stylised acanthus motifs. They are arranged with two black brooches placed one under the other on either side, and two silver brooches placed one under the other.

works.d: Keskel väänlevate kroonlehtedega kibuvitsaõit meenutav õis. Kahel poolt õit oksakesed lehtedega. Kummalgil oksal fantaasialind pika sabaga.
works.de: In the centre, a blossom reminiscent of a wild rose with twisting petals. On both sides of the blossom, twigs with leaves. On each twig a fantasy bird with a long tail.

works.d:
Keskel seisva otsevaates rahvariides naise figuur. Temast kummalgi pool pihlakalehtedest ornament. Ornamendi all visandlikke motiive rahvusliku lillkirja meenutavatest stiliseeritud lilledest. Ornamendi all paremal Kr Raua kiri: Kavand Tallinna Eesti muuseumi eluaegsete liikmete diplomile. 
Selle all tähed: I, E, M
works.de:
In the centre the figure of a woman in national costume standing in frontal view. On either side of her an ornament of rowan leaves. Below the ornament sketch-like motifs of stylised flowers reminiscent of national floral embroidery. Below the ornament on the right an inscription by Kr. Raud: Design for the diploma of lifelong members of the Estonian Museum in Tallinn.
Below that the letters: I, E, M

works.d: Tumesinisel põhjal keskel kuldne loorberipärg, selle kohal hajali 9 hõbedast tähekest + 1 täheke pärja sees. Pärja alaosast jääb kahele poole punaste tähtedega kiri: PÖRMUST TÄH - TEDE POOLE. Kahel pool kirja stiliseeritud lained. Ümber lipu tumesinise põhja kitsas must rant.
works.de: On a dark blue background, in the middle a golden laurel wreath, above it 9 scattered silver stars + 1 star inside the wreath. From the lower part of the wreath, on both sides, an inscription in red letters remains: PÖRMUST TÄH - TEDE POOLE [FROM DUST TO THE STARS]. On both sides of the inscription, stylised waves. Around the flag's dark blue background, a narrow black border.

works.d: Hobuse (külgvaates paremale) seljas istuv meesfiguur otsevaates, koti ja mõõgaga vasakus käes vilja külvamas.
works.de: A male figure sitting on a horse (in side view facing right) shown frontally, with a bag and a sword in his left hand, sowing grain.

works.d: Tumedal aluspõhjal ribaornament neliksiirkujulistest kookidest keskel ja neist üleval ja all terakestest sik-sak ribad.
works.de: On a dark background, a band ornament of rhombus-shaped cakes in the middle, with zigzag bands of grains above and below them.

works.d: Motiiv veetaimedest. Keskel viis mõikakujulist õit varte otsas, neist kummalgi pool kolm pikka lehte, all narmakujulised juured.
works.de: A motif of aquatic plants. In the middle five bell-shaped flowers at the ends of stems, on either side of them three long leaves, at the bottom fringe-like roots.

works.d: Kavandi keskel raamistuses istuva naise figuur, raamistuse kohal kroon. Vasakul äärel kuus stiliseeritud kuusekest.
works.de: In the centre of the design a figure of a seated woman within a frame, above the frame a crown. On the left edge six stylised fir trees.

works.d: U 2/3 lehepinnast täidab raamis visand. Üleval kiri: ExLIBRIS KARL ILLIPE. Selle all avatud raamat kahe 8-harulise tärni vahel. Raamatu all vasakult paremale põlvele toetuv meesfiguur suunaga paremale, hoiab ees mõlema käega tõrvikut. Paremal kummardav naisfiguur suunaga vasakule, hoiab mõlema käega põlevat tõrvikut mehe kustunud tõrviku poole alla.
works.de: About 2/3 of the sheet's surface is filled by a sketch in a frame. At the top the inscription: ExLIBRIS KARL ILLIPE. Below it an open book between two 8-pointed stars. Below the book, from left to right, a male figure resting on his knee, facing right, holding a torch in front with both hands. On the right a bowing female figure facing left, holding a burning torch with both hands downward towards the man's extinguished torch.

works.d: Lehe pinnal hajali ringikujulised motiivid (3 ringi ja üks poolik ring). Ringid on täidetud stiliseeritud õite ja lehekestega.
works.de: Scattered circular motifs on the surface of the sheet (3 circles and one partial circle). The circles are filled with stylised flowers and leaves.

works.d: Kahe küünlaalusega  lühter moodustab väikese kumerusega looga. Keskelt otse üles suundub stiliseeritud kuuse kujulise ülaosaga kaunistus.
works.de: A chandelier with two candle-holders forms an arch with a slight curvature. From the middle, straight upward, extends a decoration with a stylised fir-tree-shaped upper part.

works.d: Lehe keskel horisontaalselt vibu, vibunöör allapoole. Vibule risti asetatud nool.
works.de: Horizontally in the middle of the sheet a bow, bowstring facing downward. An arrow placed crosswise on the bow.

works.d: Esiplaanil olnud figuur (Kalevipoeg) välja lõigatud. Lainete taolised moodustised suunduvad diagonaalselt alt paremalt üles vasakule. Üleval paremal lõke ja selle taga paremal istuv (põlvili) naisfiguur poolkülgvaates paremale, käed asetatud sülle.
works.de: The figure that was in the foreground (Kalevipoeg) has been cut out. Wave-like formations proceed diagonally from lower right to upper left. Upper right a bonfire, and behind it on the right a sitting (kneeling) female figure in half side view to the right, hands placed in her lap.

works.d: Mustal aluspõhjal ribakujuline ornament kolmiklehtedest ja marjadest. Iga kolmiklehe südamikus kolm marja.
works.de: On a black background, a band-shaped ornament of trefoil leaves and berries. In the core of each trefoil leaf, three berries.

works.d: Mustal aluspõhjal ribakujuline ornament kolmiklehtedest ja marjadest. Iga kolmiklehe juurde kuulub kolm marja lehe kaenaldes.
works.de: Band-shaped ornament of trefoil leaves and berries on a black ground. Each trefoil leaf has three berries in the axils of the leaf.

works.d: Tumepunasel põhjal keskel roosa kibuvitsaõis roheliste lehtede raamistuses. Selle all kuldne kiri: KAARLI KOGUDUSE ERAÜHISGÜMNAASIUM.
works.de: In the center on a dark red ground, a pink dog-rose flower framed by green leaves. Below it golden text: KAARLI KOGUDUSE ERAÜHISGÜMNAASIUM.

works.d: Ühte küünalt hoidvat lühtrit ümbritsevad neli stiliseeritud hobusepead, mis lähevad üle neljaks kaardus jalaks.
works.de: A chandelier holding a single candle is surrounded by four stylised horse heads, which turn into four curved legs.

works.d: Keskel raamistuses istuv naisfiguur käsipõsakil triibulises seelikus. Tema kohal sammastel girlandid, mida hoiab koos põlvitav meesakt. Kavandi äärtes maleruudulised draperiid, all maleruuduline ristkülik.
works.de: In the centre, within a frame, a seated female figure resting her cheek on her hand, wearing a striped skirt. Above her, garlands on columns held together by a kneeling male nude. At the edges of the design chequered draperies, at the bottom a chequered rectangle.

works.d: Kolm põlvitavat meesfiguuri otsevaates. Vasakpoolsel käed ripuvad mööda külgi alla, keskmisel käed tõstetud kokku rinna kõrgusele ja parempoolsel käed asetatud risti rinnale. Foonil tähed.
works.de: Three kneeling male figures in frontal view. On the left figure the arms hang down along the sides, on the middle figure the hands are raised together to chest height, and on the right figure the arms are placed crossed over the chest. Stars in the background.

works.d: Tütarlapse ettesirutatud kätel kandik marjadega ja tema järel kõndiva poisi (mõlemas käes lilled) figuurid külgvaates vasakule.
works.de: Figures of a girl with a tray of berries held out on her hands, and behind her a walking boy (with flowers in both hands), in side view facing left.

works.d: Sammuv meesfiguur palkidega paremal õlal, käed asetatud ette palkidele külgvaates vasakule.
works.de: Walking male figure with logs on the right shoulder, hands placed in front on the logs, side view to the left.

works.d: Lehe ülaäärt ja paremat serva mööda stiliseeritud lilledest rahvuslik ornament.
works.de: Along the upper edge and right side of the sheet, a national ornament of stylised flowers.

works.d: Lehe keskel kaunistusteta küünlajalg kahe võrdse haruga horisontaalselt paremale ja vasakule. Keskel alt ahenev jalg, mis toetub kumerale alusele.
works.de: In the middle of the sheet, an undecorated candlestick with two equal branches horizontally to the right and left. In the middle, a leg narrowing from below, resting on a curved base.

works.d: Rinnanõela pea figuraalne. Kahe kaelapidi ühendatud väljapoole pööratud hobusepea all on hammastatud ratta kujutis. Seda ümbritsevad kolmnurkse raamistusena neli hobusejalga. Kõige all pikk nõel teravikuga alla.
works.de: The head of a brooch is figural. Below two outward-turned horse heads joined at the neck is a depiction of a gear wheel. This is surrounded by four horse legs forming a triangular frame. At the very bottom a long pin with the point downward.

works.d: Stiliseeritud laevakujutise keskel tähed: EP. Nende kohal üles suunatud nool selle ümber keerdunud 2 maoga ja 2 stiliseeritud kotkaga. Noole kohal hobuserauakujuline lint tekstiga: Estonian Produce.
works.de: In the centre of a stylised depiction of a ship, the letters: EP. Above them an upward-pointing arrow entwined with 2 snakes and 2 stylised eagles. Above the arrow a horseshoe-shaped ribbon with the text: Estonian Produce.

works.d: Väga massiivne kapp rikkalikult kaunistatud karniisiga. Ukse ülaosas krooni kujutis, ülanurkades stiliseeritud taimemotiivid. Ukse keskel kivil istuva naise figuur, pea langetatud vasakule õlale. Ukse allosas stiliseeritud taimeornament, jalad massiivsed.
works.de: A very massive cabinet with a richly decorated cornice. At the top of the door, a depiction of a crown, in the upper corners stylised plant motifs. In the centre of the door, a figure of a woman sitting on a stone, head lowered onto the left shoulder. At the bottom of the door, a stylised plant ornament, massive legs.

works.d: Alt paremalt kõrgemale vasakule suunduvate paralleeljoonte vahel (teel) kõnnib kübaraga ja kepiga väike kühmus meesfiguur poolselgvaates vasakule. Teise paari alt vasakult üles paremale suunduvate paralleeljoonte vahel vasakul seisab suur pikas riietuses meesfiguur poolkülgvaates paremale näidates parema langetatud käega alla ja vasaku ülestõstetud käega üles.
works.de: Between parallel lines (a road) running from lower right to upper left, a small hunched male figure with a hat and a cane walks in a half-back view to the left. Between another pair of parallel lines running from lower left to upper right, on the left stands a large male figure in long clothing, in a half-side view to the right, showing downward with his lowered right hand and upward with his raised left hand.

works.d: Seisev naisfiguur otsevaates pikas tumedas rüüs , paljajalu ja pikkade lahtiste juustega. Juuste varjust ette ulatuvad kokku pandud käed hoiavad valget rätikut.
works.de: Standing female figure in frontal view, in a long dark robe, barefoot and with long loose hair. Clasped hands emerging from the shadow of the hair in front hold a white cloth.

works.t: Pühapäeval. Puhkavad ja vestlevad talumehed rannal
works.d: Seitse maapinnal lamavat ja üks maapinnal istuv meesfiguur

works.d: Ebamäärase kujuga mustal foonil tihedalt erikujulisi lillekesi ja tähekesi. Lilled ja tähed jäetud foonist heledamaks.
works.de: On a black background of indeterminate shape, densely packed flowers and stars of various shapes. The flowers and stars are left lighter than the background.

works.d: Põlvitav meesfiguur, peopesad asetatud kokku õlgade kõrgusele. Põlvede ees maas kübar.
works.de: Kneeling male figure, palms placed together at shoulder height. A hat on the ground in front of the knees.

works.d: Lehe keskel musta tušiga joonistatud oksake loorberipärjast.
works.de: A small laurel-wreath branch drawn in black ink in the middle of the sheet.

works.d: Kaks muinas aegset sõjakirvest, terad sissepoole. Pikad varred diagonaalis, alaosad lähenevad teineteisele.
works.de: Two ancient battle-axes, blades facing inward. Long shafts diagonal, the lower parts approaching each other.

works.d: Paremal seisev figuur pikas tumedas riietuses, käed tõstetud kahele poole põski.
works.de: Figure standing on the right in long dark clothing, hands raised to both sides of the face.

works.d: Massiivse kolmnurkadest ornamendi raamistuses istuv naisfiguur käsipõsakil, pea kallutatud vasakule õlale.
works.de: In a frame of massive triangular ornament, a seated female figure with her cheek resting on her hand, head tilted onto the left shoulder.

works.d: Pingil istuv meesfiguur otsevaates ette maha; Parem küünarnukiga paremale põlvele toetuv käsi on asetatud paremale põsele.
works.de: A male figure sitting on a bench, in frontal view looking down; the right hand, with the elbow resting on the right knee, is placed on the right cheek.

works.d: Rinnanõela pea moodustab keeritsakujuline motiiv kolmest hobusepeast. Ülemine (keskmine) hobusepea, pöördes vasakule, temast paremal ja vasakul lehviv lint, vasakpoolne pea pööratud üles, kaela ja rinnanõele nõela vahel kuueharuline täheke.
works.de: The head of the brooch forms a spiral-shaped motif of three horse heads. The upper (middle) horse head, turning to the left, with a ribbon fluttering to its right and left, the left-hand head turned upward, between the neck and the brooch pin a six-pointed little star.

works.d: Rinnanõela pea moodustub kahest kaelapidi koos olevast väljapoole pööratud hobusepeast, mille all on paar koonjaid ülespööratud tiibu. Peade kohal on tähed: T, E, M (ülevalt alla). Kogu motiivi all pikk nõel, teravik otse alla suunatud.
works.de: The head of the brooch is formed from two outward-turned horse heads joined at the neck, below which is a pair of conical upturned wings. Above the heads are the letters: T, E, M (from top to bottom). Below the whole motif a long pin, the point directed straight down.

works.d:
Vasakul ettepoole kummarduv seisev meesakt poolkülgvaates paremale. Paremas käes lill. Pea ümber oreool.
All keskel K. Raua käega: MU KAITSEVAIM
works.de:
On the left, a standing male nude bending forward, in semi-profile view to the right. A flower in the right hand. A halo around the head.
Below, in the centre, in K. Raud's hand: MU KAITSEVAIM

works.d: Maha paremale põlvele toetuv meesfiguur, parem käsi asetatud rinnale, vasak üles tõstetud, poolkülgvaates paremale. Foonil üksikud tähed, paremal kuu.
works.de: A male figure resting on the ground on his right knee, right hand placed on the chest, left hand raised, in half-profile facing right. In the background scattered stars, on the right the moon.

works.d: Seisev meesfiguur ruudulise kostüümiga tagantvaates ülestõstetud parema käega.
works.de: Standing male figure in checkered costume, in back view, with the right hand raised.

works.d: Maas istuva meesfiguur poolkülgvaates vasakule, parema käe küünarnukk toetumas paremale põlvele, pea samale käele, vasak käsi alla vasakule jalale. Üleval paremal naisfiguur eskiislikumalt ja väiksemas formaadis.
works.de: A male figure sitting on the ground in half-side view to the left, the elbow of the right arm resting on the right knee, the head on the same hand, the left arm down towards the left leg. Above on the right a female figure in a more sketch-like manner and smaller format.

works.d: Noore pikajuukselise mehe poolakt 1/3 pöördes paremale. Vasak käsi tõstetud sirgelt üles, parem käsi sirutatud alla vasakule toetamaks keha. Suu avatud. Figuur asetseb lehe vasakpoolses osas, lehe alumine serv pisut allpool vöökohta.
works.de: A half-length nude of a young long-haired man in a 1/3 turn to the right. The left arm raised straight up, the right arm stretched down to the left to support the body. Mouth open. The figure is located in the left part of the sheet, the lower edge of the sheet slightly below waist level.

works.d:
a) Madalal künkal kahe puude grupi vahel madal õlgkatusega talumaja.

b) Üleval ait aiaväravaga, all vinnaga kaev ja õlgkatusega talumaja. Signatuur all parema: K. RAUD. Lm 21,1x17,4
works.de:
a) On a low hillock between two groups of trees a low straw-roofed farmhouse.

b) Above a barn with a gate in the fence, below a well with a sweep and a straw-roofed farmhouse. Signature lower right: K. RAUD. Sheet size 21.1x17.4

In the background on the left a lying figure in side view to the left and on the right a seated figure in back view. All wearing headgear.

works.d: Künkal istuv pikas riietuses figuur kannelt mängimas. Kannel püsti süles. Ees maas kasvavad üksikud lilled.
works.de: A figure in long garments sitting on a hill playing the kannel. The kannel upright on the lap. Below on the ground grow scattered flowers.

works.d: Osa istuva mehe kolmveerandfiguurist poolselgvaates paremale; parem käsi asetatud paremale põsele; küünarnukk toetumas põlvele.
works.de: Part of a three-quarter figure of a seated man in half back-view facing right; right hand placed on the right cheek; elbow resting on the knee.

works.d: Istuv tüdruk rätikuga peas ja sülle asetatud kätega otsevaates.
works.de: A seated girl with a kerchief on her head and her hands placed in her lap, in frontal view.

works.d: Lehe ülemise kolmandiku täidab tume stiliseeritud akantuselehe kujuline nõelapea. Selle all jäme nõel suunaga alla.
works.de: The upper third of the sheet is filled by a dark needle head shaped like a stylised acanthus leaf. Below it a thick needle pointing downward.

works.d: Ornamendi keskel ristikukujuliselt asetatud nelja lehe keskel südamik. Lehtede ümber ornament marjadest (?) ümardatud nurkadega mustall ruudukujulisel alusel.
works.de: In the centre of the ornament, a core placed amid four leaves arranged in a cross shape. Around the leaves an ornament of berries (?) on a black square base with rounded corners.

works.d: Kolmel astmel viilja ülaosaga nelinurkse alaosaga monument. Nelinurkse osa keskel raamistuses põlvitav akt (toetub vasakule põlvele) pöördes vasakule, pea kallutatud paremale. Mõlema käega hoiab paremal õla kõrgusel maski. Viilul kiri: KRISTIAI ALETMAN
works.de: A monument on three steps with a triangular upper part and a rectangular lower part. In the middle of the rectangular part, within a frame, a kneeling nude (resting on the left knee), turned to the left, head tilted to the right. Holding a mask with both hands at right shoulder height. Inscription on the pediment: KRISTIAI ALETMAN

works.d: Keset lehte lihtne baasita sammas kanellüüridega. Kapiteel laineliste motiividega kaunistatud.
works.de: In the middle of the sheet a simple baseless column with fluted shafts. Capital decorated with wave motifs.

works.d: Lehe alumisest servast algav servaga allapool küünarliigesest äralõigatud käsi kaldu paremale. Käsi hoiab suurt kiirgavat kalliskivi.
works.de: A hand cut off below the elbow, edge starting from the bottom edge of the sheet, leaning to the right. The hand holds a large radiant gem.

works.d: Künkal, osalise vikerkaare all. Teineteise käest kinnihoidva naise ja lapse figuurid tagantvaates.
works.de: On a hill, under a partial rainbow. Rear view of figures of a woman and a child holding each other's hands.

works.de: Raul Meel represents the radical wing of Estonian art renewal of the 1970s–1980s and is known as the most famous autodidact and outsider in Estonian art. Meel's desire to speak the same language as Western art renewal meant renouncing the customary possibilities and signifiers that had grown out of the Estonian art system itself. An artist with an engineering background, he began in 1970 a dialogue between art and exact science, which paved the way for the arrival of the conceptualist notion of art in Estonia and proved that visual art too is capable of reflecting the spiritually complex problems brought about by contemporary developments. works.d:
Valik eesti kunsti ühe klassiku, varase naiskunstniku Salome Trei (1905-1995) 1944.-1960. aastal valminud teostest avardab ülevaadet tema vähetuntud, Teise maailmasõja järgsest loominguperioodist.
Kuressaarest pärit Salome Trei õppis 1929-1934 Tallinnas Riigi Kunsttööstuskoolis graafikat ja lõpetas kooli 6-aastase kursuse cum laude. Seejärel õppis Trei Tartus Pallases, mille lõpetas 1939. aasta lennus.
Kunstnik emigreerus Eestist 1944. Viibinud Saksamaal DP-laagrites, elas ta hilisperioodil USA-s, kus tegutses peamiselt rakenduskunstnikuna, luues tekstiili ja tarbegraafika kujundusi erinevatele firmadele.
works.de:
A selection of works created between 1944 and 1960 by one of the classics of Estonian art, an early female artist Salome Trei (1905-1995), expands the overview of her lesser-known post-World War II creative period.
Salome Trei, born in Kuressaare, studied graphic art in Tallinn at the State School of Arts and Crafts from 1929 to 1934, and finished the 6-year course cum laude. She then studied at Pallas in Tartu, which she completed in the 1939 graduating class.
The artist emigrated from Estonia in 1944. Having stayed in DP camps in Germany, she later lived in the USA, where she worked mainly as an applied artist, creating textile and commercial graphic designs for various companies.

works.d: Visandi näol on tegemist eeltööga Vive Tolli 1960. aasta gravüürile "Võrguparandajad eided". Autori sõnul on visand tehtud Toila rannas, kiirelt skitseeritud tabavad joonistused iseloomustavad kunstniku tööstiili. Visandil on ka elemendid, mida lõppteosel pole (koer, mehed). Randlaste töö teemal valminud akvatintagravüür "Võrguparandajad eided" on suurepärane näide Vive Tolli varasest käekirjas omas ajastus.
works.de: The sketch is a preliminary work for Vive Tolli's 1960 print "Võrguparandajad eided" ["Old Women Mending Nets"]. According to the artist, the sketch was made on the beach at Toila; the quickly sketched, striking drawings characterise the artist's working style. The sketch also contains elements not found in the final work (a dog, men). The aquatint print "Võrguparandajad eided", created on the theme of the work of coastal dwellers, is an excellent example of Vive Tolli's early style of her time.

works.d:
Vive Tolli (sünd. 1928), üks eesti tunnustatumaid graafikuid, on EKM kogus oma varasemate teostega piisavalt hästi esindatud. Kuid tema hilisperioodist, pärast 1991. aastat loodud graafikast, on muuseumisse omandatud ainult mõned 1990.-2000. aastate tööd. Neile on „Vähe viltune kellatorn“ suurepäraseks täienduseks. 
Teos ei kujuta Pisa katedraali kampaniili, vaid meenutab fakti, et peaaegu kõik kirikutornid on pisut viltu. Gravüüri vasakpoolses osas on Tolli varasemate tööde elemente, sh maagilisi märke, paekivimustreid, peremärke jne. Lääne-Euroopa lahtiste rõdudega gooti arhitektuur on seotud geomeetriliste märkide ja eesti rahvusvärvidega meisterlikuks tervikuks.
works.de:
Vive Tolli (b. 1928), one of the most acclaimed Estonian graphic artists, is sufficiently well represented in the EKM collection with her earlier works. However, from her later period, graphic art created after 1991, only a few works from the 1990s–2000s have been acquired by the museum. „Vähe viltune kellatorn“ is an excellent addition to these. 
The work does not depict the campanile of Pisa Cathedral, but rather recalls the fact that almost all church towers are slightly tilted. In the left part of the print there are elements from Tolli's earlier works, including magical signs, limestone patterns, family marks, etc. Western European Gothic architecture with open balconies is combined with geometric signs and Estonian national colors into a masterful whole.

works.d: 1923. aasta detsembris esietendus Draamastuudio I lennu mängitud August Stridbergi näidend „Tontide sonaat“ („Spöksonaten“, 1907). Lavastajaks oli Paul Sepp, kunstnikuks Peet Aren. Lavastusele loodud kostüümi- ning lavakujundused annavad iseloomulikult edasi 1920. aastate kunsti- ja teatrimaastikku kujundanud ekspressionismi mõjusid.
works.de: In December 1923 the play by August Strindberg "The Ghost Sonata" ("Spöksonaten", 1907), performed by the first graduating class of the Drama Studio, had its premiere. The director was Paul Sepp, the artist Peet Aren. The costume and stage designs created for the production characteristically convey the influences of expressionism that shaped the art and theatre scene of the 1920s.

works.dm: kujutise kõrgus: 35.1 cm; laius: 58.0 cm; kõrgus: 50.0 cm; kujutise laius: 44.0 cm
works.d:
Nikolai Kummits (1897-1944) oli üks olulisi Pallase koolkonna kunstnikke, kes sageli kasutas monotüüpia tehnikat. Kummits eelistas vaesuse, üksinduse, vähenõudlikkuse jm, inimlikke teemasid, mida ta kujutas väga sugestiivselt. 
Eesti Kunstimuuseumi graafikakogusse kuuluvates monotüüpiates "Pliidi ees" (1938) ja "Rändaja" (1935) on näha Nikolai Kummitsale omane soe koloriit. Ka temaatiliselt on need talle tüüpilised: vana naine ja laps end soojendamas ning üksik teekäija maastikul.
works.de:
Nikolai Kummits (1897-1944) was one of the important artists of the Pallas school, who often used the monotype technique. Kummits preferred human themes such as poverty, loneliness, modesty, etc., which he depicted very suggestively.
The monotypes "Pliidi ees" [In Front of the Stove] (1938) and "Rändaja" [The Wanderer] (1935), part of the print collection of the Art Museum of Estonia, show the warm colouring characteristic of Nikolai Kummits. They are also typical of him thematically: an old woman and a child warming themselves, and a lone traveller in a landscape.

works.dm: kõrgus: 37.7 cm; laius: 51.3 cm; kujutise laius: 69.8 cm; laius: 69.8 cm
works.d:
Eduard Wiiralti 1927. aasta teos, mitmevärviline monotüüpia „Lapse sünd“ on unikaalne, mitmetähenduslik teos. Juba varasemalt on Eesti Kunstimuuseumi graafikakogus teosele loodud kavand (EKM G 13199), millelt puuduvad lehel kujutatud trepp, pilt seinal jm. 
Autor tegeles selle teemaga veel ka 1930. aastatel (joonistused G 14489, G 14491).
works.de:
Eduard Wiiralt's 1927 work, the multicoloured monotype "Lapse sünd" ["Birth of a Child"], is a unique, ambiguous work. Earlier a sketch for the work has already been created in the print collection of the Art Museum of Estonia (EKM G 13199), from which the staircase, the picture on the wall, etc. depicted in the sheet are missing.
The author also dealt with this theme in the 1930s (drawings G 14489, G 14491).

works.dm: lehe kõrgus: 49.0 cm; graafikaplaadi laius: 48.3 cm; graafikaplaadi kõrgus: 38.3 cm; lehe laius: 57.0 cm
works.d: Kaljo Põllu huvi hõimurahvaste ajaloo ja müütide vastu viis muuhulgas kunstiüliõpilastega korraldatud ekspeditsioonideni. Paralleelselt uurimistööga toimus ka materjali loominguline mõtestamine: nõnda tegeleb monumentaalne graafikasari „Kalivägi“ (1978–1984) soomeugri etnograafilise ja mütoloogilise pärandiga kunstilise tõlgendamise kujul. 65-leheliseks monumentaalseks narratiiviks välja kasvanud unikaalne sari ei ole Eesti Kunstimuuseumi kogudes esindatud täiskujul, mistõttu on oluline sellest võimalikult tervikliku komplekti koondamine.
works.de: Kaljo Põllu's interest in the history and myths of kindred peoples led, among other things, to expeditions organised with art students. Parallel to the research work, there was also a creative interpretation of the material: thus the monumental print series „Kalivägi“ (1978–1984) engages with Finno-Ugric ethnographic and mythological heritage in the form of artistic interpretation. The unique series, which grew into a 65-sheet monumental narrative, is not represented in full in the collections of the Art Museum of Estonia, which is why it is important to assemble as complete a set as possible.

works.d: Etüüdi tumedapäisest poisist tegi 19. sajandi Vene üks olulisemaid maastiku- ja portreemaalijaid Vassili Polenov ilmselt välisreisi ajal. Teos omandati Eestisse 1917.a. revolutsiooni järel ja on seega iseloomulik näide Vene kunsti jõudmisest siinsetesse kunstikogudesse.
works.de: The study of a dark-haired boy was made by Vassili Polenov, one of the most important Russian landscape and portrait painters of the 19th century, apparently during a trip abroad. The work was acquired in Estonia after the revolution of 1917 and is thus a characteristic example of the arrival of Russian art in local art collections.

works.d: Evi Tihemets on üks silmapaistvaid kujusid Eesti II maailmasõja järgses graafikas, kes pidi tõestama end tugeva vabagraafikuna 1950. aastate lõpu ja 1960. aastate alguse meestekeskses kunstimaailmas. Tihemetsa kunstnikuna kujunemise perioodist on pärit tähelepanuväärne autoportreeliste visandite kogum, mis annab tunnistuse noore naiskunstniku identiteedi otsingutest ja enesekehtestamisest, järjepidevast enesevaatlusest ja analüüsist.
works.de: Evi Tihemets is one of the outstanding figures in Estonian post-World War II printmaking, who had to prove herself as a strong independent graphic artist in the male-centred art world of the late 1950s and early 1960s. From Tihemets's period of formation as an artist comes a notable collection of self-portrait sketches, which bears witness to the young woman artist's search for identity and self-assertion, and to a persistent self-observation and analysis.

works.d: Raamatuillustraatori ja karikaturisti Elle Tikerpäe karikatuurid täiendavad hästi nimetatud valdkonna esindavat kollektsiooni Eesti Kunstimuuseumi graafikakogus. Olles mõtteliseks jätkuks Eesti Vabariigi algusaastatel kujunenud satiiriliste piltide traditsioonile (Gori, Otto Krusteni jt), lahkavad need (nt Heinz Valgu šaržide kõrval) oma ajastu ühiskonna aktuaalseid probleeme - liikudes nõukogude ja Eesti taasiseseisvumise aegse konteksti juurde, kus on eraldi koht kunstiteemalistel karikatuuridel.
works.de: The caricatures of book illustrator and caricaturist Elle Tikerpää complement well the collection representing the field in question in the graphic art collection of the Art Museum of Estonia. As a conceptual continuation of the tradition of satirical images formed in the early years of the Republic of Estonia (Gori, Otto Krusten and others), they dissect (e.g. alongside Heinz Valk's caricatures) the topical social problems of their era - moving on to the context of the Soviet period and the time of Estonia's regained independence, where a separate place is given to caricatures on art-related themes.

works.d:
Korovin, Konstantin (1861, Moskva
– 1939, Pariis). Sündis kaubandusega
tegelenud vanausuliste perekonnas.
Õppis 1875–86 Moskva maali-, skulptuuri-
ja arhitektuurikoolis Aleksei Savrassovi
ja Vassili Polenovi juures. Lõpetas
kooli diplomeeritud kunstnikuna. Oli
Mir Iskusstva ja Vene Kunstnike Ühingu
liige, esines nende näitustel. Alates 1901.
aastast õpetas maalikunsti Moskva kunstikoolis.
1905 omistas Peterburi Kunstiakadeemia
talle akadeemiku tiitli. Lisaks
maalimisele moodustas olulise osa Korovini
loometööst teatrikunst. Kujundas
mitmeid Moskva ja Peterburi teatrite
lavastusi, Sergei Djagilevi „Vene hooaegade”
etendusi Pariisis. 1900 esines edukalt
maailmanäitusel Pariisis, kus pälvis
mit
works.de:
Korovin, Konstantin (1861, Moscow
– 1939, Paris). Born into a family of Old Believers
engaged in trade.
Studied 1875–86 at the Moscow School of Painting,
Sculpture and Architecture under Aleksei Savrasov
and Vassili Polenov. Graduated
from the school as a certified artist. Was a
member of Mir Iskusstva and the Union of Russian Artists,
exhibiting at their exhibitions. From 1901
he taught painting at the Moscow Art School.
In 1905 the St. Petersburg Academy of Arts
awarded him the title of academician. Besides
painting, theatre art formed an important part of Korovin's
creative work. He designed
several productions for Moscow and St. Petersburg theatres,
and Sergei Diaghilev's "Saisons Russes"
performances in Paris. In 1900 he appeared successfully
at the world exhibition in Paris, where he was awarded
several

works.d:
Trapetsi kujulise märgi ülaosa laiem, alumine osa kitsam.
Muinasvärava motiiv, millest paistab kiirgav päike; ülaosas 2 hobupead kaelad koos, vaatavad väljapoole. Neist omakorda väljapoole jäävad ümaraotsalised väravapostid. Taust tumedaks oksüdeeritud, motiivid kõrgemad, hõbedakarva. Ühel märgil ülalt alla pikk sirge nõel, teisel ülalt alla vedrunõel.
works.de:
The upper part of the trapezoid-shaped brooch is wider, the lower part narrower.
Motif of an ancient gate, from which a radiating sun is visible; at the top 2 horse heads with necks joined, looking outward. Beyond them are round-ended gateposts. The background darkly oxidised, the motifs raised, silver-coloured. On one brooch a long straight pin runs from top to bottom, on the other a spring pin from top to bottom.

works.de: In front, a rocky shore rising from left to right with single trees and bushes. In the middle, at the edge of the shore, a sitting and a standing female figure - gazes directed down toward the harbour town and the sea. works.dm: "Sugar Free" on autori hullumajakogemusel põhinev installatsioon, milles on kesksel kohal metallvardaga ühendatud poolringis liikuv antiikne puidust kapp. Seinal on 18 fotofragmendist koosnev kujutis hoonest. Selle kõrval fotod autorist, millede all sildid "After" ja "Before". Kapi sisemuses on metalltrossidega rippuma kinnitatud tükksuhkruga täidetud metallist linnupuur, mille kohal põleb kaabli otsas rippuv elektripirn. Kapist kõlab helitaust (esimeses versioonis autor lugemas põhiseaduse paragrahve, teises versioonis katkend Gibson Brothersi palast "Paranoia").

works.d: Estonia as a country first participated in the Venice Biennale in 1997. The artists were chosen by a special committee at the Cultural Endowment of Estonia and not through an open competition as became the rule after 1999 when CCA took over. In 1997, Estonia was represented by Jaan Toomik, Raoul Kurvitz and Siim-Tanel Annus who held performances on the waterfront near San Marco. works.d: The Estonian Pavilion at the 48th Venice biennale included two art projects: one by artists Peeter Pere and Jüri Ojaver (curated by Johannes Saar ) and the other a solo project by artist Ando Keskküla. Both exhibitions were located at Palazzo Querini. Curator Johannes Saar: “Estonia is represented on the Venice Biennial by three middle aged, married man again. It might happen to be a embarrassing problem in the galaxy of Political Correctness, but people in Estonia don’t worry about that yet. On the contrary, in the bigger frame of Venice Biennial we are forgiven in advance as newcomers who may turn out to be a source of new blood. It would be extremely short-sighted to enter the Big Picture under the slogan of male art anyway. The curiosity called “man” has been reduced in contemporary art to a much more marginal appearance like that of Estonia on the edge of a unifying Europe. A locational similarity that gives us direction to carry on with the subject. We are redrawing the map of European culture in “reborn Estonia” at the moment and this kind of world conquest is traditionally blamed on men. Any kind of challenging statement is. Nevertheless, no matter how deeply a modernistic

It might happen to be a embarrassing problem in the galaxy of Political Correctness, but people in Estonia don’t worry about that yet. On the contrary, in the bigger frame of Venice Biennial we are forgiven in advance as newcomers who may turn out to be a source of new blood. It would be extremely short-sighted to enter the Big Picture under the slogan of male art anyway. The curiosity called “man” has been reduced in contemporary art to a much more marginal appearance like that of Estonia on the edge of a unifying Europe. A locational similarity that gives us direction to carry on with the subject. We are redrawing the map of European culture in “reborn Estonia” at the moment and this kind of world conquest is traditionally blamed on men. Any kind of challenging statement is. Nevertheless, no matter how deeply a modernistic

works.d: The Estonian Pavilion at the 49th Venice biennial was a collaboration between artists Ene-Liis Semper and Marko Laimre at La Fondazione Ugo e Olga Levi, Palazzo Giustinian Lolini. Ene-Liis Semper and Marko Laimre came to art more or less at the same time, somewhere in the mid-1990s. The first as a dangerous heroine of ritual performances and with body-focused videos; the other with actions laced by meta-art strategies and installations with an anarcho-political flavour. The work of both Laimre and Semper seems to indicate that a fundamental error, a complication, or at least a disharmony has been written into the elaborate mechanism of the present existence; and they are trying to capture it. Both have used their own selves and body as material, and have moulded the data of their personal histories into art. This is still very important to them. As strong personalities, the two artists have touched the borders of society’s threshold of tolerance and pain, either unwittingly or on purpose. The critics have seen them as radicals, and this is what they certainly are – both consider the rules set by society as repressive. Their artistic handwriting, however, has a fairly different colo

works.d: John Smith. Marko und Kaido. The Estonian Pavilion at the 50th Venice biennale John Smith (artist duo Kaido Ole and Marko Mäetamm) represented Estonia at the 50th Venice biennial with a show called “Marko und Kaido”, curated by Anders Härm at Palazzo Malipiero. Curator Anders Härm: “Yes, you are not mistaken – John Smith is the artist representing Estonia this year at the Venice biennial and the project is called “Marko und Kaido”. John Smith, of course, is a fictional character. He is the constantly changing Conceptual Persona of two artists, Marko Mäetamm and Kaido Ole, who have for years shared a studio. Under these circumstances – working side by side – the third guy John with a third point of view was born. We could recall here the statement of psychotherapist Felix Guattari: I and Deleuze never worked together, we were working somewhere in the space between us. Smith comes from the space between Ole and Mäetamm – he is the personified and schizo “uni-zone” as well as the working method of the artists. In contrast to, let’s say, Nietzsche´s Conceptual Persona Zarathustra, Smith is everything but the Übermensch. He is an … Idiot as if Deleuze´s and Guattari´s definition of this

works.d: The Estonian Pavilion at the 51st Venice biennial presented a solo show by Mark Raidpere “Isolator” (curated by Hanno Soans). “In my opinion such Estonian ‘men and women’ are enemies of the Estonian state and should be isolated: let them operate within closed walls.” Märt Sults. A Duty to Preserve the Country, Postimees, 28 July 2004. „The first thing the Germans did was to forbid Jews access to swimming pools; it seemed to them that if the body of an Israelite were to plunge into that confined body of water, the water would be completely befouled.“ Jean-Paul Sartre. Anti-Semite and Jew, Temps Modernes, 1946 Curator Hanno Soans: The intimate exhibition rooms in Palazzo Malipiero where the Estonian display is located act as a conceptual apartment. Mark Raidpere’s solo exhibition examining his personal identity contradictions marks the co-ordinates of privacy in social space. The viewer, who for the first time encounters the abundant grotesque of the homo-erotic motives of Raidpere’s earlier pictures of himself, is taken by surprise. Whence this pain, strained to its limits, discretely brought to attention by the cigarette-burned stigmas on the hands in the black-and-white photograph

works.d: Marko Mäetamm represented Estonia at the 52nd Venice biennial, with a project titled Loser’s Paradise (10.06 – 21.11.2007), curated by Mika Hannula . Curator Mika Hannula: “Marko Mäetamm has a confession to make. Or sorry, let me rephrase this: he has loads and loads of confessions to make. He wants to tell it all, just everything to us, and he wants us to listen to his worries and problems. Mäetamm is confused, he feels weak and almost completely inadequate when facing the demands and challenges of the contemporary world. He is afraid of failing, of losing his job, of not being able to pay his bank loan. He feels miserable without his wife and kids but feels equally unhappy when being with them. In other words, Mäetamm seems to be in a deep mess. But hold on, are these confessions as works of art true? Does he really mean it? Sure, of course they are both-and. These litanies of failures of coping with modern life are obviously and painstakingly as true as they are blue, but at the same time, they are also something else. They are, not so surprisingly, made, re-shaped and coloured by a wide variety of white lies. You know, with all the shades between pure white to grey on grey as i

works.d: Liina Siib, A Woman Takes Little Space. 2011. The Estonian Pavilion at the 54th Venice biennale. Liina Siib ’s project A Woman Takes Little Space represented Estonia at the 54th International Art Exhibition, La Biennale di Venezia (04.06.–27.11.2011). The exhibition connected room installations in an apartment-like, (un)homely environment. In her photo, video and site-specific room installations, the artist explored various topics, ranging from femininity and social space to different representations of women in contemporary society, as well as ‘feminine’ jobs and prostitution. The exhibition took place at Palazzo Malipiero. The title work of the exhibition, the photography series A Woman Takes Little Space (2007–2011), captures women of different ages and social status at their places of work. The title’s slightly awkward humour and reverse accusation highlights the exhibition’s most obvious level, one that arises from the politics of contemporary life. The series is inspired by a claim made in an opinion column on gender equality that appeared in the Estonian media a few years ago stating that women need less space for their everyday work (and less pay) than men. works.d: Dénes Farkas with his exhibition Evident in Advance represented Estonia at the 55th Venice Biennale (01.06 – 24.11.2013). The project was made in collaboration with the curator Adam Budak , the Berlin-based architectural bureau Studio Miessen and the London-based graphic designer Zak Group . Evident in Advance was a continuation of Farkas’s post-conceptual photo-based oeuvre that creates a deeply contemplative space using a minimalist approach. The exhibition curator Adam Budak called Farkas’s umwelten a cartography of failure and dysfunctionality. The exhibition raised a lot of questions about the way language flows through our fingers, the impossibility of using words for translation and the logic of endless re-translation in the seething theatre of words. One of the cornerstones of the project was Bruce Duffy’s novel The World As I Found It (1987) where fiction and reality, real and fake were mixed together and the lives of the three most important 20th century philosophers Ludwig Wittgenstein, Bertrand Russel and G. E. Moore were combined into one story of history, biography and philosophy. The exhibition was accompanied by a catalogue designed by Zak Group and published by the

works.d: The Estonian Pavilion at the 56th International Art Exhibition — La Biennale di Venezia was a new project from artist Jaanus Samma, Not Suitable For Work. A Chairman’s Tale , curated by Eugenio Viola (09.10 – 22.11.2015). The exhibition took place at Palazzo Malipiero. NSFW. A Chairman’s Tale was a fragmented fictive opera, which follows a Soviet Estonian collective farm chairman, on trial for acts of homosexuality in the 1960s. The exhibition will bring together archive materials from the Soviet Estonia and the elegant aesthetics of opera. Since 2007, Jaanus Samma has focused his artistic research on collecting the hidden histories of gay lives in Soviet Estonia. Not Suitable for Work. A Chairman’s Tale is based on rumours and the criminal file of war hero and family man kolkhoz chairman Juhan Ojaste (1921–90). Due to his involvement in homosexual acts, Ojaste was expelled from the Communist Party and later sentenced to one and a half years in a labor camp. works.t: If Only You Could See What I've Seen with Your Eyes
works.d: Pavilion of Estonia presented If Only You Could See What I’ve Seen with Your Eyes by Katja Novitskova at the Estonian Pavilion at the 57th International Art Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia (13.05 – 26.11.2017). The exhibition was curated by Kati Ilves . If Only You Could See What I’ve Seen with Your Eyes addressed the relationship between the domain of seeing, big data-driven industries, and ecology in times of biotic crisis. Currently, vast aspects of human and nonhuman lives are being registered and modeled on an environmental scale. Collection and processing of data has become a tool used to map all possible surfaces, moments and spectra on Earth and beyond – from faces to biological cell walls to dust on Mars. This is performed by human, and increasingly, robotic agents, and is directed at people, both wild and captured creatures, and nonliving processes. Seeing has become an expanding extractive industry.
